# AI NPC Cyberpunk Mod: TODO and captain's log

The single working document for development: open items first, then a dated log, then the standing facts every session needs. It replaces `HANDOFF_README.md` (removed October 5; still in git history). Earlier code and docs were written by a weaker model, so verify claims against code and data before relying on them.

## Open items

Rewritten 2026-10-23 at `main` 33750544. Every feature branch is in `main` except `skippy-stock` and `skippy-voice` (add-on API drafts), `exp/pocket-v4` (an evaluation, not used) and `perf-merges` (its two commits are on main as 78daabef, ddbf2a05). Log entries older than the top ten that say "NOT merged" or "NOT installed" predate their merges. A live check is owed unless it says it was seen.

Install state: the dev game is a player install of 0.2.9 from the release zips (Runtime and Scripts), plus overlays of the committed files of `main`. To test newer merged work overlay ALL committed `mod/`, `bridge/` and `r6/scripts/CyberpunkConvai/` files, never `mod/diagnostics.lua`. Lua needs a CET reload, `bridge/` a bridge restart, plugins and redscript a game restart.

### Ideas and features

- **Street reputation (idea of the owner, 2026-10-21, after Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2; built 2026-10-23 and merged, af64a5d3):** off by default as Settings > Conversations > Street reputation, ordinary NPCs only; design in `docs/REPUTATION_DESIGN.md`. The KCD2 model it follows: local reputation per group, witnessed crimes, talk checks, slow decay (sources: deltiasgaming.com, gamestar.de, kcd2.org, gfinityesports.com). Owed: the live checks in the Captain's log entry "Street reputation" and the FPS A/B.
- **Lucy and Rita Wheeler, the Night City Allies (NCA) followers, in the main mod** (player feature request, 2026-10-18; owner: main mod, not add-ons). In main: both profiles, Convai characters and twins, recognition by record (inert without NCA), both voices (in the bucket; the owner heard both in the game 2026-10-23), connect and seat fixes; talk checked live 2026-10-19. Left: the 2026-10-19 connect and seat re-checks (`docs/NCA_FOLLOWERS_PLAN.md`) if not yet seen. The request, verbatim:
  > Omg this is insane I already love it so much!!! I know this mod has just been released but would it be possible in the future to have addons for mods like NCA Rita Wheeler or Lucy? I'm using them as followers with Night City Allies but it would be so damn amazing to have actual conversations when we do a side mission or just riding along the car together.

A 30-minute test on the laptop's Intel iGPU and CPU with the existing references and the 16/32-step comparison settles it; needs a download approval (`omnivoice-q8_0.gguf`, 1.35 GB) and a licence check of the audio.cpp code before any integration.

The topic alias for `db.queen-friendship-hook` is done and 4 of the 21 rows promoted. ### Settled and dropped

- **The OmniPack keeps its DLLs (owner, 2026-10-23):** they are the engine (94 files, 4.6 GB, CUDA torch), so Vortex cannot install it and Vortex players extract it by hand (the Nexus OmniVoice line and the "Voice models" requirement say so). Idea for later if Vortex players keep asking: renamed `.dll_` files that the mod renames back at first start, which needs an MO2 check.
- **Release signing: not now (owner, 2026-10-23):** a check inside our own Runtime can be stripped from a tampered copy, `runtime-code-files.json` already catches corrupted installs, and Windows code signing only matters for a standalone .exe players run.
- **Companions can see: kept (owner, 2026-10-23, live-checked in the 0.2.9 test):** the capture helper ships in the Runtime (Desktop Duplication, no yellow border while the game is in front); the setting stays removed.
- **Johnny's glitching hologram and V talks on their own: removed completely** (owner decision D2, 2026-10-20, 662b49be; log "owner settings decisions"). "Johnny in your head" and "Johnny speaks up" stay as one list row.
- **The double-click support report (`Make support report.bat`) and the offline report: dropped** (ffd83b26, chore/drop-support-bat, 0.2.3); players use Generate report in Settings or a screenshot.
- **A CUDA llama-server build for NVIDIA: tested, not used** (e815b6ab, `deliverables/cuda-vs-vulkan-2026-10-20.md`: not faster in the open world; the slow reports were spill into shared memory).
- **Mature content on Mistral: dropped** (owner, 2026-10-20, cd50ec1f): Local AI and Custom only, never Mistral, Voxtral or Convai; it changes no voice. Cloud users' request: see Needs the owner.
- **Pocket TTS 4.0.0: not upgrading** (2026-10-21, `exp/pocket-v4`, `docs/POCKET_V4_EVAL_2026-10-21.md` on that branch): the shipped 3.3.0 student clones best; the small v4 models are only a low-end idea.
- **Gradium Phonon instead of Pocket TTS (owner, 2026-10-21): no.** Faster (~11x real time on one core, ~14 ms first audio) and rated above Pocket in Gradium's tests, but the open weights have no local voice cloning (voices come from Gradium's cloud studio from consented recordings), and the 40m/multilingual models are CC BY-NC. Pocket clones every character from its game clip on the player's PC, so Phonon does not fit.

Cause found by reading the code, not seen in the game: `reason=scene` is `M.blocked(sample)` (`tier ~= 1`, a dialogue or a choice hub), the sample is taken every half second of play time, and a call is asked for from the open phone, which slows the game and holds the scene tier above gameplay's; `worldReady` does not exclude the phone. The request was judged at once on that reading. The no-journal path adds no check that reads a contact, a phone-system call or a nil. Fix: a request whose reading says `scene` is held up to 4 s of play for a fresh reading (`M.SCENE_WAIT`), starts when gameplay is read, and is refused (with its notice) only when the scene is still there; combat and a game call refuse on the spot. The refusal line now carries the reading. Notices: every refusal in `holocall.lua` already had a text; the one silent path (the Chat tab's request for a contact the tab does not know) now shows the game's blocked notice. Tests: 4 new/changed in `bridge/holocall.test.mjs`. **Probe lines for the retest (CET log, `[Holocall]`), same call from the Chat list:** `requested contact=<key>`, then EITHER `held contact=<key> reason=scene tier=<n> dialogue=.. choices=.. (waiting for a fresh reading, up to 4s)` followed by `released contact=<key> after <s>s: gameplay again`, `no-journal call ... begin=ok`, `state=dialing`, `state=connected` (the fix did it; the held line's tier shows what the phone's reading was), OR `held ...` and then `refused contact=<key> reason=scene tier=<n> dialogue=<b> choices=<b> call=<b> replacer=<b> waited=4.xs` (the scene reading is real or stuck: read tier, dialogue and choices there to see which flag it is, and tell me), OR a different `refused` reason. Also check that the refusal notice is visible when it happens.

**2026-10-27 (branch `fix/vixen-read` from integration/0.3.3 5cb4c26f; offline tests only, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; CET reload + bridge restart):** first live test of the Flesh and Chrome / Injuries reader (probe.log 06:56 to 07:07Z, game 2.31): breath stayed at stage 4 for ten minutes, injuries read all zeros, drinks and smoke read `?`, and the bridge tagged the fac:/inj: lines `[DarkFuture]`. **Read against the mods' redscript (extracted under deliverables/reference):** every class, getter, argument and meaning in `mod/vixen-state.lua` matches (`FACSystem.GetStaminaPercent/GetEnergyPercent(player)` FleshAndChrome.reds 1784/1792, `InjuriesSystem.IsLive/GetAppliedTier(kind)/GetSeverity(region)` Injuries_System.reds 175/328/442), and no `failed` line was logged, so the calls work in CET. (a) **Breath**: `GetStaminaPercent` is the mod's own pool, so stage 4 means the mod held V at zero. Its tick refills the pool only with no jog-or-faster movement, after `regenDelayCooldownMinutes` (10 game min) times how empty it was (FleshAndChrome.reds 500/518/584), never above the energy pool (586); at the game's ~8x clock that is ~75 real seconds, so ten minutes is odd, but nothing in the reader is stale (the stage line changed at 07:06:35Z, the 5 second snapshot is not stuck). Not settled from the source: the new `Mod state probe: breath ...` line (first read, each stage change, every 120 s at stage 3 or 4) records the raw pool, energy, Exhausted status, IsStaminaRegenning, the game's own stamina pool, the mod's cooldown left and the game-clock pace. (b) **Injuries**: signatures match; Injuries only injures after 50 percent of health in 10 s then a 75 percent roll, or one 80 percent hit (Injuries_HitProbe.reds, Injuries_Config.reds), so zeros after a fall or a few shots were probably true. Added: all six `GetSeverity` and the four applied tiers in a probe line, and a second opinion (12 `HasStatusEffect` calls for `Injuries.<Kind>_T<tier>`, at most once a minute, only while the system says none; one in force is believed over the zeros and logged). (c) **Drinks/smoke `?`**: the mod has no status effect for alcohol or cigarettes (only `FACStatusEffect.Exhausted`), so the persistent `PlayerPuppetPS` fields were the only route and they did not read (`player:GetPS()` or the field access gave nothing in CET). The fields are now read directly, then through Codeware's `Reflection.GetClass('PlayerPuppetPS'):GetProperty(...)` (the combat-feats-probe pattern), each field's raw value and path logged once (`Mod state probe: PlayerPuppetPS fields ...`, `player:GetPS() failed|gave nothing`); and the public `FACSystem:GetTotalAlcohol(player)` / `GetTotalCigarettes(player)` (same call shape as the working getters) are watched from read to read: a rise is a drink (6 h window + 1 h per extra, from `GetConfig()`) or a cigarette (30 game min) counted on the game clock; a drink had before the session's first read is not seen. (d) **Bridge log tags**: `[DarkFuture] df:`, `[FleshAndChrome] fac:`, `[Injuries] inj:` (`bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` `DF_LOG_TAGS`). Wording unchanged (plain facts, no restrictions). No timers, hooks or per-frame work; reads stay on demand inside the turn snapshot (about 20 getter calls per 5 s snapshot). **Tests:** `bridge/vixen-state-lua.test.mjs` 27 (was 19; counts fallback, reflection path, GetPS failure, breath probe cadence, injuries second opinion and probe line, passive scan), mod-state/vixen-state/mod-state-lua 88 together, all green; full `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`: 10206 pass, 3 fail that are not this work (`an unreadable settings file is an unknown state` known; `Prompting: the options with their badges...` and `Johnny's follow-on, prepared while the line plays` time out under load and pass alone). **Next live test (game 2.31, owner):** (1) with Other mods' state on, sprint until out of breath, talk to a character, wait two minutes, talk again: read the `Mod state probe: breath` lines in probe.log. **2026-10-27 (branch `fix/crowd-history` from integration/0.3.3 5cb4c26f; offline tests only, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched): "the conversation history of the two female pedestrians is shared" (live test 27 Oct, game 2.31, Local AI text + Pocket voice; actors 10009597ULL at 06:56Z and 11146316ULL at 06:58Z, both `resident-female`).** Traced every per-profile store of the turn path. The conversation history itself was NOT keyed by profile: the text providers recall and record under the ambient key (`route.sessionKey`, a hash that holds the actor's entity: `bridge/conversation-knowledge.mjs` `#configuration`; `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` `localTurn`; `bridge/memory-store.mjs` and `bridge/mistral-memory.mjs` `ambient` map, capped at 48 strangers, least recently used first), the Convai session and its connection page are keyed by the same hash (`realtimeSessions`, `bridge/transport-pool.mjs` `transportKey` with the anonymous scope), and the "already told" flags (`bridge/scenery-memory.mjs`, follow-up, Natural speech) use the session key or the entity. A new test holds this with two entities on one profile on both stores, the knowledge route and the text host. Two states WERE still shared by profile and are fixed: (1) the carried mood (`EmotionSelection.recent` in `bridge/emotion-selector.mjs`, three minutes, keyed by `input.profileKey`): one stranger's mood opened the next stranger's face and voice emotion; now keyed by `personKey(input)` (`bridge/protocol.mjs`: profile for a named character, `<profile>|<entity>` for a generic one); (2) the in-game lines a stranger heard (`bridge/game-dialogue.mjs`): only `resident-*` was treated as generic, so every `npc-*` archetype body of one kind saw what another body of that kind had said in the game (matched by profile); now any `resident-*` or `npc-*` profile is matched by its entity alone (the decision ledger keeps its old rule so an older file still parses). New log line per ordinary-person turn on the text providers: `[TextProvider] Crowd person: profile=resident-female entity=11146316ULL key=ab12cd34 earlier-turns=N`; the second stranger must show `earlier-turns=0` and a different `key`. HONEST LIMIT: the bridge log alone cannot show the model's prompt, and the second woman's reply opened with "Like I said" after a first woman who also offered coffee; with the history keys proven per person, that is most likely the model repeating itself on the same persona and the same typed line, but only the new log line in a repeat of the live test can tell (talk to two women, check `earlier-turns=0` on the second). Tests: `bridge/crowd-person-history.test.mjs` (new, 8), `bridge/text-provider-host.test.mjs` (+1). Docs: `docs/NPC_ARCHETYPES.md` ("Identity and memory").

The switch-off leave uses the same run. New owner rule built: a brawl's friends (one targeting search at 1.2 s: in combat and hostile to V within 20 m, up to 4, ordinary by the same rails) get fists and a drawn gun put away; V's right hand is read once a second while the brawl lasts (max 120 s): V holding a gun makes every brawler draw its weapon (`AISwitchToPrimaryWeaponCommand`), once, never back to fists. **2026-10-27 (branch `fix/amd-rocm-speed` from integration/0.3.3; unit-tested only, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; bridge restart only): the OmniVoice AMD route is tuned from the first AMD player's findings (NTFSynergy, RX 9070 XT 16 GB, reported 27 Oct: works; stock 10 to 15 s per sentence, sometimes drops mid-sentence, MIOpen "not able to find convolution paths"; `MIOPEN_FIND_MODE=FAST` or `torch.backends.cudnn.enabled = False` (set by hand in their loader) was snappier, under 10 s; quality presets barely changed speed; the game dropped frames while generating).** All player data as reported, not measured here. Changes, ROCm only (`torch.version.hip` set; an NVIDIA/CUDA build or the Runtime's Python gets nothing new): (1) the worker (`tune_rocm`, after the CUDA gate, before any model loads) sets `MIOPEN_FIND_MODE=FAST` unless already set and turns `torch.backends.cudnn.enabled` off, re-asserted after `_ensure_loaded()`, one `[rocm]` log line; the bridge also puts `MIOPEN_FIND_MODE=FAST` in the worker's environment for a ROCm own-Python (before torch loads) unless the player set it or `omni-python.txt` names another mode. Overrides: lines after the python.exe line in `omni-python.txt` (`miopen-find-mode = X`, `miopen = on`, `priority = normal`), the player's own `MIOPEN_FIND_MODE`, and `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_ROCM_MIOPEN=1`. (2) Mid-sentence drops: `omni-pcm.mjs` ended a reply at the first LATER phrase whose render failed (and wrote the reply as text when the first failed); the worker answers a PyTorch error with an error frame and keeps running, so the AMD route now asks once more for a failed phrase (`retries`, capped 2, default 0, never on a cancel). VRAM: the AMD route already uses PyTorch's card memory (`vramMiB`) for the small-card rules and the worker's render limit is 120 s, so nothing there explains a drop on 16 GB (not confirmed live). (3) Frame drops: the normal OmniVoice start never lowered priority and a background start went back to normal once ready, with no CPU-thread cap on NVIDIA either; on the AMD route the worker is now below normal from its start for good (`keepLowPriority` in `ResidentVoice` plus the worker lowering itself, because a venv's python.exe is a launcher process). NVIDIA behaviour left as it was: the owner may want the same below-normal rule there (latency tradeoff, no measurement). Tests: `node --test` omni-own-python, omni-pcm, resident-voice, voice-selection (152 pass); `python -B scripts/test_resident_voice_paths.py` (87 OK). Docs: `docs/OMNIVOICE_AMD.md` (settings table, overrides, reported numbers, developer notes). Live check owed from an AMD player: sentence time, no cut-off replies, fewer frame drops, and the `[rocm]` / `[priority]` lines in the report. Tell NTFSynergy once it ships.

Without look-ahead (a player's own free Convai key) the line is asked for at the end of the line before with no pause of ours. Endings: the last two lines said "see-you-later" and "winding the exchange down"; they now let the topic rest and say nobody is leaving. Tests: `housemate-chat-prepare`, `housemate-chat-game`, `house-chat-lookahead`, `house-chat`. **2026-10-26 (branch `fix/perf-audit-2` from main 8006a09d; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched): performance audit of 0.3.2 (owner: "check performance, anything that could affect performance negatively").** Evidence: the Developer-mode capture `runtime/perf-probe.json` of the 26 Oct test (150 two-second windows, 06:35-06:40Z, Housemates On with four residents in the Corpo Plaza flat, reactions on) and `probe.log`. The mod's Lua costs about 30 ms/s in quiet frames with the probe on (`event:onUpdate`; the 23.7 ms/s of the 22 Oct review), 40 ms/s while a line is spoken; the largest tick rows are `init:gaze` 3.4, `init:session` 4 to 6.7, `init:knowledge` 3.3, `init:tick` 2.8 (unchanged code; the clock has 1 ms resolution, so a row under 1 ms/s is noise). Real timings: a `io.open` is 0.045 ms (0.41 ms/s for about 9 opens/s), so file polls are not the cost, native-call loops and spatial queries are. Six windows had a frame over 70 ms (759, 280, 268, 187, 120, 99 ms) and no mod section over 11 ms in any of them: the stalls are outside the measured Lua (three sit in windows of a spoken housemate chat line, two do not; the bridge's voice and model work beside the game, or the engine itself, are the candidates); only an FPS A/B tells. Turn latency (`bridge-latency.json`, 24 turns): input written to the model request 20 to 50 ms, first sentence 2.7 to 4.4 s (provider), first sound 3.2 to 5.2 s, the 150 ms Bluetooth audio delay is deliberate. Fixed (each with a test that fails without it): (1) `mod/housemates.lua`: a body that never came (`failed:spawn-timeout key=blue-moon`, 17 times in one session, a `proc:` standing place has no id to give up) was spawned and deleted every 75 s; each timeout in a row now doubles the pause (30 to 600 s), V entering the flat again starts afresh, and the step while only a body is being made is 0.5 s, not 0.25 s. (2) `mod/housemate-world.lua`: the 25 m twin scan is one query for every resident asked in the same second, each part read once. (3) `mod/housemate-service.lua`: a pair-chat file that fails to load was read and compiled on every 0.1 s tick; one try per switching On. (4) `mod/manager-party.lua` flush (four times a second): `companions.list()` (about seventy fields per copy) is built only when a copy is attaching or leaving; it was built twice every time. (5) `mod/loot-observer.lua`: with Loot reactions on (the default now) each of the hundreds of item events of a crafting, disassembly or vendor burst asked V's puppet seven native questions; the answer is kept for the frame (`convaiHeartbeat.frame`). (6) `mod/media-context.lua`: the TV targeting query (up to 400 parts, about ten native calls each) ran on every turn on foot; an empty answer now rests 20 s while V stays within 3 m. (7) `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs`: the 60 ms look-ahead poll read `group-prefetch.json` 17 times a second for text providers too (0.3.2 allows follow-on and scene lines there); one stat now, the read only when the file changed. Left, with the reason: `ReactionManagerComponent` overrides stay installed for the session once any companion is focused (a gaze, a talk): 15 to 40 us a stimulus, 0.3 to 12 ms/s in a crowd, and an owner decision (install them only for an ordinary NPC; her vanilla reactions would then be left alone while V talks to an own companion); the held-weapon inventory read (up to about 2 ms per companion on the send frame, tests pin the 5 s cache); the per-turn gear and turn-context reads (5 to 15 ms once per sent line); the call-off file poll (1 s while a meeting stands, about 0.1 ms/s; the plugin does not route that file); Housemates On steps (about 1 ms/s with four residents: `hours()` and the facts asked several times a step); Immersive `offer()` on a typed phone message with Immersive On (waypoint landmark scan, `trafficLanes`); seat-preparation rays are charged 4 for 4 cells but fire 2 to 3 each. LIVE CHECKS OWED (CET reload, bridge restart; never `mod/diagnostics.lua`): (a) a Developer-mode capture of 5 minutes in a crowd with and without a companion in the party: `hook:ReactionManagerComponent.*` rows, `event:onUpdate`, the worst windows; (b) Housemates On with a character whose body cannot be made: probe.log shows `failed:spawn-timeout` at growing gaps (about 76, 182, 348, 635 s), then every 10 minutes, and a new try when V leaves and re-enters; (c) disassemble or sell 50 junk items and look at the frame time and `hook:PlayerPuppet.OnItem*` rows; a world pickup with Loot reactions on still gets its remark; (d) a turn on foot in a busy street: `Media:` line unchanged, no repeat of `tv=none(query found N TVs)` within 20 s; stand near a TV that is switched on: it is found at once; (e) a text provider with Johnny speaks up or a companion speaking up after a scene: the prepared line is still held and said.

**2026-10-26 (branch `fix/convai-noaudio`; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched): a Convai response that ended with no audio no longer makes the next response get refused (error signatures `2da75bbf`, `b74022f5`, `6a584052`, 4 installs on 0.2.5 to 0.3.1, microphone turns on Convai voice).** Cause: one collector per turn holds ONE active owner (`convai-data-audio.mjs` `_owner`); a response whose first owned message was only an uninterrupted `bot-turn-completed` (0 audio packets, no statistics, its end) stayed the active owner for good, so the second response of the same turn (another `response_id`, with faces and the speech) hit the owner-change check and failed the turn. Fix, exact-owner rule kept: when another owner arrives and the active response has ended cleanly with no audio and no statistics (audio that came after its end does not count), that response is closed (`closeEmptyResponse`: owner kept in `closedOwners`, its end and faces dropped) and the new owner is judged like the first of a turn (not retired, not closed). Late messages of a closed owner are ignored, and `realtime-client.mjs` retires closed owners with the turn's own, so no later turn adopts them. Still fatal: an owner change before the active response ended, after it had audio or statistics, a fourth empty response, interruption, cancel. An empty response alone never completes a turn (60 s timeout as before). Tests: 7 in `convai-data-audio.test.mjs`, 4 turn-level in `realtime-client.test.mjs`. Live Convai run still owed (what the empty response is on the wire, and that the second response's speech plays). `docs/CONVAI_AUDIO_STREAMING.md` updated.

Only a passing Python runs the worker, which loads OmniVoice's code from the pack (a meta-path finder, so the packaged-source check still holds), with the CUDA graph off by default on HIP. A refusal keeps the Runtime's Python (fallback as today: Pocket or text, never cloud). Help > Setup check has an "OmniVoice Python" row (backend or the refusal reason, 13 new strings in 15 locales), probe.log gets one line per changed answer, the report carries `omniPython`. Docs: `docs/OMNIVOICE_AMD.md` (player steps, AMD's exact install commands, the pinned library list for `pip install --no-deps`), one line each in README and PLAYER_README (link to the GitHub doc, live only once merged and pushed). **2026-10-25 (branch `fix/tv-voice`, from integration/next; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed): the companions never noticed a TV, and why a Voxtral voice sounds different between turns.** (A) Live apartment test, probe.log 09:49:10Z: `Media: ... tv=none(query found 0 TVs)` with Judy and Alex beside V and a TV on (at 09:53:35Z a TV line was heard, `tv=heard`). Cause in `mod/media-context.lua` `tvQuery`: it looked at the first 40 target parts only, in no order, and a companion's body brings many parts (the door search of `mod/companion-passage.lua` has no such limit and finds doors), and it did not ask for secondary targets. Now up to 400 parts and secondary targets, a TV is class `TV` or any entity whose device controller is a `TVControllerPS`, and a line with no TV ends with `why: parts=N objects=N seen=<top classes>`, `beyondRadius=`, `notOn=`, `lookedAtTvNotOn`. Still only the game can say whether a TV is returned as a target part at all; if `why:` shows the room's devices but no TV, the TV has none. (B) Voice: no clip is chosen per turn. The routing log has `profile=alex ref="picked/autobest/omni-long 11.62s"` on all 9 of Alex's Voxtral replies, plain and Medieval alike (voice paths use the base `profileKey`; `providerProfileKey`/the memory key are Convai/memory only), and the installed clip matches its hash. Nothing about the references changed since 2026-10-21 (ordinary NPCs cut to one clip, Voxtral 3 asked for by name, first ask hedged on 10-22). What varies is Voxtral itself: it clones afresh per request (spread 0.50 to 0.65 similarity for one clip) from a two-line reference (Alex 11.6 s, cut to 8.5 s) and a long reply is two requests. **2026-10-25 (Model browser search; branch `feat/model-browser-search` from main 452b9e74, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; unit-tested only):** owner asked to search the Model browser (type "rita wheeler", invite her). Route: MCM's own "Search settings" box with the provider search mode. MCM's box normally filters the rows of the page by label and description, which on the browser sees only the twelve rows of the page; `api.ui.setNavigation(..., {searchMode = 'provider'})` (set on the models page only) makes MCM leave the filtering to the host, and `api.ui.getContext().search` carries the box's text (MCM settles it 12 frames after a key). `mod/mcm-host.lua` reads it on the existing 0.25 s tick (`followSearch`, no new timer, no per-frame work) and hands it to `mod/manager-ui.lua` `M.setSearch`, which keeps the lower-cased words; the page is built again only when the words changed. A model matches when every word is in its name, record or conversation profile (`model.search` from the scan): "rita", "wheeler rita", "RITA  wheel" find Rita Wheeler; the filter runs over the list the scan already sorted, once per text, with no rescan. Results page like any list with their normal Invite buttons; the letter group is hidden while a text is searched; the text is part of `M.pageId()`. The box is emptied (`api.ui.setSearch`) on the way into and out of the browser because MCM keeps its text across pages and filters Home and Settings by it. An MCM that refuses the option gets the page without it (one log line, no hint). One new string ("Type in the search box ...", the model-status help, MCM only) in the 15 locale files plus en.json. **Native Settings UI cannot do this**: it has no text field (switch, list, slider, button only), so its browser keeps Starts with and the page slider; a typed search there would need the game's own text box (the F6 composer) and redscript, not done. Tests: `bridge/mcm-host.test.mjs` +4 (words in any order, partial words, case and spacing, record match, 0 results, Invite from a result, box emptied in and out, no reload without a change, no rescan, an MCM that refuses the mode), `bridge/manager.test.mjs` +2 (filter words, held search, hint only when a host offers a search), `bridge/mcm-fake.mjs` follows the search box (context.search, setSearch, filter and provider modes). Docs: `docs/MANAGER_UI.md` ("Searching the Model browser"). **Live check owed (MCM 0.10.6-hf1 or 0.10.5):** (1) Model browser: type "rita wheeler" in the Search settings box: does the list become her within about half a second, with the box keeping focus so you can keep typing; (2) type only "rita": more than one result? (3) press Invite on a result: does she join; (4) clear the box: back to the full list and Starts with; (5) type, then Back to Companion Manager: is the box empty and Home complete; (6) 0.10.5 if available: does it accept the provider search mode (else the page quietly keeps MCM's own filter).

**2026-10-24 (local server never started to read a level, branch `fix/convai-no-local-start` from main, NOT merged, NOT pushed; game not touched; bridge restart):** error reports 4cf959 (0.3.0) and 52c992 (0.2.9) showed `choices.provider = convai`, Mature off, yet `local-unavailable (low-ram)` from `LocalLlmServer.ensure` via `#matureLevel`. Cause: the reports' `choices` are read when the report is SENT; the log of 52c992 shows the turn ran while the player was on Local AI with Mature on (an 8 GB card, 16 GB RAM, no room for the uncensored model), then they switched to Convai and Mature off. So no Convai turn started Local AI: `attachTextProvider` keeps every Convai turn, warm-up and voice off the text host, and `applyProviderChoice` stops the model for any other provider. The real fault was smaller: `#matureLevel` (and `#guardOn`, `#profileFor`) called `route.loadedModel`/`loadedTier`, which is `server.ensure()`, so reading a level started a server that had just failed (a second failing start in the same turn). Fixed: new `LocalLlmServer.plannedModel()` (the model a start would load, from the selection and the last start's card numbers, or the loaded one; spawns nothing) and `localRoute.plannedModel`; the three readers use it; `loadedModel`/`loadedTier` are gone. Where Local AI can still be reached by a Convai player on purpose: add-on speakers (Skippy remarks, Delamain) fall back to the local AI when no Mistral key is saved and the pack is installed (`AddonHost.routeFor`, documented in docs/ADDON_API.md); that is the add-on's own explicit feature and its turn starts the model itself. Tests: a Convai-provider turn, warm-up and direct text-host call never call `ensure`/`prewarm`/`status`; the Mature level of a Local turn with no model up never calls `ensure` from the level, guard or profile readers and uses the planned model; `plannedModel` follows the choice, Mature, a loaded model and a stop. Files for the install (bridge): `local-llm-server.mjs`, `text-provider-host.mjs`.

**2026-10-24 (V speaks your microphone lines, branch `feat/v-voice-mic` from main 6cafd2d0, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; Lua needs a CET reload, bridge a restart):** a player asked for V to speak what they say over the microphone, not only what they type. New setting **V speaks your microphone lines** (`vVoiceMic`, Settings > Voices, right under V's voice, **off by default**, meaningful only while V's voice is on). (1) **Why push-to-talk never replayed V:** the first version (29234fb4) only says "you already spoke it": a typed line is silent so V's voice is the only way it is heard, a spoken line was just heard in the player's own voice and its words already show as V's live subtitle. The default stays off and the setting's description gives that reason. (2) **Design:** after a voice turn the final transcript is spoken by the same V voice path (engine, gender, volume, reference, language rules, group and phone gates). On Mistral, Local AI and Custom the transcript exists before the reply is asked for (`options.onTranscript`), so `bridge/mic-v-line.mjs` starts V's line there, beside the reply's text request. (3) **Ordering against the reply:** a typed line is waited for (the reply's audio is held until V ends, 30 s at most without audio). That rule would delay the reply for an echo, so a spoken line is **soft** (`VLine` `soft`): it never holds the reply. When the reply asks (its audio is ready, or its voice request goes out on the Pocket worker V shares) V is cut short if audible (`cut-for-reply`) or dropped if not (`reply-ready`). Not with OmniVoice (its render sits in front of the companion's on the one GPU worker, skipped as `mic-omni`) and not with the Convai provider (its transcript arrives with the reply, skipped with one log line). Empty recording, cancelled or superseded turn: no line. (4) **A leak closed:** a spoken line to an add-on's voice (Delamain, Skippy) or a made character carried no source mark, so V already spoke it and the reply waited for it; those turns now follow the new setting (off). (5) Strings in all 15 locales (Haiku translated 2 strings), `localization/en.json` regenerated, `docs/V_VOICE.md` section "Microphone lines", README rows. **2026-10-24 (a spilled model nobody can replace stays loaded, branch `fix/spill-keep-running` from main b2022e2f, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed; bridge restart only):** error-report triage fix candidate 2 (signatures 014a3be6 / 316c6d2b: 4 installs, 12 GB cards included, "the local model server did not start (low-ram)"). Cause: `#spillAct` unloaded a spilled model that still answered BEFORE it checked that anything could replace it; the checks came after the stop, found nothing (377 to 2,544 MiB free, no smaller model, the CPU part needed 6,723 MiB of system memory against 870 to 5,793 free) and Local AI was gone for the session. Fix (`bridge/local-llm-server.mjs`): `#spillReplacement` judges first, with the model still up and no step gate held (a turn is not made to wait for a look): the free memory plus the model's own dedicated memory, then refit whole (once) / next smaller model whole / same model with part on the CPU only if at least 35% of the layers stay on the card, the system memory is free and reloads are left. A replacement is stopped-and-loaded as before; with none the model stays (log "nothing can replace it" once per load, recheck no sooner than 10 minutes, the refit is not used up, no notice because 'local-cpu' says "processor"). The LOW_RAM gate is unchanged on purpose: free RAM is Windows "available" memory (already counts the file cache) and every refused machine was 930 to 5,800 MiB short of the real need, so relaxing it would only start models that crawl; the fix is not unloading the model that answered. Tests: `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs` (keep with no replacement, keep for lack of RAM, smaller model that does not fit vs one that does, fitted-once-then-spilled stays, switch cases, gate thresholds 6,722 refused / 6,723 starts, a turn during the look is not held; the old tests that expected "low-memory" or a hopeless offload after a spill now expect the model to stay). **Live check (needs a card the game over-commits, e.g. 8 GB or 12 GB with OmniVoice and only the Mature good model installed):** play until a reply is slow; the bridge log should say "has N MiB in shared system memory ... nothing can replace it ... it stays loaded" and replies keep coming (slowly), with no "unavailable (start-failed: low-ram)" line; close other programs or free the card and the next look (10 minutes later, after a slow reply) should refit it whole. Copy `bridge/local-llm-server.mjs` into the install.

Everything said before the device opened was lost. **Now (docs/VOICE_INPUT.md):** (1) Key down writes `runtime/microphone-live.json` (new, `mod/microphone.lua` `holdKey`) right after the target is found; the bridge (`bridge/mic-live.mjs`) opens the **microphone tap** (`bridge/mic-tap.mjs`, 40 ms chunks) at once and keeps every chunk (pre-roll). The `start` command that follows adopts the tap by the key's hold id. Local recogniser, Mistral transcription and multilingual packs take the kept audio through `TapCapture` under the unchanged `createLocalSttChannel`; Convai takes it through a relay (`RealtimeHost.startRelayPump` -> `window.convaiRealtime.pushAudio` -> `bridge/pcm-relay.mjs` -> a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` the SDK publishes; only from 250 ms before the first speech frame; the page falls back to the SDK microphone if the relay cannot open, `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_MIC_RELAY=0` switches it off). The request id now rides beside the voice config (`MicrophoneSession.start` -> `beginVoice(config, {requestId})`), never inside it. (2) Key up writes `down:false` (the tap stops on the spot) and `finish` in ANY recording state; a hold under 0.2 s is dropped silently. The 700 ms minimum recording is gone (`minRecordMs: 0`). Tap mode no longer exists (it was never a setting). (3) No notice for a normal turn: removed "Connecting microphone", "Listening - press {key} again to finish", "Use {key} to finish this recording", the voice key's "Preparing connection"; kept once each: language note, no speech ("Hold the talk key while you speak"), microphone sends no sound, unavailable, no Convai connection. The live words are the existing path (subtitle line, else the `mic-heard` notice). (4) **Voice activation** (Settings > Voices, `voiceActivation`, off by default; MCM and Native Settings UI; 15 locales): `mod/voice-activation.lua` (loaded only when on) opens the tap for listening only while a profiled character is faced or a companion is within 8 m, no scene tier 3+, dialogue, choice list or call, no menu or text box, no turn in flight, and no AI line playing or ended less than 0.9 s ago (the microphone is closed, not filtered, while a voice plays). The detector is `bridge/voice-activity.mjs` in the bridge (30 ms frames, gate max(-50 dBFS, floor + 12 dB), pitch-correlation "voiced" test, start 8 voiced of 12 frames, 300 ms hangover, **end after 900 ms of quiet**, 300 ms pre-roll): Lua reads one field of `microphone-state.json` (`vad`) at 4 Hz while listening, begins the turn like the key (notices muted) and finishes it on the detector's end (fresh game context). Off: device closed, detector and pre-roll dropped, module not loaded, one boolean per tick. **Cost:** nothing per frame; two small file writes at the key edges; the detector 60 s of audio in 25 ms. **Measured** (`node scripts/Measure-VoiceKey.mjs`, real tap and channel, simulated time, first word 250 ms after the press, 1.5 s of speech, device 150 ms to open): speech lost at the start before/after 231/0 ms (prep 300 ms), 730/0 (800 ms), 1,414/0 (1,500 ms); release to the recogniser having everything 0 ms both, but 507 ms after at a 1,500 ms preparation before (the old minimum-recording wait). Real Edge with the fake device (`bridge/mic-tap-browser.test.mjs`): signal to open device 54 ms on a warm capture page, about 490 ms when the page must be created, so the page is opened ahead when the hidden browser starts and stays 10 min. **Not measurable offline:** the owner's first-word-to-reply on the real game (the stage clock starts at the request, not at the key); read `[CyberpunkConvai] Microphone: microphone tap open ... in N ms` and the `microphone.start` stage in `bridge-latency.json`. **Tests:** new `mic-tap`, `mic-live`, `mic-wiring`, `mic-tap-browser`, `voice-activity`, `voice-activation`, `pcm-relay`; changed `microphone-adapter`, `knowledge-integration`, `localized-feedback`, `notices`, `world-lifecycle`, `manager`, `realtime-client`, `transport-pool`, `ui-catalog`, `provider-switch-race`, settings fixtures; `localization/en.json` regenerated. Cause: after the 400 the request went on with `effort: low` but the unchanged 300-token reply budget, which the model's 100 to 1500 thinking tokens (it ignores `effort` and `reasoning.max_tokens`) used up, so the turn paid for an empty reply and a second full request (5 of 6 turns in the measurement). API on `PromptProfiles`: `list`, `getDefault`, `getEffective`, `getOverride`, `validate`, `set`, `reset`, `preview`, `resolve`. Gains are modest and mostly inside judge noise; the Mature models never lectured. - **Forget label.** The row's name was "Forget all memories" and its button text "Forget (6 characters)" (the count lived in the button). Now the name carries the count, "Forget all memories (6 characters)", and the button is "Forget". The name is held to the button-row budget (`BUTTON_LABEL_UNITS` 29 in `mod/manager-ui.lua`, the figure `mod/nsui.lua` already cut to; the English with two digits is 29.9 units, so 10 or more characters read "Forget all memories (12)", and a translation that does not fit falls back to the same, then to the name alone). `nsui-labels.test.mjs` now publishes a count of 6 and checks the row in all 16 languages. Mod Configuration Menu draws the same row (name and button text), nothing else to change there.
- **Dynamic info page** (`docs/DYNAMIC_INFO.md`). A button under Memory and Relationships opens nine switches, all on, saved as `dynamicInfo.<kind>` in `runtime/settings.json` (applied through `manager.applySettings` like Relationships, in the support report's settings section with a `dynamicInfoOff` list, part of Restore defaults on both hosts): **Location**, **Time and weather**, **Company and vehicle**, **Health, heat and fights**, **V's money**, **V's gear and clothes**, **V's gender and lifepath**, **Quest and journal**, **Recent game dialogue**. **2026-10-22 (game-side performance pass from `deliverables/review-performance-2026-10-22.md`; branch `perf/game-side-1022` from main b21f2d81, worktree `.claude/worktrees/perf-game-side-1022`, 7 code commits, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `mod/` Lua, one redscript method in `r6/scripts/CyberpunkConvai/Composer.reds` (needs a game restart), tests in `bridge/`; every touched Lua file compiles and passes `scripts/lua-upvalues.mjs`, the redscript passed `scripts/Compile-Redscript.ps1` (scc exit 0)).** The owner's rule: no per-frame main-thread work, on-demand only. All seven findings kept their behaviour; only the cadence or the number of native calls changed. Savings are arithmetic from the review's measured rows (a native call through CET is about 8 us on this install, the docs use 25 to 30 us), not measurements.
- **1. History scan readiness (`c2a0c3e9`, `mod/journal-history.lua`, `init.lua`):** a scan frame did the 7-call journal readiness check twice (before and after the step). Inside `updateKnowledge`, after this frame's session check, init.lua now vouches for the session (`convaiHeartbeat.sessionProven`), and the collector re-checks only the journal (`GetJournalManager`, `HasAnyDelayedStateChanges`) before and after the step: 14 calls become 4 per scanned frame. Outside that window (a capture on a send, tests) the full check runs. Saves 10 calls x 60 = 600 calls/s: 5 ms/s at 8 us, up to 15 ms/s at 25 us; the review reconciled about 10 to 12 ms/s of the 19 to 21 ms/s plateau.
- **2. Spoken replies (`b22f1265`, `speech.lua`, `continuous-speech.lua`, `facial-playback.lua`, `init.lua`):** the speaker identity (V's id, the actor attached and not dead), the voice-enabled read, `continuous.update`'s own 8-call `validActors` and the face layer's `speaker()` proof now run at 10 Hz (and at once for a new reply or speaker) instead of every frame; `convaiInMenu` is read once per frame; `facial-playback` `M.sync` no longer builds a closure per frame and reuses the provider and upper tables (the mix table is per expression slot, because the slot keeps it as `holdMix`). Target loss and a muted voice are noticed up to 100 ms later (tested: 7 frames at 60 FPS at most). Test count: `judy:IsAttached` 180 calls per 60 frames before, 16 after. Expected: about 13 to 18 native calls per speaking frame become about 2, 6 to 9 ms/s at 8 us (the review: 8 to 12 ms/s of the 21 to 46 ms/s measured), plus about 4 tables and a closure per frame of garbage.
- **3. Gaze scan (`d51cab93`, `init.lua`):** one candidate per entity at insertion (the other parts, the closest and the looked-at object used to be measured and dropped as repeats after their NPC, attached and dead reads); the Head slot (2 to 4 calls, 2 closures) is skipped for an NPC whose chest aim point is outside the 32 degree cone by more than the head's 1.5 m could move it, and never for the looked-at NPC; the per-candidate closures are named functions; and the scan is two phases on two 10 Hz ticks (`gatherTargets` on the half-way tick, the measuring on the next with fresh crosshair data), so the native query and the per-candidate reads no longer share a frame. The talk key still runs both at once. Estimate (the review's crowd figure is itself an extrapolation): 10 NPCs within 8 m, about 260 calls and one 8 ms spike every 12 frames become about 120 to 150 calls in two spikes of 2 to 4 ms; the quiet `init:gaze` row (3.2 ms/s) changes little. The tests that cut `targetAtCrosshair` out of init.lua now start the slice at `convaiEntityKey = function`.
- **4. World-ready bundle (`a8180622`, `Composer.reds`, `init.lua`):** new `PlayerPuppet.ConvaiFrameFlags()` returns a bit mask (attached 1, dead 2, pre-game 4, paused 8, in a menu 16, composer open 32, phone open 64); `convaiSessionReady` calls it once per frame and `convaiWorldReady`, the phone-open read and `convaiInMenu` read the mask: about 11 per-frame native calls become 1 (plus `GetPlayer`). A missing method or any error falls back to the old separate calls and tries the mask again after 1,200 frames. Saves about 9 calls x 60 = 540 calls/s: 4 ms/s at 8 us (the review: 6 to 7 ms/s). A redscript compile error would disable every `.reds` file; this one compiles.
- **5. Send-frame hitch (`5432932d`, `journal-history.lua`, `init.lua`):** opening the composer asks the collector to pre-encode the history rows of a scan under way (`preEncode(30)`: up to 12 rows and 1.5 ms per frame for 30 s), so `partialPart` on the send frame finds them encoded. Expected: the 37 to 38 ms `init:reply` maxima of windows 13 and 68 shrink to the rest of `sendRequest`, if the history rows were the source, as the review inferred (not proven; no `init:send` timer was added).
- **6. Loot hooks (`e646d8f5`, `loot-observer.lua`):** Added, Changed and Removing return at once while Loot reactions are off (the default): 12 to 18 native calls and 0.4 to 0.5 ms per inventory event become one settings read; a 100-event crafting or vendor burst loses about 50 ms. The ever-owned set is not fed while off (the baseline on turning it on rebuilds the owned counts), so an item acquired and consumed while off can later count as new equipment once.
- **7. `ReactionManagerComponent` overrides (`bf1248ff`, `vanilla-reactions.lua`):** the five CET overrides stay registered (CET cannot unhook), but each now starts with one `R.idle()` test and returns to vanilla before the protected call, the varargs and the stimulus read. Honest size: about 1 us of the 15 to 40 us a stimulus costs, 0.02 to 0.3 ms/s at 20 to 300 events/s. The real saving needs the redscript filter the review describes (a quiet-until deadline on the addressed NPC), which waits for a crowd capture.

**2026-10-22 (voice pipeline fixes from the Opus review `deliverables/review-voice-pipeline-2026-10-22.md`; branch `fix/voice-pipeline-1022` from main b21f2d81, worktree `.claude/worktrees/voice-pipeline-1022`, nine commits, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, and the two Python workers changed, so the Runtime needs an update zip. Left alone on purpose: the face timeline rebuild and `continuous-speech.lua` (perf agents), V on OmniVoice after the fallback and the Pocket language swap (`fix/028-regressions`); the `voice-selection.mjs` diffs are small additions).**
- **1. The worker chain (W1, W2, W3, W7).** An exit that could not be confirmed is looked at again (`bridge/worker-process.mjs` `recoverExit`: the process is polled, stopped again every 10 s, up to 2 min, through `closeConfirmed` in `voice-selection.mjs`, the V helper and the OmniVoice candidate) instead of leaving `retiring` rejected for the rest of the session; a later retire still closes its own worker. The kill is `%SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe /T /F` by PID with its exit code checked and a fallback to the handle (Pocket and OmniVoice). Cancel: 15 s (30 s before the first sound), then up to 15 s more with a log line, and the worker skips decoding its backlog the moment it is cancelled (`skip_decoding_when_stopped`) and goes to normal priority from its reader thread. Exit confirmation 15 s with a second kill at 6 s. The worker's ack wait is 45 s (Node's consumer limit is 30 s for the first packet, 10 s after) and ends only the request.
- **2. Pocket breaks (P1).** `continuous-pcm-core.mjs`: each break of a line doubles the refill (0.4 to 0.8, 1.6, 3.2, 4 s) and jumps to the measured carry time when the audio arrives slower than it plays (the worklet gives `append` the clock); a refill waits 6 s at most. `speech-pace.mjs` now follows the broken line's speed and the bridge keeps one pace per engine (Voxtral, Pocket, Convai); the log line prints the real lead.
- **3. "Startup stalled" (W4).** The worker's heartbeat carries read and written bytes and the module count besides CPU time; any of them growing is progress; no progress for the window gets one extra wait (60 s, 120 s while importing) before the stop; a restarted worker gets at least 200 s of the bound.
- **4. V's Voxtral limit (R1).** `lane: 'v'`: a 429 on V's request pauses V only (`readyForV`) and holds the shared scheduler 1.5 s at most; the companion's reply is asked as usual. A reply that finds the cloud voice cooling down for 1.5 s or less waits instead of being written.
- **5. Failures that repeat (W5, W6).** `voice-failures.mjs` and `permanentVoiceFailure`: Windows blocks, Pocket integrity or version mismatches (source differs from the pinned revision, assets missing, a worker that does not attest), missing files or modules are not retried by Pocket, OmniVoice or V's helper (one log line). A dead worker's failure carries the exit code in words and the last error line of its stderr (so a CUDA out-of-memory load on a small card now reaches the existing memory rule), both workers turn `faulthandler` on, and an access violation gets one retry after 5 s with `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_CUDA_GRAPH=0`.
- **6. A Voxtral stall holds the text (R2).** The first ask is hedged: no audio 2.5 s after the request was sent and the same line is asked again in parallel, the first audio wins (V's own lane is not hedged; when both fail the first ask's error stands, and the hedge's 429 pauses the scheduler for a moment only); first-audio limits are 5 s (was 7) and 6 s for the second ask (was 10). Publishing the text before any audio exists was NOT done: `ConvaiContinuousSpeech.frame` and the Lua side admit an actor only with validated PCM, and changing that needs a live test (see the owner list).
- **7. V on Voxtral with no key (R6).** `vSettingsFor` keeps V's engine on Voxtral without a key (Mature content still makes it Pocket): no Pocket worker for V, the line is skipped with 'no Mistral key', and V speaks as soon as a key is saved.
- **8. V's lines and the wall-clock limits (R4, W12).** A V line is no longer dropped for length (no rescue budget) nor stopped by the companion's voice request on the shared worker; the reply waits for it and follows it; it is given up only when stuck: no audio 30 s after the reply was ready (`V_GRACE_MS`, was 600 ms). Pocket's 120 s render limit is 120 s to the first sound and then 60 s without a new chunk; the worker's wall timer is a `ProgressTimer` (every chunk and acknowledged packet starts it over); the local PCM page's 150 s counts from the last accepted packet or the last advance of the heard position.
- **9. Convai rate correction (R3).** The page also reports the rate the player was opened at (`openedSampleRate`) and the host hands the live speech that rate, so a correction found with the final statistics no longer throws "Continuous speech format changed"; the corrected rate still goes to the remembered-rate store. The first turn of an unremembered mislabelled character plays at the label's rate (too fast) and completes; re-opening the player is not possible because the correction is known only after all the audio has played.

**2026-10-22 (native plugin fixes from the Opus review; branch `fix/native-1022` from main b21f2d81, worktree `.claude/worktrees/native-1022`, 14 commits, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed in the game, game not launched; `native/core`, `mod/native-core.lua` and its tests; the DLL is rebuilt, a bridge restart is not needed, a game restart and a CET reload are).** Source: `deliverables/review-native-plugin-2026-10-22.md`. New DLL `CyberpunkConvaiNative.dll`, SHA-256 `efeb0a65cb181babe44bd0de1e33fcf8a7fd7a9acf36a534526bba3090718d6a`, built clean from commit `2c6b4353` under `%TEMP%\release-u4\nb-1022` with `scripts/Build-NativeCore.ps1` (copy in the scratchpad `natives-1022/CyberpunkConvaiNative-2c6b4353.dll`). 75 headless tests pass (two latency tests, `io_worker_notices_a_replaced_file_within_a_few_ms` and `io_game_thread_never_waits_for_the_workers_json_check`, fail on a loaded machine and pass on a quiet one: they are timing, not logic), the plugin host loads the DLL, and the 86 Lua and packaging tests around `native-core.lua` pass. An Opus review of the branch found one real regression (a switched-off system could not flush or answer the handshake) and five smaller points; all fixed in `2c6b4353`.
- **Threads (`313bc743`, `2d78c20a`):** file IO now starts after everything in `Load` that can still fail (the RTTI check moved up), every failed `Load` stops it, and the module is pinned (`GetModuleHandleEx` with the pin flag) before any thread is detached, so a late worker can never run in an unmapped DLL. The watcher and worker thread bodies catch everything, log it and stop cleanly (the worker marks IO as stopped and wakes the waiters; `Stop` still joins the watcher when the worker ended itself).
- **Guard (`473f2e9e`, `2c6b4353`):** a system is switched off at its first structured exception (C++ exceptions still count three). Every native checks a lock-free off flag first (set by the kill-switch file, `all` and a trip; `core` is never off). The log names the exception code, the faulting module and offset, the access kind and address, and the native (`std::source_location`). `rtti::GuardAlways` is for the natives that must work while their system is off: `Io.Flush`, the handshake write and remove, the faces pose release, clear and reset.
- **MO2 (`20f8726b`, `456acb61`):** when `usvfs_x64.dll` is loaded the plugin replaces files with `MoveFileExW` instead of the handle-based rename that bypasses the virtual file system; `ConvaiNative.Status()` has `"vfs":true|false`. The handshake failure reason now reads: `the plugin writes to a different runtime folder: <step>; plugin folder <path>, CET folder <path>[ (a virtual file system is loaded)]`, where the step is the native write refused, the flush timed out, the file missing in CET's folder or other text there. (The reason text is in the same commit as finding 7 because both rewrite the handshake.)
- **Handshake gates only `io` (`456acb61`):** `present` (plugin loaded, same API) gates every system, `ioReady` (handshake) only `io`; `api.ioReady` and `api.ioReason` exist. `CheckVersion` no longer needs the file worker. On a failed handshake the game's `io` and `os` stay untouched and faces, vehicles, chauffeur, passage, clearance, actions and gaze still run natively. Tests that said "present == false" now say "ioReady == false and actuator still native".
- **Kill switch and verify files (`1d779933`):** UTF-8 byte order mark and UTF-16 (marked in either order, or recognised by the zero bytes) parse like plain text, in `Switches::ParseFile` and in the two Lua parsers (`controlText`); the log line now lists the names it read.
- **FPS (`d1f4d1fd`, `5ebbe141`):** vehicles call sites keep six (class, function) pairs, misses included, so the mounting check no longer re-walks 1,500 functions on every class change. The combat-flag routes and a missing static function are searched once (lists included) and a miss stands for the session: no 256th-call rescan, no list dump twice.
- **Faces (`56373b08`):** NaN or infinity in the control or speech array is replaced by 0 (logged once) and the frame goes on; a short array or an unknown family returns -1 (rejected frame, not a fault). Lua is untouched, so a later `-4` code with a Lua fallback was not needed.
- **File order (`b9874cfa`):** a write merges only into the last queued operation, so A, B, A' reach the disk in that order (a marker file lands after its payload). The cost is fewer merges when two channels alternate.
- **Mackinaw (`fe523743`):** the seat check compares the TweakDB ID's low 40 bits (hash and length), not the offset bits.
- **Checked calls (`ba3c69a1`, fixes in `2c6b4353`):** `plugin/CheckedCall.hpp/.cpp` (`Verified`, `CheckSignature`, `Invoke`, `ExecuteForObject`, and the vehicles `Value` moved there) checks parameter count, sizes and types and the return type and size once per function and call-site shape (cached), and a mismatch is one WARN line plus "unavailable", so Lua runs that call. Used by `game::Call` and `CallStatic`, `Player()`, `GameSystem`, the combat routes, faces, vehicles and chauffeur (typed arguments; the chauffeur owner must be the dynamic entity system, `given` an AICommand), actuator, clearance (`Overlap`, `SyncRaycastByCollisionGroup` against `physicsTraceResult`) and gaze (the player must be an `entEntity`). A function that returns a weak handle into our strong `Handle` is converted instead of written as is (review finding 4). Integers are checked by size only, struct names only where the RTTI name is certain.
- **Not done:** the review's findings 13 (game-thread flushes), 15 (per-call heap work) and the Low list (verify mode for faces and gaze, passage and clearance finite checks, the RTTI host class flags, actuator miss warning every tick) were not in this pass.

  1. **Load:** `CyberpunkConvaiNative ... loaded` and `RTTI: ... registered N natives` for all nine classes; no `Native fault`. `probe.log` shows `Native core: io=native`.
  2. **Every system once, and grep the RED4ext log for `does not match what the plugin calls it with`:** any hit is a call that worked before this branch and is now on the Lua path (the line names the function and the reason). Expected: no hit. The most likely ones to check are actuator (`IsAttached`, `IsDeadNoStatPool`, `GetWorldPosition`, `GetCommandState`), clearance (`Overlap`, `SyncRaycastByCollisionGroup`, the `physicsTraceResult` size), gaze (`SetEntityTarget`, `SetWorldOffset`, `SetStyle`, `SetAdditionalPartsArray`), chauffeur (the owner and `GetCommandState`) and the combat flag (`Game access: combat flag read through ...`).

  4. **Vehicles and chauffeur:** ride with a companion (mounting check) and call a Delamain/leased car: `vehicles=native`, `chauffeur=native`, no seat stuck on the Mackinaw (the back right seat stays unused).
  5. **Passage and clearance:** a lift ride and a door or doorway pass with a companion: `passage=native`, `clearance=native`.
  6. **Actions (actuator) and gaze:** a companion that follows, waits and looks at V: `actuator=native`, `gaze=native`, no `Gaze:` decline line.

  8. **MO2 handshake location check (the item the review called the biggest practical problem):** run the game through Mod Organizer 2 with a copy of the mod also installed physically in the game folder (the case that failed). Expect `Status().vfs` true (`"vfs":true` in the status JSON or in a support report), `Native core: io=native` and a `runtime/native-handshake.txt` that never stays behind. If the handshake still fails, `probe.log` has the new line `io=lua (the plugin writes to a different runtime folder: ...; plugin folder ..., CET folder ...)`: send both folders; every other system must still read `=native`. Also check where `*.native-tmp` files appear while the game runs (the MO2 overwrite folder or the real folder). Without MO2 the plain game must read `"vfs":false`.

**2026-10-22 (bridge latency and resource pass from `deliverables/review-performance-2026-10-22.md`; branch `perf/bridge-1022` from main b21f2d81, worktree `.claude/worktrees/perf-bridge-1022`, 8 fix commits (one per finding) plus a packaging commit, the log entry and the review-pass fixes below, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `bridge/` and three docs only, so a bridge restart and the next Runtime update zip; no `mod/`, `r6/` or locale change).** One commit per finding, each with tests; the full suite (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, 8,164 tests) is green apart from two things this pass caused and fixed in the ninth commit: the new `child-registry.mjs` had to be listed in `packaging/runtime-layout.mjs` and `release-plan.json`, and the voice routing test sandbox needed `replyStreaming: false`.
- **1. Local AI no longer waits for the action decision when the words certainly settle it (`da042daf`, narrowed in the review pass below).** On a route that serves one request at a time (`parallel: false`: Local AI and a model server the player runs) the model decision is skipped only for a line that is nothing but a command ("drive me", "Judy, follow me.", "attack him"; plain ASCII, DRIVE, FIGHT or FOLLOW, never a leave) and for a line that is nothing but a question about the character herself ("do you know how to drive?", "did you ever fight in the pits?"). Questions that are requests, suggestions ("Why don't you drive?", "How about you take the wheel?", "Are you coming with me?"), remarks, every dismissal ("I work alone.", "Why don't you go home?"), a leave among the words the screen found, and every other language (a Polish "i" is not read as English "I") go to the model as before, and the reply still waits for that decision (one slot: a decision sent beside the reply only queues in front of it or behind it, so "start the reply first" cannot work there). The action still goes to the game after the reply, and the persona stays in the slot when no second request replaced it. `noteSlot(null)` is left as it is on purpose: it is true when a decision does run. Gain: the decision's whole round trip (about 0.2 to 0.6 s on a free card, several seconds at 3 to 5 tokens a second) on the common bare commands and questions, fewer than before the narrowing. - **2. Default route streams the first sentence to the voice (`34d2de2f`).** Convai text with a local voice (Pocket, Voxtral, OmniVoice) now goes through `respondConvaiStreamed`: `RealtimeHost.evaluateSpeech` reads the reply's text so far from the page every 40 ms (`window.convaiRealtime.partialReply(key)`, the key is the turn's own marker so no other turn's text is ever read) into a `ReplyStream`, and `voiceStreamedReply` (the same code as Mistral and Local AI) starts the voice on the first safe sentence. The finished reply is cut back to the sentence the voice already has if it disagrees; Convai's emotion label (the ordered one, or the late one by token) is read when the reply returns and the face planner takes it up as before. Not for a held look-ahead speaker, a reaction line, or Convai's own voice, and `replyStreaming: false` still turns it off. The page half is in `bridge/realtime-client.mjs`, so the Runtime update zip must carry the rebuilt `realtime-client.js` bundle (`npm run build:voice`); an older bundle has no `partialReply`, the poll reads nothing and the reply is voiced as a whole, as before. **Not measured: no Convai call was made here.** Estimate 0.3 to 0.7 s of first word (the gap between the first sentence and the full text; the reviewer's figure), zero if Convai delivers its text in one piece. The stage clock now shows it: `firstSentence` and `ttsSent` before `fullText`, `streamedHead: true` in the record. Tests `convai-text-stream.test.mjs`, `realtime-client.test.mjs`.

Prompt cache order (`1a8f8ccc`).** The per-turn world knowledge block now follows the older-talk summary in the system message (its own short heading "WORLD KNOWLEDGE FOR THIS TURN") instead of sitting inside the world context before it, and the world context's cap cuts at a place that no longer depends on the facts' length (it moved with it before). The game reads none of `coverage` (checked in `mod/`). Gain: the 65 + 30 ms/s of copy and encode the review measured for a 10 s line now happens only while audio is still arriving. Not incremental row by row (rows before the end can change when a phonetic interval or the model arrives late), so a growing line still re-copies per packet.
- **6. CompanionVision (`f918412f`).** No picture is held while another provider answers (frames, staged frame, queue, recordings' frames, answered turns' pictures), the pictures of answered turns go after 90 s and a recording's after 10 minutes, the ids stay. Knowledge parts (`9f8d3952`, reworked in the review pass).** The game publishes a part inside the turn's own capture (`mod/init.lua` `captureKnowledge`), in the same frame as the request, so a per-revision preload on a file watcher only moved the turn's parse into another callback and could parse the same part twice; it is gone. What stays is the start-up preload for a bridge that is restarted while a session runs (the supervisor restarts it after a crash): 2 s after start the three parts written in the last 15 minutes are read (async), their header is looked at first so a revision already in memory is never parsed again, calls share one read, then parsed and frozen; an older file (an earlier session) is not read at all. **2026-10-22 (security and privacy fixes that needed no owner decision, from `deliverables/review-security-privacy-2026-10-22.md`; branch `fix/security-1022` from main b21f2d81, worktree `.claude/worktrees/security-1022`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT deployed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/`, `mod/` (two Lua files), `packaging/`, `auth-backend/`, `scripts/` and the release workflow changed, so a bridge restart, a CET reload and the next Scripts and Runtime update).** Findings 1 to 4 (shared Convai key, shared report and token secret, release signing, add-on consent and sandboxing) wait for the owner and are untouched. One commit each, with tests:
- **Report text reaching agents (finding 5, `91e24ac3`):** `scripts/Fetch-ErrorReports.mjs` now writes INDEX.md as an untrusted-data header, a table of fixed-shape fields only (signature, kind, counts, versions, dates, each checked), and every free-form string (messages, frames, slow-turn values) in fenced blocks as one escaped JSON string per value (backtick, angle and square brackets, `://` and invisible or bidi characters escaped or removed). Each saved `<id>.json` starts with an `_untrusted` notice the server's answer cannot replace. Unicode Tag characters and every other invisible format character are stripped from the index and the saved files. Agent briefs should still say that report content is untrusted data.
- **Report flooding (`a59cfb73`, not deployed):** `auth-backend` counts an IPv6 caller per /48 for error reports (the token handler keeps /64), keeps the first 3 bodies of a signature pinned (the rest of the 10 are the newest), and the index text is a running majority vote of the reports, not the first writer's. Needs a deploy to take effect; 126 auth-backend tests pass.
- **Opt-out (finding 7, `25c2e1ab`):** nothing is sent before the game has marked the in-game notice (`errorReportsNoticed` in settings.json; what is queued waits, up to a week), and a settings file that is there but unreadable (no readable copy) is an unknown state: nothing recorded, sent or deleted, never on. A non-boolean `errorReports` counts the same. Merge review fix (`26405565`): the Lua side does NOT save the setting off for an unreadable file; it acts as a fresh install (on, notice flag gone), so the notice is shown and marked again, the queue is kept and nothing is sent before that. Residual: a player who had turned reports off and whose settings file is then damaged loses that choice (the notice comes back before anything is sent).
- **Scrubbing gaps (finding 10, `95bdd9a0`):** the support report passes the player's account names to the redactor (a path anywhere, not only under `C:\Users`), the error reports do too (two-letter names as path parts only), and both the service and `mod/support-report.lua` now scrub `user:pass@host`, emails, secret-named query values (`code`, `pass`, `pwd`, ...), the Mistral key as exactly 32 letters and digits (hyphenated or underscored runs stay at 40, so model and record names survive), and a Lua user path with a space in the name. File names such as `kokoro@v1.0.onnx` are not e-mail addresses. Not done: the computer name in UNC paths.
- **Hidden Chromium sandbox (finding 8, `aaf0a01e`, reworked in `2f134ddc` after the merge review):** `chromiumSandbox: true`, no `--no-sandbox`. The sandboxed browser is trusted only after one blank page has opened and run a line (8 s at most, once per start); the sandboxed launch has a 20 s limit; a failure, hang or dead first page closes it and starts it again without the sandbox, and the result is remembered by all three hosts and in `browser-sandbox.json` in the state folder (per browser, 30 days; delete the file to retry). Real Edge and Chrome pass the probe here. Not tried under Wine or Proton. Known limit (docs/CONVAI_AUDIO_STREAMING.md): audio-enhancement software silencing a sandboxed browser cannot be detected; live check: one Convai voice turn with the sandbox on, audio heard, first-sound time against main.
- **Convai sign-in (finding 9, `ad89dff6`, reworked in `20e2ab59` after the merge review):** the loopback callback is taken at once only when the browser's Referer says login.convai.com; any other callback (another site, a loopback Referer, none) is redirected to a clean `/confirm-page?state=...` that names the site and saves nothing until the player clicks there; a callback with nothing usable ends the sign-in at once with the did-not-finish page. The live Convai page has still never been tried, so it is not known whether it sends a Referer to loopback (if not, every sign-in shows the confirm page). The "show the account name before saving" idea of the review is not done (needs a UI).
- **Key headers on redirects (finding 11, `809308f7`):** `redirect: 'error'` on every Convai call that carries `CONVAI-API-KEY` or `API-AUTH-TOKEN` (bridge and auth-backend) and on every Mistral call. Dev scripts under `scripts/` were left as they were.
- **vgmstream (finding 12, `3b634186`):** each decode runs with `-i`, a 10 s limit and a 16 MB output cap that is watched while the file is written (vgmstream is stopped past it). Not done: caching a failed archive by hash (a bad mod still costs one capped decode per start).
- **DLL temp folder (finding 13, `52f7d87e`):** the `C:\Users\Public` fallback is gone; the fallback is a folder under the player's own LOCALAPPDATA or USERPROFILE when that path is ASCII, else one clear log line and the probe fails as before (Lip sync delay assumes 0 ms).
- **Removal list (finding 14, `5e59be44`):** a part that looks like an 8.3 name (`~1`) is refused, and the protected paths are checked again against the file's resolved real name (catches short names and junction aliases). The real 8.3 case was tested on this C: volume.
- **Release workflow (finding 6, `491715e5`, not run):** actions pinned by commit SHA (checkout 4.4.0, setup-node 4.4.0, setup-python 5.6.0, upload-artifact 4.6.2, SHAs checked with `gh api`), `persist-credentials: false`, `contents: read` at the top, `contents: write` only on the Runtime job (publishing is the last step of that job; splitting it into its own job would mean handing the multi-GB zips between jobs as artifacts, not done), CI Python tools installed from `packaging/ci-tools.requirements.txt` with `--require-hashes --no-deps` (CPython 3.12 win_amd64 only), `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (only esbuild has an install script, not needed), ffmpeg 9.0.2 from the gyan.dev GitHub release with its SHA-256 checked instead of `choco install`. The PowerShell ffmpeg step has only been read, not run on a runner.
- **Not fixed (finding 15 and the info items):** the model manifest and Pocket YAML integrity pins, bare-name executables, the editor token in the URL, the llama-server port race, the public `/api/readyz`, a `.vercelignore` for `auth-backend/`.

**2026-10-21 (branch `feat/v-voice-omni` from main c7b5d5e0; unit-tested and timed on the real OmniVoice pack, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): OmniVoice as an engine for V's own voice.** A player asked for it; the owner accepted a short wait on typed turns. V's voice list (Off, Pocket, Voxtral) gets a fourth entry, "OmniVoice · short wait" (`vVoiceEngine: 'omni'`).
- **Design (docs/V_VOICE.md, "V on OmniVoice").** V's line is one more job on the companions' own OmniVoice worker, 16 steps, v-male / v-female references, queued the moment the line is built at the top of `runInput` (`VLine.omniProducer`, not waiting for the renderer page), so it renders while the companion's text is written; the companion's renders queue right behind it (ResidentVoice runs one job at a time, in call order; a V job still queued when its turn ends is cancelled before it starts). Owner change mid-task: no time cap. The `VLine` is `patient` (no grace, no rescue budget): the reply waits for V's first audio however long the render takes and then for V's end; only a real failure (worker error, exit, its own 2-minute render limit, no audio, the turn ended, the Omni route gone) skips V, with one log line giving the reason, and the companion answers as if V were off. Nothing extra loads: `VVoice.wantsPocket` is false for the engine, so no V Pocket worker, and no second Omni worker; V's voice is one more prepared prompt in the Omni worker's cache (8). Prepared at the composer opening (`prepareOmni`, about 0.8 s once). Any language (OmniVoice speaks every language; Pocket stays English only, Voxtral keeps its list). Playback Off releases OmniVoice and V is silent then (nothing loads in its place).
- **Offered only with OmniVoice companions.** Usable when the pack is installed and the saved companion voice is OmniVoice (`mod/manager.lua` `vOmniBlock`; bridge: `vOmniUsable` + `vSettingsFor` in `bridge/v-voice.mjs`). Otherwise greyed out with a reason (MCM `disabledElements[4]`; Native Settings UI: label "OmniVoice · needs Omni voice" / "needs Omni pack", apply refuses it). A saved `omni` that is not usable reads as Pocket (value left alone); a save that moves the companions off OmniVoice also saves V as Pocket with the notice "V's voice switches from OmniVoice to Pocket." An Omni worker that is only loading or failing does not change the engine (V's line is skipped with the reason; no Pocket worker is started beside it).
- **Measured on this PC (RTX 4080 Laptop, Balanced, game closed, player install's pack, repo's ResidentVoice, long reference, warm):** V's render at 16 steps 0.76 s (53 chars, 4.2 s of speech), 0.90 s (91 chars, 7.0 s), 0.97 s (117 chars, 9.3 s); at 32 steps 0.99 to 1.61 s; prepare 0.78 s (male) / 0.87 s (female); a new text length costs about 0.2 s (graph capture); V line then companion phrase queued together: V done at 0.77 s, companion's phrase at 1.7 s. So V is first audible about 0.8 to 1 s after the send (plus the renderer's start buffer), about 1 s later than Pocket V, and the reply starts when V has ended; vs V off the reply is later by that first-audio time plus V's speaking time (about 4 s for a 50-character line), not 1.5 to 3 s. The settings help text says "a short wait (about a second more than Pocket, before V starts)". Raw numbers: scratchpad `vomni/raw-long.json`.
