**2026-10-21 (memory extraction loop on Convai; branch `fix/memory-extract-loop` from main 25fb84d6, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; bridge code changed, so the bridge needs a restart):** a clean 0.2.6 player install (Convai chat, Voxtral voice, a Mistral key set) logged `memory extract failed (Mistral cannot extract facts now [mistral:request]); retrying in 60 s ... 480 s` forever. Cause: the memory store (`bridge/memory-store.mjs`, the per-character store under `local-memory/`) schedules fact extraction whenever an extractor is set and exchanges are pending, and the host's extractor (`#extract` in `bridge/text-provider-host.mjs`) refuses on the Convai route (`provider.active` false: Convai keeps its own long-term memory); that refusal counted as a failure and backed off. Owner decision: extraction never runs on the Convai route, even with a Mistral key, and no fallback uses the key for Convai chats. Fix: `setExtractor(fn, canRun)` plus `refresh()` on the store; while `canRun` is false nothing is scheduled (no attempt, no retry, no log line, no timer; the exchanges stay pending); the host passes `provider.active` and re-plans on `provider.onChange` (unsubscribed in `close`); a job that was planned before a switch to Convai ends quietly (`retryLater`, no backoff, no log). Mistral, Local AI and Custom extraction is unchanged, a real failure still backs off and logs. Tests: two in `bridge/memory-store.test.mjs`, two in `bridge/text-provider-host.test.mjs` ("Convai route: no extraction scheduled", "Mistral route: unchanged"). Full suite green.
**2026-10-21 (error reports for 0.2.7, second pass; branch `fix/reports-027` from main 25fb84d6, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `bridge/` only, a bridge restart picks it up; no Lua, no new strings):** fetched 14 new reports (259 in all; 0.2.6 is now 27 reports from 11 installs, 11 of them new from 4 installs); triage in `deliverables/error-reports-triage-2026-10-21b.md`. Every new signature was checked in the code; only one is a real bug.
- **`55741d05` "Invalid continuous speech state", Convai voice + automatic language (install `ab6981`, GTX 1060, Portuguese; the same line fails on every twin turn in its log):** the Convai multilingual twin sends 44.1 kHz audio labelled 24 kHz; a LIVE (continuous) turn already plays at 24 kHz when the final statistics correct the rate, so the turn fails (position past the shorter duration), it does not "play slow once" as the morning triage and `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` said. Main's per-character memory (`eb027257`) learned only from a turn that succeeded, so a character that failed never learned and failed forever. Fix: the page snapshot carries `sampleRateCorrected` / `sampleRateHintMissed`, `RealtimeHost.evaluateSpeech` learns them in its `finally` (a failing turn still teaches its character), and the multilingual twins are seeded with the 24,000 to 44,100 hint (`audioRateSeed`, `AudioRates` `seed`; a seed the statistics do not confirm is dropped for good and saved as `null`). Tests: `convai-audio-rates.test.mjs`, `realtime-client.test.mjs`. **Live check owed:** Convai voice, a Portuguese or Spanish line with an NPC: the first line of a twin plays at normal speed and does not fail. If the seed is wrong for some twin its first line fails once, then it is remembered as right.
- **Not fixed, with reasons:** `6a584052` (Convai replaced the speech owner, once, right after the failed twin turns: probably a follow-on of the above), `3d51bdf8` (Convai memory NETWORK_ERROR on a stalled PC), `fe955b83` / `3e3639c4` (Pocket worker starved of CPU), `014a3be6` / `316c6d2b` (real low system memory with a 4B Mature model, designed message), setup signatures (`22703faa`, `de57ef76`, `a08726a2`). `1aa616f1` fired again on 0.2.6 and is already fixed on main (`ef00a780`).

**2026-10-21 (the llama.cpp engine moves into the Runtime; branch `feat/engine-in-runtime` from main c0346235, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, no package built, game not launched; `bridge/local-ai-pack.mjs` needs a bridge restart, packaging files are build-time):** owner decision, so an engine fix reaches players through the small Runtime update zip instead of a 1.4 to 5.3 GB pack.
- **Design.** The Runtime carries `app/llama-cpp/` (llama-server, llama-fit-params and the libraries they load: 26 files, 82.5 MiB, 29.8 MiB zipped; same pinned zip, hash and keep/drop/require as before; `localAi.server.runtimeFolder`). `detectLocalAiPack` (`bridge/local-ai-pack.mjs`, the one place `pack.server` is made, so `LocalLlmServer`, `LlamaEmbedder` and `fitToolPath` follow) takes the Runtime engine FIRST when all of `ENGINE_FILES` are beside the server, else the pack's own `llama/llama-server.exe` as before (still chosen from one real folder under MO2). The service passes `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_ENGINE = layout.engine` (the real `appDirectory/llama-cpp`; a player's own value is stripped), the bridge falls back to `<project>/llama-cpp`. A pack marker or Mature marker with no `server` counts when the Runtime has the engine; a developer folder (`CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_AI_DEV`) keeps its own engine. The answer carries a new `engine: {source: 'runtime'|'pack'|null, runtimeMissing?}` field ONLY when the Runtime has an engine folder (a pack-only install is byte-identical to before). Name `llama-cpp`, not `llama`, so it cannot be confused with a pack's `llama/`.
- **Combinations (all tested).** old pack + older Runtime (unchanged); old pack + new Runtime (Runtime engine runs the pack's models); models-only pack + new Runtime (works) or + older Runtime (not installed, as before); new Runtime with no pack or an own server (engine present, `installed` false, `missing` `['model','embed']`, no process, no notice); Mature pack alone (models-only or not); Runtime engine missing a DLL (an antivirus tool: falls back to the pack's copy, support report `packFiles.engine` and the MO2 log lines say what is missing).
- **Packs.** Decision: keep the engine in the packs for one release (`localAi.server.inPacks: true`, the default) and flip it to false at the next pack rebuild. Why: no pack has to be rebuilt or re-uploaded for this change (the packs on Hugging Face are reused unchanged and the old ones work with the new Runtime), and a pack a player downloads without updating the Runtime still runs. With `inPacks` false the build writes models only (no `llama/`, no llama licence file, no `server` in the manifest or Mature marker, notices point at the Runtime), about 37 MB smaller per pack, and the pack needs Runtime 0.2.7 or later (say so on Nexus requirements and the model card).
- **Removal safety / update zip.** `apply-removals` already protects `app/local-ai/` as a whole; a test names `llama/llama-server.exe` and the DLLs. The Runtime update from 0.2.6 adds the 26 files (`build-runtime-update` compares paths, so nothing to change; a test builds an update from a Runtime without the engine). `packaging/lib/runtime-required.mjs` has a third group, `llama.cpp engine`, so `check-runtime-contents.mjs` and the install test refuse a Runtime without it.
- **MO2.** The engine is one folder of the Runtime's mod: server, DLLs and fit tool are always neighbours; the packs' markers and models are found through the merged virtual folder as before. Tests (`packaging/engine-in-runtime.test.mjs`): both models-only packs in separate mods on the Runtime mod's engine, a Mature pack alone, old packs beside the new Runtime mod, old packs without it.
- **Size.** Runtime 0.2.6 is 1,024,672,024 bytes; the engine adds about 31.2 MB zipped (+3.0%, about 1,055.9 MB) and 82.5 MiB on disk. The Runtime update from 0.2.6 is the old 0.2.6-to-0.2.7 content plus about 31.2 MB (the 0.2.5-to-0.2.6 update was 899,507 bytes). The packs shrink by about 37 MB each only after `inPacks` is flipped. Under the 1.95 GB per-asset limit.
- **Antivirus / Windows.** The binaries are unsigned, as in the packs. What changes: every Runtime player now gets 26 unsigned files (a 41 MB `ggml-vulkan.dll`, `llama-server.exe`) on disk, not only pack owners, so Defender or another scanner may flag or quarantine one on extraction even for players who never use Local AI (the engine check then falls back to a pack copy, else Local AI is unavailable with the usual reason; nothing else in the Runtime depends on them); a Nexus or mod-manager scan sees them too. Nothing runs them unless Local AI is on (no process, no `--list-devices`), so Smart App Control / Application Control still only matter at the spawn, with the same `windows-blocked` reason as before; a block now also hits a player whose pack was not the source of the file. Files extracted by Explorer carry the download mark in both cases.
- **Tests.** New `packaging/engine-in-runtime.test.mjs` (11), 9 new in `bridge/local-ai-pack.test.mjs`, release/runtime-contents tests updated. Full suite on this branch: 7820 tests, 7791 pass, 25 skipped, 4 fail, all four because this worktree has no `node_modules` (`release-inputs` playwright, `runtime-bootstrap` allowlist, `facial-timeline`, the pinned SDK adapter test); they pass in the main checkout. `packaging/test-release-install.mjs` (updated: Runtime engine starts with nothing else installed, fit tool answers, the bridge uses the Runtime engine, with `--local-ai` the pack-copy fall-back) was NOT run: it needs the built Scripts and Runtime zips (about 1 GB), both Local AI packs (6.7 GB), the launcher test host and, for the update variant, the 0.2.6 Runtime and Scripts zips; the release build is not allowed here.
- **Next release must.** (1) Replace `local-ai/dl-llama-vulkan/vulkan.zip` in the main checkout with b11782 (or build from the URL; the pin's sha256 is checked); the Runtime build needs the 36.8 MB zip. (2) Build the Runtime, then `build-runtime-update.mjs --old <0.2.6 Runtime> --new <0.2.7 Runtime>`: check it holds the 26 `app/llama-cpp/*` files and `app/licenses/llama.cpp-MIT.txt`. (3) Run `check-runtime-contents.mjs` on the Runtime and `test-release-install.mjs --local-ai` (and `--update-from`) with the 0.2.6 packs: expect "the packaged bridge uses the Runtime's engine" and the pack-copy fall-back. (4) No pack rebuild is needed; reuse the 0.2.x packs. (5) Nexus: mention that the Runtime is about 30 MB larger and carries the Local AI engine; when `inPacks` is flipped later, require Runtime 0.2.7+ for Local AI packs. (6) Live check: with the old pack and the new Runtime, Local AI starts from `app/llama-cpp` (the log's `View`/pack lines under MO2, `engine.build` b11782 in the report), then the fit lines on a tight card.

**2026-10-21 (pedestrian voice varied within one reply; branch `fix/one-reference-voice`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `bridge/voxtral-voice.mjs`):** the owner heard one Voxtral pedestrian ("Homeless Woman", `npc-homeless-female-v2`) sound like different people inside one reply.
- **Cause.** Not a per-segment or per-emotion reference choice (the voice key is picked once per turn, emotions are carried but read by no voice, Pocket and OmniVoice use one state or prompt per key and a fixed seed). The reference of an ordinary NPC is 2 to 6 game lines joined with silence, each in its own delivery, and Voxtral clones every request afresh: a reply is 2 to 4 requests (head and tail of the streamed reply, each split in two past 160 characters), so each leaned on a different line.
- **Fix.** `VoxtralVoice.build` sends one clip for references under `archetypes/`: `singleClip` takes the longest piece between seams of exact digital silence of 0.9 s or more, trimmed. Cached per voice, so the same bytes for every request and reply. 176 of 178 long references are cut (median 7.2 s); 2 stay whole (longest piece under 2 s). Named characters unchanged. Details in `docs/CLOUD_VOICE_VOXTRAL.md`, "Ordinary NPCs: one clip".
- **Owed.** Live check: a long reply from a pedestrian on Voxtral sounds like one person; the log has `[Voxtral] <key>: cloned from one clip, ...` once per voice. Prepared Ogg slots shipped for archetype voices no longer match (new signature): the next release's `voxtralCache` rebuilds them; until then a machine without ffmpeg sends the clip as a WAV (first audio up to about 0.8 s slower for those voices).

**2026-10-21 (MCM font on small screens; branch `fix/mcm-font-small-screens`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `mod/mcm-host.lua`, CET reload):** at windowed 1366x768 every setting label (bool, select, int) was cut to "(...)" while buttons were fine; 1080p and above were fine.
- **Cause (read in MCM's own files).** `rowFontSize` is not canvas units: `MCMPanelPresentation.Walk` sets each text to `size / accumulated widget scale`, so it is a size on the screen. The label boxes keep canvas units (`MCMLayout.reds`: content 980, label box 444 after `ApplyLabelWidth`), and the whole 1920x1080 canvas is shrunk by `uniformScale = min(width / 1920, height / 1080)` times the profile (`mcm_host.lua` density). A fixed 22 therefore takes a bigger share of the box the smaller the screen is; at 1366x768 the text is 22 / 0.711 = 31 canvas units in a box made for 22.
- **Rule.** `rowFontSize = floor(22 * min(w / 1920, h / 1080))`, never above 22 (so 1080p and up stay 22: 1600x900 gives 18, 1366x768 gives 15, 1280x720 gives 14). The text then takes the same share of its box as at 1080p, in every profile. Under 12 (below about 1046x589, MCM refuses sizes under 12) or when `GetDisplayResolution()` cannot be read, the option is left out and MCM keeps its own size, which always fits. `labelIndent` stays 20 (canvas units, scale-free). Assumption to confirm live: MCM's host size (ink root) equals `GetDisplayResolution()`; the density formula is MCM's own.
- **When.** Read once when the presentation is given and again each time the page is opened (the shortcut in `M.open`, or the player picking the page in MCM: the closed to open edge in `update`); a call is made only when the size changed (MCM ignores an unchanged presentation), nothing per frame, nothing while closed. MCM 0.10.5 and Native Settings UI unchanged.
- **Live check owed:** windowed 1366x768 (and 1600x900): Settings page labels read in full, buttons look the same size; 1080p unchanged; change the resolution, reopen the page, the size follows.

- **Cause.** `bridge/turn-context.mjs` stated "It is raining." and the clock as a fresh fact in every turn of every kind (companion, stranger, phone). A model reacts to an unprompted fact that comes again and again (the add-on voice form was cut for the same reason on 2026-10-14). Health, heat and money are standing state, not scenery, and stay as they were.
- **Fix, no setting.** The weather and the part of the day leave the right-now block for one short line, `Background (mention only if it matters or V asks): It is late night, about 2 AM. It is raining.`, in the volatile tail, and a conversation hears each only when new to it: first turn, a change (weather kind, or part of the day), the first turn after 20 minutes of silence, or when V's words ask (keyword check). New `bridge/scenery-memory.mjs` (one entry per character, per physical NPC or per phone contact, 256 kept; the decision is made once per turn id so the prepared reply, the look-ahead, the turn and the log line agree; no id, no snapshot or a reaction is never gated; cleared with the conversation sessions). `bridge/turn-context.mjs` (`sceneryFor`, `split`, `fresh`, `background`), `bridge/quest-context.mjs` (`turnContextOptions`; the Background block follows the head and group blocks), `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` (log line ends `background=<chars>|none`; memory cleared where sessions are). The right-now block no longer changes when the weather comes and goes, so a text provider's prompt cache keeps its prefix; a prepared or prefetched reply needs no drop on a weather change (it is built from the same snapshot as the turn that uses it, like the clock was). Who gets what is unchanged.

Only the ordinary-NPC archetypes do: street resident ("wry humor about money and rain", also `characters/natural-speech/npc-street-resident-female.json`), and sample lines in food vendor and bartender. Not changed (generated files, not clearly the cause alone): owner decision whether to soften them if players still hear rain from street residents.

**2026-10-21 (0.2.5 error reports, round 3; branch `fix/reports-025c` from main fc2b8c82, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live provider turn; install all committed `bridge/` files and restart the bridge; no Lua, locale or catalog change):** triage of the newest reports found five issues; each is fixed with tests (details in `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, "0.2.5 error reports, round 3" and "Convai audio labelled with the wrong sample rate").
- **1. A step-down race left Local AI on the cloud for the rest of the session (`4e68387c`, "model server was stopped").** `#spillAct` stops the model and awaits the free-memory read; a retried turn's `ensure()` started the large model in that gap, `#stepDown` stopped it again, the turn failed with `stopped`, and `failure()` marked Local failed (`RETRY_ON_CHOICE` lacks `stopped`). `bridge/local-llm-server.mjs`: `ensure()` waits for a step under way (a gate held by every step-down, spill action and device-lost step; the steps start their next model through `#kick`), re-awaits the newer start when its own start ended with `stopped` because a newer one took its place (a plain `stop()` still ends with `stopped`); `bridge/text-provider-host.mjs` `failure()` no longer tells the provider about `stopped`.
- **2. The first turn after the idle stop ran out of time before asking (`22f77797`).** A "no attempt made" error (`noAttempt`, a record with no request time) is never counted as a stall, so a fast card is no longer pushed toward a step-down by a slow reload; its explanation says the model was loading or busy. The load now starts with the turn (`loadPending` / `prepare`), and the turn's clock gets `LOCAL_ATTEMPT_ROOM_MS` (15 s) after the model is ready, never past `LOCAL_TURN_HARD_CAP_MS` (86 s; the game gives up at 90). The 10-minute idle stop is kept (VRAM goes back to the game); the composer opening already reloads a stopped model through `prewarm`; no reload on merely looking at a character (hitch with nobody talking; FPS rule).
- **3. Dead first turn on 10 GB cards (RTX 3080, Mature good, 0.7 to 1 GB spilled every session).** One counter read at the first request of each load (`begin()`: persona warm-up or turn) and one when a turn has had no response headers after 10 s (`SPILL_LIMITS.noHeadersMs`, `LocalLlmServer.noteHeaders`, 20 s rate limit); a spill takes the existing refit / step-down path. Nothing per frame, nothing per turn, none without counters.
- **4. Convai audio at 44.1 kHz labelled 24 kHz failed the whole turn (`14e50b97`, `0e895ffe`; Multilingual on).** `bridge/convai-data-audio.mjs` takes the clip at 44,100 or 48,000 Hz (within 0.5%) when the byte count and the declared duration agree on it and writes the WAV at that rate; other format faults carry `formatFault`; `bridge/realtime-client.mjs` `audioOptional` (set from `localChoice(profile).uses` in `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` `realtimeConfig`) turns such a fault, on a player whose own voice is not Convai's and a turn not played live, into the written reply (`audioError`) with the connection retired after the reply. The follow-on "realtime connection closed" (`92f464e9`): `rejectTransport` already ignores the `disconnect` of a connection `close()` retired, and the fault no longer retires it; no separate guard.
- **5. Prompt-cache misses from the history fitter (confirmed in simulation).** `bridge/prompt-budget.mjs`: older exchanges are dropped one at a time, so a conversation at the limit moved the start of the history every turn (an RX 6700 XT re-read about 4,650 tokens with 0 cached, 22 to 26 s to the first word). They now go in blocks of `BUDGET.trimBlock` (3), so the prefix is byte-identical for up to three turns.
- **Tests:** `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs`, `bridge/local-turn-diagnostics.test.mjs`, `bridge/convai-data-audio.test.mjs`, `bridge/realtime-client.test.mjs`, `bridge/prompt-budget.test.mjs`.
- **Design questions for the owner:** (a) 10 GB cards: the 3,000 MiB game reserve (8 GB class) does not change a pick for 10 GB (Mature good needs 6,288 of 10,240 - 3,000 = 7,240); a reserve of about 4,000 would put every 10 GB player on the lite model on one install's evidence; left unchanged, the early spill look is the fix. (b) The turn can only be stretched 6 s past its 80 s budget because the game gives up at 90 s; a load longer than about 70 s still ends in the "still loading" words. Raising the game's 90 s for a turn that is known to be loading would need a Lua change. (c) A Convai-voice player (voice not local) still fails a turn on an audio format fault that is not a mislabelled standard rate.
- **Live checks owed (game, Local AI, install the committed `bridge/` files, bridge restart):** (a) Local AI, Mature good on a 10 GB card with the game open: the log has `graphics memory of the model server after the first persona warm-up after the load` (or `the first turn`) at the first composer opening, and a spill reloads fitted or steps down within seconds, before a turn is lost; (b) leave Local idle for 10+ minutes, open the composer, type and send: no `ran out of the turn's time before the model could be asked`, no `stalled` line for it, the reply arrives; (c) force a step-down while a turn is retried (small free memory): the turn is answered by the smaller model, Local stays the provider, no `stopped` failure, no cloud fallback notice that sticks; (d) Multilingual on with Pocket (English) and a non-English line: the reply is spoken by Convai at the right pitch or shown as text; the log has no `PCM size does not match`; (e) a long Judy talk at the context limit: consecutive `[LocalTurn]` lines show `cached` staying high (history start fixed for about three turns).

**2026-10-20 (0.2.5 error reports, round 2; branch `fix/reports-025b`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; install all committed `mod/` files incl. `mod/locales/*.lua` and `mod/setup-check.lua`, plus the Runtime bridge files):** triage of the latest automatic reports found four small issues, each fixed with tests.
- **1. Local AI `ErrorDeviceLost` never restarted the server (RX 580 8 GB, Vulkan: seven turns in a row, 50 to 100 ms each, until llama-server crashed).** `/health` still answers when the device is lost, so `recover()` returned null. Now `deviceLost` (`bridge/local-server-recovery.mjs`: `ErrorDeviceLost`, `device lost`, `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` in the error or in the server's log tail) sends the failed request to `LocalLlmServer.noteDeviceLost` / `recover({deviceLost})`, which ends llama-server and starts it again past the health check (2 s pause first, `deviceLostPauseMs`); the turn is asked once more on the new server and the usual `local-restarted` notice follows. The second loss of a session steps down one model size through the existing `#stepDown` (its `model-stepdown` notice; cloud when none is smaller), and the count restarts for the smaller model; a custom model is only restarted, and after two more losses Local AI is marked failed. One process counts once; a loss on the retry is noted at once. Fixture: `FAKE_LLAMA_DEVICE_LOST_FROM`. Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`.
- **2. Null Convai connection race (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'updateContext')`).** `reply()` awaited `connect` and `stageTurnVision` while `close()` set `client = null`. `bridge/realtime-client.mjs`: `reply()` checks `!client` or a changed epoch after each wait, and `updateContext` at its top and just before `connection.updateContext`; the turn then ends with an `AbortError` "Conversation cancelled" / "Conversation context update cancelled", which `reportableTurnFailure` never reports (name and the word "cancelled").
- **3. Latency: the repeated-line re-ask doubled a slow local turn (fullText 38.5 s, voiceStart 74.8 s).** `bridge/text-provider-host.mjs`: a reply whose only fault is a repeated line first has the repeated sentence left out (`dropRepeatedLines`, `bridge/mistral-prompt.mjs`, costs nothing, when words of its own remain); otherwise it is kept, not asked again, when the first attempt took longer than `SLOW_TURNS.slowMs` (15 s) or the local server is one stall from stepping down (`LocalLlmServer.stepDownNear`). A quick turn is asked again as before; a reply that breaks character or leaks reasoning is always asked again.
- **4. Wrong-base Runtime update showed as a bridge crash loop (Scripts 0.2.5 on Runtime 0.2.2, exit 1 within 0.3 s, 6 to 7 times).** `bridge/runtime-files.mjs`: `missingModuleInLog` also reads Node's `The requested module '...' does not provide an export named` and names the file relative to the Runtime; `versionMismatchInLog` tells it apart; `bridge/bridge-supervisor.mjs` logs `mismatchMessage` ("The Runtime does not match the mod's Scripts: ... Download the full Runtime again, or apply the Runtime update zips in order") and publishes `install-incomplete` after one start (no restart loop, no `bridge-crash` report). The game's line "The Runtime is incomplete ({code}). ..." now ends "(or apply the Runtime update zips in order), then restart the game." in English and all 15 `mod/locales`; `localization/en.json` regenerated and `--check` passes.
- **Tests:** `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs`, `bridge/local-server-recovery.test.mjs`, `bridge/realtime-client.test.mjs`, `bridge/error-reports.test.mjs`, `bridge/mistral-prompt.test.mjs`, `bridge/text-provider-host.test.mjs`, `bridge/runtime-files.test.mjs`, `bridge/bridge-supervisor.test.mjs`, `bridge/setup-check-lua.test.mjs`.

**2026-10-20 (Memory page deselect; branch `fix/memory-deselect`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; install all committed `mod/` files, CET reload):** player report on 0.2.5 (MCM): Companion Manager > Settings > Conversations > Memory > Whose memories: once a character is chosen it cannot be unchosen, only a game restart clears it.
- **Cause (`mod/manager.lua`, `M.selectMemoryCharacter`):** the choice is a single value (`memorySelected`, one character at a time, not a set), and pressing a row only ever assigned it; a second press on the chosen row set the same key again, so nothing could clear it, and the value lives for the whole Lua session (it is not saved, hence "restart the game"). The row's button text said "Selected", which read as a state and not as something to press. Not an MCM or Native Settings UI caching problem: both hosts redraw the whole page after every press (`schemaChanged = true` / the page signature includes `selectedKey`), and the test now shows the earlier choice goes back to Choose in the same redraw. "More than one" was the player's reading of that; the code never holds two.
- **Fix:** pressing the chosen character again unchooses it (it also drops a Forget review waiting for Confirm); the chosen row's button now reads **Unselect** (`mod/manager-ui.lua`), unchosen rows keep **Choose**; the line under the way back says "{name} unselected.". New strings Unselect and {name} unselected. are translated in all 15 `mod/locales/*.lua` (catalogue regenerated and checked; `scripts/Extract-UiCatalog.mjs` allowlists Unselect). No Clear selection button: with a single choice the Unselect press is the same thing. The choice is cleared when the memory service reports a character clear **succeeded** (`updateMemory`; not at Confirm, so a pending or failed clear keeps it and Forget can be tried again); a Forget all leaves it alone. It is **kept when leaving the Memory page**: the page's own note after closing says "Your selection is unchanged", the Forget review also survives leaving, and nothing is per-frame (the redraw happens only on a press or on navigation).

**2026-10-20 (MO2 voice workers: a player running the game through Mod Organizer 2 had no voice at all, V's included; branch `fix/mo2-voice-workers` from main 16c873d3, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live turn; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, and the service (`packaging/runtime/`) a game restart; no Lua, locale or catalog change).**
- **Cause, confirmed in code:** both Python workers compared `Path.resolve()` results. Under USVFS the resolved path of a file is the mod folder that holds that file, which is not where its folder resolves to when the folder is a merge of several mods, and the OmniVoice pack is a mod of its own outside the Runtime's folder. Pocket: `local_asset()` (`bridge/pocket_voice_runtime.py`) did `path.resolve().is_relative_to(root.resolve())` -> "Pocket export asset is missing or linked", fatal for the whole voice (V's helper uses the same worker); `plain_absolute()` returned the resolved path, so every later overlap and containment check used the real mod folders. OmniVoice: `resolve_worker_paths()` (`bridge/resident-voice-worker.py`) needed the model and adapter inside `ROOT` (the real folder of the worker script) -> "Portable voice assets must remain in the application directory"; `asset_file()`, `validate_portable_source()` and `checked_absolute_directory()` resolve the same way. The earlier doc claim that the workers' checks "canonicalize both sides alike" held only outside USVFS.
- **Fix (same approach as the Local AI and mic packs: the service's USVFS flag, nothing relaxed outside it):** with `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_USVFS=1` (set in every process the service starts under MO2; both worker spawns copy the bridge's environment) the workers compare paths as spelled (absolute, `..` collapsed, case folded, never resolved) and still refuse a symlink or junction in every component; Pocket's pinned source/asset SHA-256 checks and OmniVoice's reference hashes read the real bytes as before. Pocket: `usvfs_active`, `spelled_inside`, `plain_absolute`, `local_asset`, and the `pocket_tts` import check in `bridge/pocket-voice-worker.py`. OmniVoice: `usvfs_active`, `checked_absolute_directory`, `resolve_worker_paths`, `asset_file` (no resolved containment under USVFS; every part must be a plain name), plus a second approved root for model, adapter and Python package: the pack folder the service names in the new `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_OMNI_PACK` (`serviceEnvironment(layout, {usvfs})`, `start-service.mjs`; set only under usvfs; persistent voice data and the player folder must stay apart from it). A physical install sets neither variable; every check is identical there.
- **Not changed:** the phone-analysis worker (nothing in the player install writes its config), the setup-check "Pocket voice" row (its text says restart and send a report, which stays true for any other start failure; with the fix MO2 no longer hits it).
- **Tests:** `scripts/test_pocket_voice_runtime.py` (`UsvfsPaths`, 8) and `scripts/test_resident_voice_paths.py` (`UsvfsVoicePaths`, 11) simulate USVFS by patching `Path.resolve()` (a folder answers in mod A, each file below it in mod B) and check: accepted with the flag, refused without it, links refused with it, hashes still enforced, pack must be inside the named pack or the app, data apart from the pack, no escape by `..`; `packaging/mo2-voice-workers.test.mjs` (service side, shared variable names). Docs: `docs/PACKAGING.md` ("The voice workers").
- **Live checks owed (MO2 player or an MO2 test instance):** Runtime and the OmniVoice pack as separate mods plus a Runtime update mod over the Runtime: Pocket starts (V speaks), OmniVoice starts, the service log lists no "missing or linked"/"must remain in the application directory". Open question that code cannot answer: Python's own stat of a file that exists only in a mod folder (the usvfs 0.5.6.1 on Windows 11 24H2 case that Node needed fallbacks for); the workers still use `is_file()`/`stat()` on those files. Also open: `referenceDirectory` is the Runtime mod's REAL `voices` folder, so a reference clip that only an update mod holds would still be missing under MO2 (the profile becomes unavailable, never a crash).

**2026-10-20 (token estimate: "the soft target said 3,306, the server counted 5,262"; branch `fix/token-estimate` from main 73433ecc, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live cloud or Convai turn; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, no Lua, locale or catalog change; one short server run per model on the dev card for the measurements, all stopped; full write-up in `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, "Token estimate and calibration").** Question from the 931d456381ee3ec6 flag below: is the estimator 1.6 times low for the lite model, or is something sent outside the budget?
- **Measured (real llama-server, four models, two tokenizers):** this prompt is **4.2 to 4.5 characters a token on Gemma 4 (standard, Mature good) and on Qwen3.5 (Bonsai 2 lite, Mature lite)**, persona head 4.3 to 4.5, template 44 to 47 tokens for 8 messages. Gemma 4 and the Mature good model count identically, so do Bonsai and the Mature lite model. The estimator (3.6 before anything is learned, 4.1 to 4.3 after one turn) was 25% high at the start and 3 to 8% high after, never low, for English prompts; the tokenizer verification matched the server to 0.3%. Texts: Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian 3.8 to 4.4; slang 3.9 to 4.1; turn-context ids and JSON 2.6; Haitian Creole and Hungarian 3.0 to 3.4; tag strings 3.3; CJK 0.48 to 0.67 of a token a character (counted 1.05: 1.6 times too high); Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai, Hindi 0.27 to 0.47 (counted 0.55); Polish, Czech, Turkish letters of Latin Extended 1.0 to 2.7 tokens a letter (counted as plain: 25% low).
- **Nothing is outside the budget (checked in code and live against the real server):** `fit.messages` is what `chat` sends; `streamChat` adds only `stream_options`, `return_progress`, `stop`, `chat_template_kwargs` (no tokens); no tool, image or vision text reaches the Local route (no `image_url` in `bridge/`); the retry nudges are inside `args.text`; the Mature layer, world rules and action notes are in the fit's arguments (a test pins that the list the tokenizer counted is the list sent). A whole `localRoute` run (real builders, prewarm, 8 exchanges of history, a slow reading faked into the timings, a cut context) for eight turns on Bonsai: the fit's count and the server's differed by 8 to 20 tokens every turn. **The 1.61 of that one report did not reproduce and is not explained**; the other ten fit-line and `[LocalTurn]` pairs in the reports on file agree within 1% (one, an estimate, within 5%).
- **What the report did show: a cliff, fixed.** The soft target of a slow machine is the held head plus 600 to 3,500 new tokens. A prompt cut as far as it can be that still missed the step (turn 2: 3,270 of 3,306, the next turns a few tens of tokens more) was **sent whole**: the old code fitted the hard limit, which cut nothing and logged nothing. That is turns 3 and 4 (5,328 and 5,618 tokens at 200 a second: 20 s instead of 12 s). Reproduced offline (turns 2 to 8 sent at 5,600 tokens), now **4,040 to 4,550**. `PrefillMeter.soft(floor, reach)` returns the smallest larger step that holds the cut prompt, `budgetedChat` fits to it first (log: `(raised soft target)`), and only a prompt that even the largest step cannot hold goes whole as before. A fast machine, or one nobody has measured, is untouched.
- **Calibration (per model, no extra request, no per-token work):** `seedRatio` (4.0 for the shipped families, 3.6 for any other model); `TokenMeter` learns from plain text of every answered turn (a prompt with a Russian line used to teach nothing), and a new **bias** (1 or more: the server's count over what the budget counted for that prompt, tokenizer count when it asked, else the estimate under the ratio learned meanwhile; larger of the last two turns, at most 2.5) multiplies the estimate and the tokenizer's count in the next fits, so the soft and hard limit are met in the server's tokens. A gap of 15% or more logs `The local AI: the server counted N tokens for a prompt this computer counted as M (by the server's tokenizer or by estimate, x times); later prompts are counted x times higher` (three per model); a fit made with a bias says `(counts corrected by x)`. If the report's 1.61 comes back, that line says whether the tokenizer or the estimate was off. Scripts re-measured (CJK 0.72, other 0.5, Latin Extended 2.0); the tokenizer scale clamp 1.6 -> 3.
- **One estimator:** the compact character text aims at 1,900 tokens counted with the model's own ratio (quantised 0.2, kept in 3.8 to 4.6, taken once when a character's text is chosen, so a held character's text never changes under it; without a ratio the old 8,000 characters); its log line counts with it too (it used 3.6, 17% high); the warm-up uses the same ratio as the turn.
- **Tests:** new `bridge/token-estimate.test.mjs` (12 tests) against `bridge/fixtures/token-counts.json` (counts recorded from the real server, no server needed): whole prompts of both tokenizers (never low, at most 15% high), 24 texts, learned ratio, bias and its recovery, bias in the fit, the log, everything sent is counted, the raised target, the compact target. `bridge/prompt-budget.test.mjs`: "sent whole" became "raised to the next step". Full `npm test`: see the result line in the final report.
- **Live check owed (needs a slow machine):** the `(raised soft target)` line instead of a turn with no line and 5,300+ tokens; and, if it recurs, the `the server counted ... for a prompt this computer counted as ...` line.

**2026-10-20 (fourth round of 0.2.4 error reports; branch `fix/reports-024c` from main 1c24c103, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live cloud or Convai turn; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, no Lua, locale or catalog change, no new module).** Reports read: `deliverables/error-reports/` up to 2026-10-20 08:07 UTC.
- **`94bc8efa4ebda288` ("convai: page.evaluate: Target page, context or browser has been closed", one install, 0.2.4): the party plan closed the page a running turn was using. Fixed.** What the player saw: the game's "The conversation service could not reply. Please try again." (no error code, so no extra notice), twice in a row, V's own typed line still spoke. Evidence in the report: (1) `game audioware: problem missing`, so `speech-state.json` says `available: false` for the whole session (`mod/speech.lua`: `available` is false while Audioware is missing) and `audioReady()` is false; (2) the six turns that worked and the two that failed were all `npc-sixth-street-male`, ordinary residents of one profile; the probe log shows the failing turns went to the resident V had **not** just talked to (the one V had talked to is the plan's `partners` entry, one route per profile, `nearby-warm.mjs` `entities`); (3) both failed about 2 s in, with the V line still playing on the other renderer page (so the browser itself was alive). Mechanism: `convai-bridge.mjs` hands a turn's route to the plan (`connections.setRequest(input, turnRoute)`) only `if (canWarm ...)`, and `canWarm` is `audioReady(runtime)`; without it the plan lists the other resident's route, and the bridge's 150 ms poll runs `connections.maintain()`, whose `applyPlan` calls `RealtimeHost.retain()`, which has always closed every pool page that is not in the plan, **busy or not**. The turn's `page.evaluate` then fails with the closed-page error. Reproduced offline with the real `RealtimeHost` and `PartyConnections` (`bridge/realtime-page-recovery.test.mjs`, first test: failed before the fix, passes after). Not the cause: the idle reaper (`releaseIfIdle` needs an empty pool and 5 idle minutes), the audio-heartbeat close (it aborts the turn first, so nothing is reported), memory or a crash (no sign in the log). It also applies to a game that stalls past 5 s (audio "not ready") and to any key the plan does not list.
  - **No recovery existed:** `RealtimeHost.run()` retried only through `recover()` (plan-limit and identity refusals), the pool reused an idle page without looking whether it had closed, and a closed page surfaced as a plain failure.
  - **Fix (`bridge/realtime-host.mjs`, `bridge/transport-pool.mjs`):** (1) the host pins the key of every running turn and microphone lease (`pin()`, `keepKeys()`): `retain()` passes the plan's keys plus the pinned ones to the pool, so a page is swept when its turn is over, not under it (a turn on a page the plan does not list still opens a fresh page each time, as before; it just no longer dies). (2) `run()` asks the same turn once more on a fresh page when the call ends with a closed/crashed/destroyed-context error (`pageGone`), unless the caller aborted or the host closed itself on purpose (a world reset, a key or provider change: that ends as a cancellation, no failure report); one log line `The conversation page closed during a turn; opening it again and asking once more`; a second loss fails the turn as before. A lost browser starts again through `start()`. (3) `TransportPool.acquire` replaces an idle page that is closed instead of reusing it. Tests: `bridge/realtime-page-recovery.test.mjs` (6: the plan case, the microphone lease, the closed idle page, one retry and no third, warm-up retry plus abort and deliberate close never retried, the error classes). Not changed: the bridge still skips the hand-over when audio is not ready (such a turn's page is swept afterwards, one extra connection per turn on an unplanned resident); a retry after the user's text reached Convai can put that line in Convai's history twice (a retried turn is rare and the page was already gone).
- **`fb572ec20560db52` ("omni: Local voice generation timed out", 0.2.3 and 0.2.4, two installs: RTX 4070 Ti with Local AI Mature lite, RTX 4070 SUPER with Mature good, both OmniVoice 32 steps with the Pocket helper beside it, Vulkan Local AI on the same card): cause not proven; GPU pressure is the likely one, no code behaviour changed.** The reports carry the NEXT session's log (reports are sent at the next start), not the failing one. From the probe and report times both installs fail the same way: the first reply of the session is spoken about 26 s after the first typed line (the text, then probably Omni's character preparation), its `synthesize` starts about 120 s before the failure and never answers, while the next typed line (Local AI on the same card, `prompt read` of 3,000+ tokens) is already running; the game's own 75 s result error for that second line follows. 120 s is `VOICE_WORKER_LIMITS.renderMs` (a phrase is 1.3 to 2.6 s on a card with room), so this is a hang or a crawl, not a long text. Same family as the 4080 install of `da69d0ca4938ed07` (Omni preparation timed out with 3.7 GB free). After the timeout `voice-selection` retires the worker, Pocket (the V helper's CPU engine) speaks, Omni is tried again after 45 s, 3 min, 10 min; the reply of the turn that timed out is shown as written text (`audioError`). What was changed: **diagnostics only**. When a generation or preparation runs out of time, `ResidentVoice` reads the worker's Windows graphics-memory counters once (`bridge/gpu-memory.mjs`, up to 4 s, never at startup, not in tests) before ending it, logs `graphics memory of the voice worker after its generation ran out of time: N MiB on the card, M MiB in shared system memory`, and the report's `detail` gets `gpuDedicatedMiB` and `gpuSharedMiB` (two numbers; signature unchanged). The next `fb572` report says whether the worker had spilled. Tests: `bridge/resident-voice.test.mjs` (+2), `bridge/error-reports.test.mjs` (+1), `bridge/voice-selection.test.mjs` (+1). Not done on purpose: a shorter render deadline (a throttled laptop can legitimately take far longer than a card with room; no evidence yet that a spill is the cause, and the Omni worker's normal shared-usage baseline is not measured, so an early "spilled" verdict would risk downgrading healthy players).

Not covered: the lite model loaded with layers on the CPU (2,267 MiB free) stalled twice, each a 60 to 75 s wait, before the cloud took over. **Fixed here:** a model loaded after a step-down in the same session, again with layers on the CPU, steps down at its first stall (`#offloadedAfterStep`, `bridge/local-llm-server.mjs`; test in `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs`, "a model loaded after a step-down with layers on the CPU").

On turn 5 the estimate and the count agree (3,085 against 3,077, nothing cached). So on a slow machine the soft target did not hold for four turns: the estimator under-counted by about 1.6 times, or content outside `buildMessages`' accounting (a note appended after the fit) rode along. **Not found, not changed:** it needs the real prompts (a `[LocalTurn]` line with the message sizes, or a repro with that character on the lite model and a prompt log) to tell the tokenizer ratio from an unaccounted block. **Followed up on `fix/token-estimate` (entry above): the ratio is right (4.2 to 4.5 measured), nothing is outside the budget, turns 3 and 4 were the soft-target cliff (fixed); turn 2's 1.61 is not explained and is logged if it recurs.**

**2026-10-20 (MO2: microphone packs installed as separate mods; branch `fix/mo2-mic-packs` from main cd534f4f, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `bridge/local-stt.mjs` needs a bridge restart, `packaging/runtime/prepare-state.mjs` and `start-service.mjs` are Runtime code (a Runtime update); no player text, locale or catalog change).** The gap left open by `fix/mo2-split-packs`.
- **Read:** `start-service.mjs` `packRootsFor` and `prepare-state.mjs` `installLayout` / `serviceEnvironment`; the bridge's `resolveLocalSttPaths` (`bridge/local-stt.mjs`, used for every pack by `convai-bridge.mjs` `packStts` / `installedPackIds`, so the speech-language plan needs no change). The mic packs unpack into `app/models/stt/<id>`; the bridge looked only in `<project>/models/stt/<id>` (the Runtime mod's real folder) and the optional `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_STT_PACKS` (never set by the service), so a mic pack as its own MO2 mod was invisible and Parakeet / SenseVoice never counted as installed.

With `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_USVFS=1`, `resolveLocalSttPaths` maps each model file with `realPathFor` and takes the real folder that holds the most of the model's files (each candidate folder is asked for all files itself, so a stray file of the same model in a higher-priority mod cannot hide the complete one; tie = folder of the first file); the worker gets that real folder. Not complete in any one folder = `model-missing`. The Runtime's own folder stays the second place looked at; English Moonshine is untouched. Service log: `Mod Organizer 2: voice-input pack models, where each runs from (...)`; the prepare-only summary gets `packs.stt`.

**2026-10-20 (MO2: packs installed as separate mods; branch `fix/mo2-split-packs` from main 251684df, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `packaging/runtime/start-service.mjs` is Runtime code (a Runtime update), `bridge/` needs a bridge restart; no player text, locale or catalog change).** The likely cause of the Nexus report "one model with Mature on, none with Mature off" for a player whose mod manager is not confirmed (MO2 is only a guess; Vortex or a manual install would not do this).
- **The chain, confirmed in the code:** `start-service.mjs` `packRootsFor()` called `usvfsCompat.locate(app/local-ai)`; for a folder that stat cannot see (usvfs 0.5.6.1 on Windows 11 24H2) that is `realpathSync.native`, which maps a folder merged from several MO2 mods to ONE mod's real folder. `installLayout` put it in `layout.localAi`, `serviceEnvironment` set `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_AI` to it, and `detectLocalAiPack`, `detectMaturePack`, `describePackFiles` and the custom-model scanner all read their markers from that single root. The other pack's marker and model were invisible: Mature mod chosen = Mature on shows one model, Mature off says "Only Mature models found" (exactly the report). When stat works on the folder `locate` returned the virtual path and merging worked, so it needs the 24H2 stat gap. Reproduced in `packaging/mo2-split-packs.test.mjs` (first test).
- **Fix:** under usvfs the service now hands the bridge the VIRTUAL `app/local-ai` (stat fallbacks list and read it merged, so every marker and manifest is found whichever mod holds it) and the pack modules map each file a manifest names to its own real place with `realPathFor` (`realpathSync.native` of that file; only when `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_USVFS=1`, identity otherwise: a physical install is byte-for-byte the same, the test deep-equals it). `bridge/local-ai-pack.mjs` (server, tiers, embedding model, Mature marker's model check), `bridge/mature-pack.mjs` (models) and the mod folder of `bridge/custom-models.mjs` use it; the engine processes get real absolute file paths. Omni is NOT affected (one pack, one mod, Python runs from its real root, kept as before).
- **llama-server's DLLs:** the exe and the DLLs it loads must be neighbours in one real folder. If both packs ship `llama/` (they do in the release layout) and USVFS maps the exe from one mod and a DLL from the other, `chooseServer` takes the folder with the most of the DLLs the merged `llama/` lists: the winning exe's folder first, then the real folder of every marker that names a server (a marker file is unique to its pack, so it maps to that pack's mod); a tie goes to the winner. The result says `places.server.complete` and the DLL names left out.
- **Report:** the service log gets `Mod Organizer 2: Local AI pack files, where each really is (...)` (one line per marker, model, the server with its DLL status, the embedding model; `packPlaceLines`), and `describePackFiles` adds `foundIn` (MO2 mod folder name, never a path) per marker, model, models/ file and an `engine` list, which the support report's `localAi.packFiles` carries; a physical install has none of these fields. The Setup check's Lua text is unchanged (no new code). The offline report branch (`offline-report`, not merged) calls `describePackFiles`; it needs `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_AI` (the virtual folder) and `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_USVFS=1` in its environment to show the places.
- **Tests:** `packaging/mo2-split-packs.test.mjs` (12 tests: the old single-root bug, a merged folder from two mods, both orders, three packs, the server in one mod only, DLL split, a physical install deep-equal and without extra fields, `realPathFor`, report labels without paths, a custom model); `packaging/usvfs-runtime.test.mjs` now expects the virtual local-ai root.

- **`0069edffb62cb1a4` (Pocket generation stopped) and `0eb8ec71acd1b7d9` (did not stop its cancelled request), one RTX 5050 laptop with OmniVoice + V's helper Pocket:** two different faults, one consequence (V's helper stayed off for the whole session, 27 lines skipped). (a) Upstream's decoder decodes every queued latent frame in one call (`max_decoder_frames_per_call = 0` in the pinned source), so on a busy machine one chunk can pass the worker's 4 s packet limit; the worker raised "outside its frame limit" and a synthesis failure retires the process. Now a long chunk goes out as ordered packets of at most 1 s (`PACKET_FRAMES`). (b) A V line cancelled before its first sound hit a worker starved of CPU that was still preparing the voice or reading the text (neither can be interrupted); the 2 s deadline killed it. A stream with no sound yet now gets the long wait (`prepareCancelMs` 15 to 30 s), one that is generating keeps 2 s. (c) `VHelperVoice` had no recovery: it is now loaded again after 45 s, 3 min, 10 min (like the companions' Pocket), never while a reply is in flight, no retry for a Windows block, off after the fourth failure; due-checked from the poll and each V line. The 51 s publish-to-lease gap in the same install's slow-turn report is the game starting playback (`published` 13.1 s, `playbackObserved` 64.5 s), not the helper (it was ready about at the publish); not attributed, not changed. **2026-10-20 (Local AI speed like Ollama: free-memory fit and spill detection; branch `perf/local-like-ollama` from main c19694ca, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no cloud or Convai turn; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart and the next Runtime update zip carries two new files).** Full write-up with the Ollama / LM Studio / KoboldCpp comparison, the report table and every measurement: `deliverables/local-speed-ollama-2026-10-20.md`; developer notes in `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` ("Free-memory fit and spill").
- **Root cause of the 0.8 to 5 tokens/s players:** the driver moves part of the model into shared system memory after the load. Reports: RTX 4090 / 4070 SUPER / 5070 with 10 to 11 GB free at the load, the whole model on the card, 0.9 to 5.6 tokens/s for the session (a CPU placement cannot do that on a 4090). **Reproduced** (RTX 4080 Laptop, Silent mode, four other servers over-committing the card): 1,103 MiB of the 3.2 GB server in shared memory (Windows counter "GPU Process Memory > Shared Usage", healthy 80 to 100 MiB) took it from 83 to 3.9 tokens/s and 3,400 to 683 prompt tokens/s. Second finding: `file + 1,200 MiB` overstates Gemma 4 E4B by about 3 GB (per-layer embeddings stay in RAM: 3.3 GB used at 16k), so 4 to 5 GB cards were "offloaded" and the prompt budget assumed 120 tokens/s.
- **Ollama / LM Studio / KoboldCpp:** Ollama's engine is now llama-server with `--fit` (margin 1,024 MiB), a conservative file+KV prediction, min(own accounting, driver free memory), automatic context by VRAM tier (4k under 24 GiB) with retry at 32k then 4k, mmap off on Windows CUDA, 5 min keep-alive, and **no check for a spill after the load**. LM Studio: per-model offload/context/flash attention, `lms load --estimate-only`, a CUDA-only "limit offload to dedicated memory". KoboldCpp: layer guess from file size, blasbatchsize 512, flash attention on. None detects a spill.
- **Changes:** (1) `bridge/local-vram-fit.mjs`: `llama-fit-params` (shipped, 2 s, allocates nothing) projects 16,384 / 8,192 / 8,192 q8_0; the first rung with projection + 512 MiB free loads the whole model; only for the chosen model and Mature models, only when the file-size rule says no room (no probe on a card with room, default choice unchanged); a pinned model whose projection fits is kept. (2) `bridge/gpu-memory.mjs`: one `typeperf` read after a slow reply (< 12 tokens/s, >= 20 pieces) or a stall, at most every 3 min; shared usage beyond a 128 MiB baseline by >= 300 MiB and 10% = spill. (3) Spill reaction: unload, read free memory, reload the same model fitted (margin 1,024 MiB) once per model per session, else step down as before. (4) A model with under 35% of its layers on the card steps down at its first stall (the 8 GB 4060 report: 60 s twice). (5) `reselect()` no longer reloads the 5 GB model when the changed choice would end on the loaded one (error-reports agent's item); the notice is still sent. (6) Diagnostics `engine.fit`, `engine.spill`, `engine.kvType`.
- **Numbers (Balanced unless stated):** footprint Gemma 4 E4B standard 3,144 / 3,008 / 2,940 MiB at 16k / 8k / 4k, Mature good 3,316 / 3,180 / 2,933, lite 1,814 / 1,550 / 1,418; q8_0 saves 135 MiB at 16k and costs 7 to 10% prompt speed, `-ub 256` saves 80 MiB and costs 14%: no cheap knob. Projections are about 340 MiB above use. Before/after, Mature good pinned, ~5 GB free: 8,192 context `-fit on` ("part on the CPU") 4,114 pp / 83.2 tg against 16,384 whole 4,231 / 83.6: **no speed change where llama.cpp's own fit already kept every layer on the card** (the gain is the context, no 120 tokens/s assumption and prompt cuts, one load instead of two). End to end spill with the real server and counters: 6.2 tokens/s (1,073 pp) with 751 MiB shared, reaction 6.5 s, lite then 102.6 tokens/s (3,658 pp) (Silent: 6.2 to 109, 8.8 s). A partial placement shows 76 MiB shared (no false spill).
- **Tests:** `bridge/local-vram-fit.test.mjs` (8), `bridge/gpu-memory.test.mjs` (4), 7 new in `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs`; both new modules added to `packaging/runtime-layout.mjs` and `packaging/release-plan.json` (the bootstrap allowlist test needed them). Full `npm test` before that fix: 7,529 tests, 7,503 pass, 25 skipped, 1 fail (the allowlist test, now fixed: `runtime-bootstrap` and `packaging-plan` pass, 31 of 31). No `development-tools` failure (game closed).
- **Not changed on purpose:** the default model choice (a bigger model on an 8 GB card takes room the game wants: FPS first; the 3,000 MiB reserve was tuned against the overstated need, re-tune after the live check), `-ub`, the cache type on cards with room, the 10-minute idle stop, NVIDIA's sysmem fallback policy (a driver setting). Not measured: `-t` / `--poll` under a busy game for a partial offload.
- **Live check owed (game, 8 to 12 GB NVIDIA card; install all committed `bridge/` files, bridge restart):** (1) Mature good pinned, game in the open world with 4 to 5 GB free: log `fit of ...: projected 3734 MiB`, `model ready ... whole model on the card by the free-memory fit`, no "part on the CPU"; (2) a reply under 12 tokens/s logs `graphics memory of the model server after a slow reply: N MiB on the card, M MiB in shared system memory`; with a spill it reloads fitted or steps down within about 10 s; (3) flip the Local AI model to one that does not fit while Mature good is loaded: no reload, `it stays loaded`, the usual notice.

**2026-10-20 (compact character text on measured-slow machines; branch `feat/compact-persona-slow` from main 3d8ace77, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live or Convai turn; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart).** The owner approved "shorter character text on slow PCs only" (owner decision 3). Local AI only (our llama-server and a server the player runs through Local AI); a fast machine's prompt is unchanged byte for byte.
- **Slow is measured:** `PrefillMeter.compact` (`bridge/prompt-budget.mjs`): two prompt-read readings in a row under 600 tokens a second (or one stalled request) switch it on, two in a row at 1,000 or more switch it off, between keeps the state; the CPU-offload prior is not a measurement; a model loaded again starts from the state before. Thresholds from the 0.2.4 reports (36 to 420 tokens a second when slow) and the dev card (about 5,000).
- **What it does:** `bridge/compact-persona.mjs` cuts the persona by section to a head of about 8,000 characters (1,900 tokens): keeps the opening paragraph, voice, relationships (with the line about V), background, current-save and limits notes, the closing style paragraph, two example lines; drops the public-topic lore with its Scope lines, the appearance, extra examples. The output rules, Mature or guard layer, world rules, the character's own rules and facts are never cut (they shrink the persona's room, floor 2,600 characters). Judy 3,570 to 1,910 tokens, Jackie 3,330 to 1,600, Judy with Mature 4,185 to 2,070; every named character 1,300 to 2,200 across the roster (est. at 4.2 characters a token). Pure and deterministic: the same text every turn, so the prefix cache holds.
- **When:** chosen at a character's first turn and kept while the server holds that character (a machine that turns slow mid-talk keeps that talk's cached prompt; the next character starts compact); the warm-up reads the same text (`route.shapePersona`). One log line when it starts, one per cut character, one when it ends. `localRoute` `shape` hook (3rd argument `base` added to `budgetedChat`'s call) and a hook in `TextProviderHost#prewarm`; `local-llm-server.mjs` not touched.
- **Not measured:** the game was open (and a `llama-bench` of someone else was running), so no GPU benchmark; arithmetic from the reports' rates is in `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` (Judy first turn at 100 tokens a second: 36 s to 19 s; at 300: 12 s to 6 s). The first character of a never-measured session still reads the whole text (and a warm-up before any turn too): a prior from the CPU-offload flag or from a warm-up's timings would cover it, left out because the owner asked for measured speed (follow-up if the reports still show it; the warm-up's `timings` are in the non-streaming reply but `local-llm-server.mjs` is another agent's file now).
- **Tests:** `bridge/compact-persona.test.mjs` (7: the cut and its keeps, the Mature/world-rule room, the whole roster, hysteresis, choice kept per character, fast machine byte for byte over five turns, slow machine within budget and the same head three turns running, warm-up on the same text); `prompt-budget`, `text-provider-host`, `local-*` suites green. **Live check owed** (slow or throttled machine): talk to one character, then a second; the log shows `compact character text (this computer reads about N tokens a second)` before the second one's first turn, its `[LocalTurn]` line shows about 1,600 fewer `new` tokens, the reply still sounds like them, later turns have `cached` near the whole prompt; on a fast machine the log shows nothing about it. Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` "Compact character text on slow machines". New module added to the Runtime allowlist (`packaging/runtime-layout.mjs`, `packaging/release-plan.json`; the next Runtime update carries `bridge/compact-persona.mjs`). Full `npm test`: only the expected "Close the game first" failure (native install, game running) after that allowlist fix.
**2026-10-20 (CUDA vs Vulkan llama-server benchmark; branch `feat/cuda-llama` from main, TODO entry only, no code changed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, game not touched by the agent):** the bundled Vulkan server is llama.cpp b11560 (commit b13a93a3d); the official `ggml-org/llama.cpp` b11560 Windows CUDA 12.4 build (265 MB) and cudart zip (391 MB) were downloaded (published SHA-256 matched) to `local-ai/dl-llama-cuda-b11560/` and benchmarked on the RTX 4080 Laptop against it with our flags (`-fa 1 -ub 512`, 4096-token prompt, 128 generated, same Gemma 4 E4B standard, Bonsai lite and Mature good files). **Verdict: CUDA is not clearly faster, so nothing is shipped and no selection code was written.** Idle card: CUDA reads the prompt 1.15-1.23x faster, generates 0.90-1.02x. Game at the menu: 1.19-1.38x prompt, generation about equal (one partial-offload reading 1.32x). Game in the open world (RT medium, 1080p): prompt 0.94-1.19x, generation 0.88-1.05x at full offload (CUDA slower on both Gemma models), partial offload `-ngl 24` 1.17x/1.27x on standard and about equal on Mature; real-server time to first token for a 2,500-token prompt is the same (about 1.5-1.7 s), generation 15-25% slower on CUDA; CUDA also uses 5-10% more video memory. The 0.8-5 tokens/s players are not explained by the backend (our in-world rate is 30+ on the same model class): likely memory spilling into shared memory or the game holding the card; the support reports' layer count, context and free memory are the next thing to look at. Packaging, if ever wanted: the CUDA server folder is 1.14 GB (ggml-cuda 572 MB, cublasLt 474 MB, cublas 100 MB), 656 MB to download, so a separate NVIDIA add-on, not the Local AI pack. Full write-up: `deliverables/cuda-vs-vulkan-2026-10-20.md`. Owner decisions: delete the old broken `local-ai/dl-llama-cuda/cuda.zip` (56.9 MB, not a valid archive), and `local-ai/dl-llama-cuda-b11560/` (about 1.8 GB) when no longer needed.
**2026-10-20 (seated driving for the companion drive action; branch `feat/seated-drive` from main 3d8ace77, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched; `mod/` needs install of all committed Lua plus a CET reload, `bridge/` a bridge restart; no redscript changed, so no reds compile was needed):**
- **What it does:** "drive me", "you drive", "swap seats", "take over" now also work when V already sits in their own stopped car (driver or passenger) with a map destination set. The offer carries `seated: 'driver' | 'passenger'` and reaches Convai's action context and the Mistral/Local/Custom text route. Detail and the evidence in `docs/COMPANION_CHAUFFEUR.md`, "Seated drive".
- **API choice (fallback, on purpose):** no forced swap. The installed scripts show V's native `switchSeats` state needs the target seat free and sends a front passenger straight back to the empty driver seat after 0.2 s; NPCs have no animated seat switch; the instant `MountingFacility.Mount` request the game uses bypasses the player state machine. So: companion steps out (`AIUnmountCommand` from this car), V leaves the driver seat with the normal exit (asked through the character's reply and the existing "Step out of the driver seat so your companion can get in." notice), companion boards the driver seat (`AIMountCommand`, the existing driver boarding), V boards a passenger seat, the existing trip departs. The mod never moves V.
- **Cases:** V driver + companion in a passenger seat (step out, V steps out, drive); V driver + companion outside (V steps out, then the on-foot boarding); V passenger + companion already driver (straight to departure); V passenger + companion in another seat or outside (companion steps out and takes the wheel). Refused as before: no waypoint, V in a vehicle that is not their own car (`player-driving` / `player-seated`, now only for that), car moving, combat, companion in another vehicle or still boarding the party car (`transport-busy`).
- **Safety:** no car driverless (companion is the driver before any command), V never stuck outside by the mod, 45 s for V to leave the driver seat counted only after the companion is out, exit attempts bounded (3, 25 s), combat/timeout/foreign AutoDrive before the driver seat hands the party back to the ordinary boarding (`yieldToPlayer`), no per-frame work.
- **Code:** `mod/companion-chauffeur.lua` (offer, queue adopts the fleet's V car and the companion's seat record, new phase `exiting-passenger`, yield rule, probe.log stages `vehicle-seated-drive`), `mod/companion-vehicles.lua` (`stepOutOfSeat`), `mod/companion-chauffeur-native.lua` (car = the exact owned vehicle V sits in), `mod/manager-ui.lua` (status rows), `bridge/companion-actions.mjs` + `bridge/text-actions.mjs` (offer key, context/menu text), `bridge/text-action-words.mjs` (seated stems in 15 languages, English plain requests). `localization/en.json` regenerated (reference line numbers only); no new UI strings, locales untouched.
- **Tests:** `bridge/companion-chauffeur.test.mjs` (+10 seated tests with the real fleet), `bridge/companion-chauffeur-native.test.mjs` (+1), new `bridge/seated-drive-actions.test.mjs` (5).
- **Live check list (the lead drives; Judy in the party, V's own car stopped, a map pin set; read probe.log, `Companion recovery vehicle-seated-drive` and `vehicle-exit` lines):**
  1. V in the driver seat, Judy in the front passenger seat: type "you drive". Judy's reply tells V to step out. Log: `stage=queued mode=driver vSeat=seat_front_left companionSeat=seat_front_right first=exiting-passenger seat=seat_front_right`, then `vehicle-exit decision=seated-drive-step-out seat=seat_front_right attempt=1`. Judy gets out within about 5 s (watch: does the exit animation run from a car V is sitting in, and does the car stay put?).
  2. Still in the driver seat: log `stage=boarding-driver` then `stage=waiting-for-driver-seat`; the notice "Step out of the driver seat so your companion can get in." shows. Step out with the normal exit key: Judy walks round and sits in the driver seat (`stage=waiting-for-player`); V never ends outside with a driverless car.
  3. Board the front passenger seat yourself: `waiting-for-party`, `starting`, `driving`; she drives to the pin; arrival as in the on-foot trip. Check the car never moves before you sit.
  4. Repeat 1, but stay in the driver seat 45+ s after Judy is out: the trip cancels, Judy gets back in the car (ordinary boarding), nothing was driven, `stage=yielded`.
  5. V in the back seat (through the rear door) with Judy in front: "swap seats". Log `mode=passenger vSeat=seat_back_left ... first=exiting-passenger`; Judy steps out, takes the driver seat, V stays seated, departure with `enableSeat` = your seat (no V movement at all).
  6. Judy outside the car (not yet boarded) while V sits in the driver seat: "take over". `first=releasing`, V asked to step out, then as 2-3.
  7. No pin set, V seated: "you drive". Text route: Judy says she needs a destination; Convai: no action. Nothing moves, no `queued` line.
  8. Start a fight while Judy is stepping out (1 above): trip ends, `stage=yielded`, Judy rides again, V unmoved.
  9. V in a vehicle that is not theirs (Delamain cab, a stolen car): "you drive" does nothing.
  10. Regression, V on foot beside the car: "drive me" works as before (no `queued mode=` line, boarding as in the 2026-10-03 check). Request words: "you drive", "swap seats", "take over", "your turn to drive", and one non-English line ("Du fährst", "Tu conduis").
  11. FPS unchanged in the car (no per-frame work added).
  Unproven in the game and worth watching: `GetMountingInfoSingleWithObjects` for V reporting `seat_front_left` while driving; the unmount of a companion while V sits in the same car; whether an exit from a seat while V is in the driver seat blocks on the exit workspot (log `waiting-for-native-exit`).

**2026-10-20 (the 0.2.4 error reports; branch `fix/reports-024` from main 7f352b92, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, `mod/setup-check.lua` and the locales need a CET reload):**
- **`44b553fc86440f70` (8919 tokens against 8192), cause and fix:** our own server (Mature good, 4070 SUPER, part on the CPU). The speed-based soft target of 0.2.3 (persona or held prefix + allowance) can exceed the context for a long persona (9,315 in 8,192); `budgetedChat` fitted to it, nothing was cut, the server refused, and the retry was fitted to the same target and refused again. Now a soft target is used only when its limit is below the context's own (`fitLimit`); a refused prompt is retried once, cut to the server's count. Tests in `bridge/prompt-budget.test.mjs` fail without the fix.
