**2026-10-20 (two error signatures from 0.2.3 Vortex installs: `26d9eb59191a945a` and `f309bd3f807c9dd0` Pocket source differs, `9ef0b3204aaef8fa` launcher-not-configured; branch `fix/vortex-pocket-launcher` from main, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart; the launcher DLL needs a rebuild and a game restart; `mod/setup-check.lua` and the 15 locales need a CET reload).**
- **Pocket (`26d9eb59191a945a`, `f309bd3f807c9dd0`), cause:** both reports are one install (Vortex, RX 6600, Convai text + Pocket voice) that went 0.2.1 -> 0.2.2 -> 0.2.3 in place; the worker failed within 0.5 s on every start with "Pocket source differs from the pinned official revision". The old check hashed every file under `app/pocket-tts` (minus a short ignore list), so any file beside the pinned 140 failed it, and the report could not say which. The two earlier rounds ignored the Vortex marker and Explorer files; what else sat in that folder is not in the report (candidates: a `.vortex_backup`, a leftover from an older Runtime, a file added by a scanner). It cannot be told from the data, so the check no longer depends on it.
- **Pocket, fix:** `bridge/pocket_voice_runtime.py` now has `SOURCE_FILES` (path -> SHA-256 of the 140 files of the pinned revision; `digest_manifest()` equals `SOURCE_SHA256`) and `verify_source`. Only listed files are looked at, so extras (markers, backups, deployment files, `__pycache__`, leftovers, scanner notes) are ignored by design. A listed file under `pocket_tts/` or any `.py` that is missing, changed or a link fails, and the error names the first three ("pocket_tts/x.py changed, y.py missing, +2 more", relative paths only; the worker's fatal reason is 300 characters now, was 160, so the bridge log and the error report carry the names). A pinned README, test, notebook or picture that differs does not fail; the worker logs one line naming them. A text file whose line endings were converted to CRLF counts as unchanged. `validate_config` keeps a `source_hasher` test seam.
- **Pocket, build:** no new file for the Runtime. The list lives inside `bridge/pocket_voice_runtime.py`, already a `bridgeWorkers` file of the Runtime. `packaging/build-release.mjs` now stops when the files it ships under `app/pocket-tts` are not exactly that list (`packaging/lib/pocket-source-list.mjs`; `packaging/pocket-source-list.test.mjs` also ties the list to `release.config.json`'s `treeSha256`). Whatever patches the 0.2 base must carry `app/pocket-tts` unchanged (same 140 files) and ship the new `app/bridge/pocket_voice_runtime.py` and `pocket-voice-worker.py` (and `pocket-voice.mjs`, the reason cap).
- **Launcher (`9ef0b3204aaef8fa`), what it means:** `launcher-not-configured` is published by the native launcher (`native/autostart/CyberpunkConvaiLauncher.c`) when `red4ext/plugins/AiNpcCyberpunkMod/launcher.ini` is not there (or an argument in it is too long). The launcher DLL was there, `launcher.ini` was not. The report's own launcher log (a later session, game folder on Steam, Vortex) shows the launcher starting the service fine, so the file was missing in the first session and present in the next; that log is overwritten each start, so what removed it cannot be seen. The Runtime holds `launcher.ini` only in the full Runtime zip; the update zip leaves unchanged files out, and Vortex can leave a plugin folder with the DLL and no ini (a partial update, a purge, a deployment that missed it).
- **Launcher, fix:** `launcher.ini` is optional now (launcher 1.0.1). Missing, or present with no `program`, the launcher starts the Runtime exactly as the shipped file says (`DEFAULT_*` in the C file, held equal to `packaging/lib/launcher-ini.mjs` by a test); `enabled=0` still turns it off; no node there still publishes `launcher-program-missing`. The log says "using the built-in settings". Needs the new `CyberpunkConvai.dll` (built from `native/autostart/CyberpunkConvaiLauncher.c`, `scripts/Build-AutostartPlugin.ps1`) in the Runtime and in the update zip (the DLL changes, so the update builder carries it).
- **Player text:** an older launcher's `launcher-not-configured` now has its own sentence in the Help page's Conversation service row (names `launcher.ini` and the folder; translated in all 15 `mod/locales/*.lua`; `Extract-UiCatalog.mjs --check` passes). PLAYER_README "What's new in 0.2.4" gained two bullets (not copied into `docs/NEXUS_PAGE.md`: tell the owner).
- **Tests:** `scripts/test_pocket_voice_runtime.py` (8 new: manifest = pinned digest, ignored extras incl. `__pycache__` and a leftover, changed/missing `.py` and package file named, "+N more", docs-only differences note, CRLF, link, wrong manifest, end to end through `validate_config`); `packaging/pocket-source-list.test.mjs` (2); `bridge/autostart-plugin.test.mjs` (3 new against the real built DLL: built-in settings with no ini and with an ini without a program, missing node, enabled=0; plus the C defaults equal the shipped ini); `bridge/setup-check-lua.test.mjs` (the new sentence).
- **Player workaround on 0.2.3:** Pocket: delete the whole `red4ext/plugins/AiNpcCyberpunkMod/app/pocket-tts` folder (and its copy in a Vortex staging folder if the Runtime was installed as a mod), then extract the 0.2.3 Runtime zip over the game folder by hand so the folder comes back with exactly the pinned files; the real fix is the new `pocket_voice_runtime.py`. Launcher: extract the full 0.2.3 Runtime zip over the game folder by hand (not as a Vortex mod) so `red4ext/plugins/AiNpcCyberpunkMod/launcher.ini` is back, then restart the game.
- **Test results:** `npm test` (436 files) exit 0 on this branch (with a `node_modules` junction, removed again); `python -B scripts/test_pocket_voice_runtime.py` 48 tests OK; `node scripts/Extract-UiCatalog.mjs --check` clean; `bridge/autostart-plugin.test.mjs` 8 of 8 against the DLL built here (SHA-256 `1485f5d3ff751c059c3b223862800856428c0738f3806be25d75448e218d2686`, reproducible with `/Brepro`). Nothing was run against a real Vortex install.

**2026-10-20 (a player's own model server, two error signatures from one 0.2.3 player: `a9493da8945aae6e` thinking-only, `74856599d4439f90` prompt longer than the loaded context; branch `fix/thinking-only-own-server` from main, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart; `mod/` Lua (init.lua, notices.lua, phone-chat.lua, 15 locales) needs a CET reload).** Setup of both reports: Local AI on a server the player runs on the home network (LM Studio style, `manifest.custom.json` `endpoint` entry, model label "Laptop AI", context 8192).
- **Thinking-only (`a9493da8945aae6e`), cause:** `reasoningSteps` (bridge/reasoning.mjs) asks a server to skip thinking only when the model id looks like a reasoning model, and only on the `custom` provider. This is the `local` route over an external server, which never sent any such field, so a model with an unlisted name thought until the 160-piece stop (about 4.8 s, `noRetry`), on every turn.
- **Thinking-only, fix:** `noThinkingFields` (reasoning.mjs): a home server gets `reasoning_effort: 'none'`, `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` and `think: false`; another host `reasoning_effort: 'low'` plus the template switch; OpenRouter and DeepSeek nothing new (they are asked on every request). `streamChat` (mistral-client.mjs, new `noThinking`): a reply that was only thinking is asked again once, at once (`attempt--`, the turn's `deadlineAt` and `minAttemptMs` still hold), with those fields; `adapt.thinks` remembers the endpoint for the session (per address and model, in memory: `localRoute` and `customRoute` keep one adaptation each), so later turns send them from the start; a server that refuses one by name loses just that one (`adapt.noThinkDropped`, `namedNoThinkFields`, `REASONING_FIELD` now also names `think` and `chat_template_kwargs`). Only for `external` servers and custom endpoints: the packaged models never think and are never sent them (`leaseBody` unchanged). The custom provider's existing retry with more room (`retryBudget`) and the new fields are one retry, not two. A second thinking-only reply fails with `...even when asked not to think` which `errorCodeFor` turns into the new notice `local-thinking` ("Your model only thought and didn't answer. Turn thinking off for it in your model server, or pick a non-thinking model."); the custom provider keeps `custom-reasoning`. Both new codes are in `OWN_DOING` (bridge/error-events.mjs): the fix is in the player's server, not a fault to report. Thinking text is never spoken (nothing changed there).
- **Context (`74856599d4439f90`), cause:** LM Studio wraps llama.cpp's `exceed_context_size_error` inside its own error and answers 500 or 502 ("Engine protocol predict request returned 400: ..."). `mapFailure` read overflow only on status 400, so it became `network` + `slow`, the route's `failure()` called `externalLost()` and the supervisor logged "stopped answering" and dropped the server, and nothing was fitted again. The server's loaded context was also smaller than the reported 8192.
- **Context, fix:** `contextRefusal` (mistral-client.mjs) reads a refusal for length by its words at any of 400, 413, 422 and 5xx (llama.cpp `n_ctx` and `n_prompt_tokens`, `request (N tokens) ... (M tokens)`, OpenAI-style "maximum context length is M tokens", LM Studio's "context length of only M tokens"); it is kind `request` with `overflow`, so nothing marks the server lost. `budgetedChat` (prompt-budget.mjs, new `server` flag in `budget()` and `learn` hook): the named context replaces the reported one, a refusal that names none halves the assumed one (never below `MIN_SERVER_CONTEXT` 2048), `LocalLlmServer.learnContext` keeps it per address and model for the session and `handle().contextSize` uses it; the prompt is fitted again (persona shortened when `lastResort`) and sent once; no number from the error no longer makes the budget NaN. The persona prewarm (`#complete` now reads a refusal's words) learns the same and is never counted as down. A prompt that still does not fit, or a second refusal, on such a server is a `PromptTooLarge` with `server: true` and the new notice `local-context` ("Your model server's context is too small for this character. Raise the context length in your server (8192 or more)."). Our own llama-server keeps `local-failed`.
- **Player text:** two new strings in `mod/init.lua` (also the phone status table in `mod/phone-chat.lua`, notices `local-thinking` and `local-context` in `mod/notices.lua`, repeat 30 s), translated in all 15 `mod/locales/*.lua` (Haiku), `node scripts/Extract-UiCatalog.mjs` and `--check` clean. Docs: NOTIFICATIONS.md (two rows), LOCAL_AI.md (own server: thinking, context), CUSTOM_PROVIDER.md (3b).
- **Tests:** new `bridge/own-server-thinking-context.test.mjs` (18 tests: the retry and its fields, the per-endpoint memory, a second thinking-only reply, a field refused by name, the time budget, the custom provider's single retry, packaged models untouched; LM Studio's 500/502 as an overflow, named and unnamed context, the floor, still-too-small, end to end on a scripted server through `TextProviderHost`, the prewarm). Full `npm test` result in the commit report.
- **Live check for the user, when convenient (nothing was tested against a real LM Studio):** with a thinking model of an unlisted name on a home server, the first turn should take about one extra thinking-stop (a few seconds) and answer; the next turns answer in one request. A server with less context loaded than it reports (LM Studio's default 4096) should answer after one learned step, with the log line "prompts are fitted to N tokens from now on".

**2026-10-20 (slow-turn reports and a logging audit; branch `feat/slow-turn-reports` from main, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched, backend NOT deployed (no backend change); `bridge/` needs a bridge restart and the Runtime update zip, `mod/init.lua` and the locales a CET reload).** Players say replies get slower over a session (Local AI from 2 to 3 s to a minute or two); reports held only the tail of the logs, so the early turns were gone.
- **New report kind `slow-turn`** (`bridge/slow-turns.mjs`, docs/ERROR_REPORTS.md "Slow replies"). The stage clock already times every turn; each finished turn that reached its first sound is judged once (a few array writes, no file read, nothing per frame or per chunk). Fires when 3 of the last 5 turns took more than 15 s from the bridge reading the request to the first sound, or any turn took more than 45 s (`SLOW_TURNS`, constants). One per bridge run, then the usual one per kind per UTC day, five a day, and the Privacy setting. Left out of the trigger: a failed turn (`turn-failed` has it), a turn the game paused during (the playback lease's `paused`, new `onPaused`), the first turn after Local AI loaded its model (slow by nature; kept in the history). A focused or unfocused window is not known to the bridge. The report's `slow` section (rebuilt by `cleanSlow`: numbers and fixed names only): why it fired, turns and minutes in, provider, voice, free video memory (what the local server saw at its last start, no new probe), background connection counts, the sound times of the last turns, and for the first 3 turns and the slow ones the time of every stage, model, prompt tokens (new and cached) and event-loop stalls. Plus the usual choices and log tail. Never any text.
- **Backend: no deploy.** `auth-backend/api/_lib/errors.js` accepts any kind that matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` and any `report` object within 64 KB; the new kind goes through unchanged (tested against the real handler). `scripts/Fetch-ErrorReports.mjs` INDEX gains a "By kind" line and a table of first sound for the first turns against the slow ones.
- **Player text.** The in-game Privacy help gained one sentence (translated in all 15 locales, `Extract-UiCatalog --check` passes) and the Nexus "Error reports" FAQ says slow-reply timings are sent. README's error-report paragraph not changed (it lists the kinds of content, not each trigger).
- **Logging audit, fixed.** (1) The bridge's polls (`pollMicrophone` 150 ms, preparation 150 ms, look-ahead 60 ms, settings, phone, memory, support, setup, paid tier, editor, the 50 ms request tick) logged every failure on every tick; they now go through `repeatLimiter` (`bridge/repeat-log.mjs`): once per cause, then once a minute with a count. (2) `bridge.stdout.log` / `bridge.stderr.log` were rotated only when the supervisor started: now cut back to their last 3 MB when over 6 MB (every 5 minutes, in the supervisor, `bridge/log-cap.mjs`); the service log to 500 KB at 1 MB. (3) A status file that cannot be written logged every 5 s: once now. (4) `probe.log` and `mcm.log` (Lua) were uncapped (probe.log 539 KB in 4 days on the dev machine): cut to their last quarter at each load when over 1 MB / 256 KB, in place, before the native core takes over io; the reporter then skips the older sessions' lines in the cut file (`since`). (5) `last-input.json`, `group-prefetch.json`, `reaction-lease.json`: the JSON is encoded before the file is opened, so an encoder that raises cannot leave the turn request emptied with the handle open. (6) The probe.log force-flush keyword test matched `error=false` / `failed:0` (89+ lines, a CET `io.open` of 1 to 3 ms each when the native plugin is off): harmless lines wait for the batch. (7) The latency record (`bridge-latency.json`, 6 to 8 whole-file replacements a turn) shares a write that has not started: at most one running and one waiting. (8) The report queue's `sent.json` and queue `.tmp` files left by a write that was cut short are removed (the queue itself was already bounded at 20, a week, one send per 15 minutes after a failure, three failures stop it). (9) pydub's "Couldn't find ffmpeg" RuntimeWarning (13 of 82 reports) is silenced for the OmniVoice worker only.
- **Checked and fine.** Per-turn and per-chunk bridge writes are async and queued (`atomic`), none synchronous on the turn path (the crash capture's one sync write runs as the process ends); `voice-routing.log` trimmed to 500 lines in batches; `launcher.log` is created fresh each game start; `movement-trace` is 2 MiB per file, dev mode only; `perf-probe.json` 150 windows, dev mode only; `error-events.json` about 6 KB; Lua's `convaiLogFile` batches (1 s, 64 lines, 8 KB) and `convaiLogOnce` caps 64 keys; `mod/error-reports.lua` writes only on events inside `pcall`; the reporter runs in the supervisor process (never the game thread or a turn), reads log tails async, spawns `reg.exe` once for the graphics card (5 s timeout, cached), backs off 15 minutes after a failure and stops after three; a failing log write (full disk, locked file) is swallowed by design in the supervisor log, the recorder and `#save`.
- **Not changed, for the owner.** Per-frame `onUpdate` calls without `pcall` in `mod/init.lua` (`companions.beginSpatialFrame`, `ui.update`, `companions.update`, `updateGroup`, `updateGaze`, `microphone.update`): no Lua error appears in any report or log, CET catches a raise per call and the reporter would see it as `lua-error`, and a pcall on each adds per-frame cost; `continuous-control.json` is rewritten every 150 ms while speech plays when the native plugin is absent (by design); dev-only logs without a cap (`gesture-probe.log`, `face-test.log`; `perf-probe.lua` rewrites its whole history every 10 s) are not shipped; the speech state file is replaced at the poll rate during playback (protocol, not logging).

**2026-10-20 (Local AI: "fine at first, then 1 to 2 minutes after typing, growing"; branch `fix/localai-growing-delay` from main bcde8de1, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, nothing in `mod/`, no new player text).** One Nexus player (version unknown, 0.2.2 or 0.2.3): 2 to 3 s per reply at first, then 1 to 2 minutes that keep growing; they guess memory piling up. Findings, in the order of the six suspects (full text and evidence in `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, "The single slot"):
- **1 Queue pile-up on one slot: held, in one place.** The llama-server has one slot (`-np 1`). The summary of older talk (one per 8 exchanges rolled out of the history, so it starts only after the first 16 exchanges, which is why the first minutes are fast) was sent with no cancel path and as soon as the bridge's gate opened (at once after a slow turn); a typed line waited behind it (up to its 40 s). Memory extraction was already stopped by a turn, the summary was not. The 0.2.2 error reports show the wait: `no response` after 60 s with no headers, and headers after 25 and 38 s. Everything else is bounded: one `active` request in the bridge (the next aborts it, the game cancels automatic reactions when V acts), one look-ahead, one warm-up, nearby characters get no persona warm-up, add-on remarks are paced, stock lines are Mistral only.
- **2 Prompt growth: not a cause.** Every part is capped (history 11 exchanges of 1,000 characters, summary 1,400, recalled memories 4 records and 1,200 characters, game dialogue 14 lines in the last message, world facts 12,000 characters, per-character files never injected whole). In the reports prompts run 3,000 to 8,300 tokens, a Jackie talk 6,600 to 8,300 over six turns, no steady growth.
- **3 Broken prefix cache: held, twice.** (a) A persona warm-up (the composer asks for one every time it opens) for the character the slot already holds read the bare persona and left the slot with only that; Gemma 4 and Qwen3.5 resume only from checkpoints, so the next turn read the whole world block again (reports: `cached` fixed at 2,350 while about 3,000 new tokens were read, and `0 cached` on six turns of one Jackie talk). (b) The history window dropped its oldest exchange on every turn from the ninth turn on, so the first history message changed every turn and the whole history (800 to 1,000 tokens) was read again each turn; this starts at the ninth turn on any machine. Round 1's move of the world facts stays.
- **4 Memory store or embedder cost: ruled out.** Retrieval is one embedding call with a 400 ms limit and a flat scan of at most 600 records; extraction is background and stopped by a turn.
- **5 Video memory pressure: interacts, unchanged.** Step-down (two stalls) is as it was. A wait behind our own summary was one of the stalls it could count; that wait no longer happens. Not proved as this player's cause: no report with their numbers exists.
- **6 Leaks: none found.** Every lease is released in `finally`, every timer is unref'd or cleared, the request tables are bounded. A stopped request is aborted through its signal.
- **Fixes (all with tests).** `LocalLlmServer`: `begin({background, cancel})`, `preempt` stops every background request (summary) besides a warm-up of another character, `backgroundRefusal` (no background work while a turn is served, within 10 s after one, or while other background work runs), `noteSlot` and the warm-up skip (a turn in flight, or the slot already holds that persona; tied to the load), `diagnostics().queue` (`stopped`, `refused`, `warmSkipped`). `TextProviderHost`: summaries carry a signal and stop when a turn starts, a busy summary asks again in 10 s, a busy extraction sets `retryLater` (the memory store asks again at its 10 s gate interval instead of the doubling 60 s backoff). `MEMORY_LIMITS.slide` (3): the history is cut back to 8 in one step once it has grown to 11, so its start holds for four turns (`LIMITS.turns` is 11 in the prompt builder, one line; kept minimal for the world-rules branch). **One line per turn, always:** `[LocalTurn] ok: first word ..., prompt N new + M cached tokens, took ... | waited W ms before sending, behind K other requests` (first turn after a load, slow turns and failures keep the long form; `diagnostics().lastTurn` has `waitedMs` and `behind`). Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, `docs/MISTRAL.md` (history size).
- **Tests.** New `bridge/local-queue.test.mjs` (8: arbitration, warm-up skip, route lease, host stops a summary for a turn, server stops one the host does not know, busy retry, the per-turn line, the history window keeps the whole prefix on 3 turns of 4); `bridge/memory-store.test.mjs` (the window, the extraction put off; two older tests made independent of the window size), `bridge/mistral-memory.test.mjs`, `bridge/mistral-prompt.test.mjs`, `bridge/local-turn-diagnostics.test.mjs` (the line; one test says the warm-up of the same persona is only waited for when the slot does not hold it).
- **Live checks owed (need the game and Local AI):** (1) Talk to one companion for 20 turns on Local AI: no turn waits for a summary (the log has `summary put off` or none, and each `[LocalTurn]` line shows `waited` near 0 and `behind 0`); `cached` should be most of `prompt` on turns after the first of each character. (2) Open the composer twice for the same companion between two turns: the log must not show a second warm-up read (`cached` stays high on the next turn). (3) Read a report from a machine with the slow-prompt problem: the lines say whether the wait is in `waited` (queue) or in the prompt (`new` large, `cached` small) or in the model (a long first word with little to read).
- **Player line (for the user to send):** "found a few things that stack up as a talk goes on: a background summary could sit in front of your typed line, and opening the chat box kept making the model re-read the character from scratch. fixed in the next version, and every reply now logs how long it waited, so if it still crawls Generate report will show where."

**2026-10-20 (Local AI on 8 GB cards: stalled turns step down; branch `fix/localai-small-card-stepdown` from main f6e8e34d, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart, `mod/init.lua`, `mod/notices.lua` and the locales a CET reload).** Two 0.2.3 reports (`d85a5d82c0f335ce`, `a6eb76b5657ab3ab`): an RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB with `mature:good` (5,088 MiB, context 16,384, Vulkan) loaded with 7,174 MiB free, then persona warm-ups got no answer in 60 s, a turn had no response, and the next was stuck at 3,071 of 5,472 tokens. The 0.2.2 reports with the same signatures are on 8 to 12 GB cards.
- **Why the Nexus promise ("steps down by itself: standard to lite, then lite to cloud text") did not hold.** The only step-down was at load: `chooseLocalModel` takes the largest model that fits the free graphics memory at that moment, and a model that does not start is replaced. Nothing looked at turns afterwards: a stalled turn only went to Mistral for that one turn when a key was saved (`local-turn-fallback`), or failed `local-failed`. Free memory was never read at turn time. The Mature family was covered at load only (good then lite, never a censored model) and never stepped on failures.
- **Fix.** `LocalLlmServer` counts stalls (a turn failing with `slow` and reason `no-response` / `prefill-stalled` / `no-first-token` / `stalled`, or a persona warm-up with no answer in its wait; an answered turn or a new load clears the count). Two stalls step down: the model goes into an in-memory set for the session, the server is stopped (memory back to the game), and the next start chooses without it: standard to lite, Mature good to Mature lite, never across the Mature line, never for a custom model or a server. With no smaller model installed, or none that fits the free memory then, the server fails `low-memory` and the existing cloud fallback takes the text. The saved pin is never written; `reset()` (choosing Local AI again) and a changed choice try everything again. One new notice `local-stepdown`: "Local AI switched to {model}: the game is using most of your graphics memory." or, for the cloud step, "Local AI was too slow because the game is using most of your graphics memory, so a cloud provider is used." (15 locales, `localization/en.json` regenerated; `Extract-UiCatalog --check` clean). Log lines `[local] ... stalled (n of 2)` and `[local] stepping down from ...` (with one `nvidia-smi` free-memory reading); `diagnostics().steppedDown` for the support report. Work happens only on those failures, nothing per frame or per turn.
- **Load-time pre-check.** On a card of 8,704 MiB or less the default rule (no pin; the settings page's default too) keeps 3,000 MiB of the card for the game: a model must fit total minus 3,000 or the next smaller one is taken (the old rule when none passes). So an 8 GB card's default is the lite model; a pinned model is loaded as chosen and can still step down. 10 GB and larger cards are unchanged.
- **Tests.** `bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs` (5 new: stall count and standard to lite, the Mature family and the cloud step, a pin inside its family, no smaller model installed, a lite model that no longer fits and a custom model), `bridge/local-model-choice.test.mjs` (3: `stepDownTarget`, `stalled`, the 8 GB reserve), `bridge/mistral-key.test.mjs` (the notice), `bridge/local-turn-diagnostics.test.mjs` (two stalled turns through the host to the cloud step).
- **Live checks (need the game on an 8 GB card, or any card with the game's memory filled):** with Mature content on and `mature:good` chosen, load a heavy scene, talk twice: after two stalled turns the next turn should answer on the Mature lite model with the one notice, and the log shows `stepping down from`. With only one model installed the same should give the cloud text and the other notice. The saved row must still show the model the player chose.
**2026-10-20 (Pocket import stall, report `0493bf629d636be0`, kind `voice-failed`, V's helper voice, release 0.2.3; branch `fix/pocket-import-stall` from main, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` needs a bridge restart and the Runtime update zip (`bridge/pocket-voice-worker.py` changed)).** One install (RTX 5090, Vortex, game under Program Files (x86), Local AI Mature with OmniVoice, V's voice on with Pocket) saw V's Pocket helper fail twice in a row with "stalled at importing-dependencies" after 45 s each (+6.5 s for the first phase, so the disk was slow too). The 5 GB model and OmniVoice had finished loading before the helper started (it already starts after OmniVoice is ready), so the cause is a cold `import torch` (Windows Defender scanning every DLL, a slow disk) taking longer than the 45 s window, and the watchdog then killed the worker and began the same cold import again, which was just as slow.
- **Fix.** The worker has a startup heartbeat (`pocket-voice-worker.py`): a thread reports the process's CPU time every 2 s until the worker is ready (then it stops), and a mark follows each heavy import (numpy, torch, yaml, pocket_tts). The bridge (`pocket-voice.mjs`, `heartbeat()`) treats a mark, a new phase, or CPU time up by 100 ms since the last progress as progress and starts the stall window over. Only a worker with no progress for the window (importing now 60 s) is stopped and started once more; a second hang gives up, as before. A worker that keeps moving is never restarted (a restart is another cold import). The hard bound `startupMs` is now 240 s for the whole start (a restart gets what is left, never a fresh window); a worker still moving at the bound fails with the existing "startup timed out" and is not restarted. The log says which import finished and, every 30 s, "still importing-dependencies (worker CPU Ns), not stalled"; a real stall line now also shows the worker's CPU time. A late beat from a worker that is being stopped is ignored, a malformed beat fails the worker. No per-frame work and no polling: one small line per 2 s only while starting.
- **Not done:** serialising the heavy starts (V's helper already waits for OmniVoice to be ready and for any other Pocket worker to exit, `v-helper-voice.mjs`); the llama-server load was finished in this report too. The player-facing Help row "Pocket voice" is unchanged and still appears when the start truly fails (hang on both attempts or the 240 s bound). I/O counters were not added to the heartbeat (CPU time is enough to tell a deadlock from a slow import).
- **Tests:** `bridge/pocket-voice.test.mjs` (5 new: slow import with progress is not killed and gets ready; hung import killed at the window while a slow second attempt is left alone; hang on both attempts gives up; the hard bound fails a moving worker without a restart; malformed beats), existing stall tests now use the importing window; `scripts/test_pocket_voice_runtime.py` 39 ok. Live check owed: on a slow disk, V's helper voice should start (the log shows `imported torch` lines) instead of failing at 45 s.

- **V's voice with Pocket (a player: "I still don't hear V's voice ... do we have to install Pocket locally?").** No: Pocket ships inside the Runtime. Of the 13 installs, 9 started Pocket normally (a start takes 11 to 41 s, importing the libraries is the slow phase at 2 to 36 s; one of them had Voxtral for V), one was still loading when its report was cut, and one never started the service at all (no Chromium browser: nothing can speak; main already has the browser fix). Two installs have no V voice, both on Vortex under `Program Files (x86)\Steam`, one RTX 4060 (Convai text) and one RTX 5090 (Local AI, OmniVoice companions): Pocket failed at every start and retry (45 s, 180 s, 600 s) with "Pocket source differs from the pinned official revision", V's own Pocket worker failed once and stayed off ("typed lines stay silent"), the game said nothing. Cause: Vortex's `__folder_managed_by_vortex` marker inside the Runtime's folders (the service log of the 4060 install lists it among the files it copies), the same as round 2's find. That fix is on main (`SOURCE_IGNORES`, any depth) and covers the only place the source tree is hashed (`digest_source`); no other code walks the Runtime. Not seen on the reports: missing V clips, V's voice off, a Python or venv error, an antivirus block. The 5090 install also has OmniVoice failing twice (CUDA "out of memory" for 1.14 GiB with 30 GiB free, then exit 3221225477) and `llama-server` exiting 3221226505 (the ECONNREFUSED report): all three GPU workers died on that machine, looks like the driver or the card, not our code (another agent has the ECONNREFUSED part). V lines not heard on working Pocket installs: `voice-not-loaded` (a typed line before Pocket finished loading; once per session) and `slower-than-reply` / `reply-voice-started` (1 to 3 of 12 to 40 lines on three installs); by design.

(3) A voice that cannot start is an error report of its own: kind `voice-failed`, `<engine>: <reason>` for `pocket`, `v-helper`, `omni` (`ErrorEvents.voiceFailed`, wired from `VoiceSelection` `onFailure`, once per reason per run). (4) Settings > Help gets a "Pocket voice" row while Pocket or V's helper is failed (setup check `voice` / `pocket-failed` from `VoiceSelection.voiceProblem()`, row in `mod/setup-check.lua`; says nothing needs installing, restart, send a report); 2 new strings, translated in all 15 locales (Haiku), `Extract-UiCatalog --check` clean. **2026-10-20 (player latency report: "5 to 7 s extra before the speech, gone after alt-tab"; branch `fix/foreground-latency` from main b63eb997, worktree `agent-a0ae706d15301dadf`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; bridge restart plus Runtime update for 0.2.3, no CET reload, no DLL).** One player (release 0.2.2, provider and machine unknown, speech and text input both slow, then fast after switching windows and back). The error reports on disk carry no stage timings of a slow player turn (the `marks=` lines are fast V-helper and Pocket lines from other machines), so the findings come from the code.
- **1. Process priority: held, and it is the likely cause.** What ran at below normal on the critical path of a turn: the Pocket worker for its whole life (`pocket-voice-worker.py` `lower_priority()` at start, never raised), the chat model's llama-server after its warm-up (`LocalLlmServer` `lowerAfter: 'ready'`, `proc.lower()`), the embedding server (lowered at spawn, even while it loads), the speech recogniser (`local-stt.mjs` and `--priority below`). The bridge (Node), OmniVoice (raised to normal once loaded, `resident-voice.mjs`) and Chromium are at normal. A game that keeps every core busy at normal priority starves a below-normal thread (Windows also gives the foreground process longer time slices, which alt-tab removes, and the game eases off while it is in the background): `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` already measured it on 2026-10-19 (a model at below normal: 29 s to the first word at 3 tokens/s, at normal under the same load 3.7 s warm at 11 to 12 tokens/s). The 2026-10-19 fix raised only the model's LOAD; the finished model went back to below normal and generation was assumed unaffected because it runs on the card, but the server's own thread tokenizes, feeds the card and streams the reply.
- **Fix (Node and Python, no per-frame work, two system calls per turn).** (a) `LlamaProcess.raise()` (only if it was lowered); `LocalLlmServer.begin()` raises the ready chat model to normal at the start of a turn's request and `end()` lowers it `priorityHoldMs` (5 s) after the last request, one hold per process (cancelled by a new request, dropped with a stop, an idle stop or a crash so it never reaches the next process); a persona warm-up and the memory work (`begin({background: true})`, `text-provider-host.mjs` passes its `background` flag) stay below normal. (b) The embedder loads at normal (`lowerAfter: 'ready'`), is lowered once it is up and is raised for each query (`local-embed.mjs`). (c) The Pocket worker raises ITSELF (`PriorityGate` in `pocket-voice-worker.py`: `SetPriorityClass` from inside, because the python.exe the bridge starts can be a launcher whose child is the real worker, so `os.setPriority` on its pid may not reach it) for a `stream` request and for a `prepare` the bridge marks `urgent` (`PocketVoice.synthesizeStream` -> `ensurePrepared(..., {urgent: true})`; `prepareProfile` warming ahead of a reply is not urgent), and goes back to below normal 3 s after the last one (the gate is checked only in the worker's 0.1 s command wait; it never flaps between the sentences of one reply). Windows only; elsewhere nothing changes. V's helper Pocket worker is the same script. (d) The recogniser raises itself from `begin` until 3 s after its last message (`PriorityGate` in `local-stt-worker.py`; `--priority normal` changes nothing). OmniVoice already stays at normal after loading.
- **2. GPU priority: nothing set, nothing worse.** No `D3DKMT` call, no `--prio`, no llama.cpp priority flag anywhere (only a design note in `docs/LOCAL_OPTION_DESIGN.md`). WDDM schedules the card per process at equal priority, so a model on the card shares it with a game that keeps it busy; that is the same effect as the CPU starvation and ends too when the player switches windows. Raising a process's GPU scheduling class needs a privilege the bridge does not have (lowering is allowed and would only slow the model), so nothing was changed. Prompt reading on a busy card is the remaining cost on Local AI (`docs/LOCAL_AI.md`: 40 to 300 tokens/s); the cache (`--cache-ram`, `prewarm`) is what limits it.
- **3. The game-to-bridge hop: the polls are time based (`delta` accumulated, 30 ms reply probe, 0.1 s tick, nothing counts frames) and the bridge side has a 4 ms file watcher plus 50 to 150 ms polls, so neither adds seconds by itself. But the native plugin's file worker (`FileIo.cpp` `WorkerMain` and `WatcherMain`) runs at `THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL` inside the game, and EVERY routed file goes through it: the request Lua writes (`last-input.json`), `reply.json`, `speech-stream.json`, `continuous-speech.json` and the playback lease all wait for that thread to get a core. A CPU-bound game can starve one below-normal thread until Windows' anti-starvation boost (a thread that has not run for about 4 s gets a boost), so this is a second, plausible 1 to 4 s per direction, and it is not fixable without a new DLL (change both `SetThreadPriority` calls to normal: tiny CPU, small files; to be measured for frame time). The 0.2.2 DLL polls the worker every 15 ms (plus the 15.6 ms timer tick) per watched channel, 500 ms for a channel nothing has read for 3 s (a read wakes it at once), so with a free core the hop is at most about 0.6 s; the directory watcher (`2a82b154`) is not in 0.2.2 and only removes the poll wait, not the starvation. Not changed: the release carries the old DLL.**
- **4. Chromium: flags were already close.** The launch passed `--disable-background-timer-throttling` (and Playwright's own defaults add the other backgrounding switches). Made explicit anyway in `realtime-host.mjs`: `--disable-renderer-backgrounding` and `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` (no `--disable-features`: a second switch would replace Playwright's list). The hidden pages play the reply and hold the Convai connection, so a renderer at a lowered class or throttled timers would be a delay on every route that speaks through the browser.
- **5. Is it streaming? Yes, on every route, and the stage clock says where (`turn-clock.mjs`, `bridge-latency.json`).** Local AI and Mistral/Custom: the request is `stream: true` (`llmSent`, `llmHeaders`, `firstToken`), `ReplyStream` finds the first complete sentence of at least 28 characters while the model is still writing (`firstSentence`), that head goes to the voice at once (`voiceStart`, `ttsSent`), and the audio streams: Pocket sends PCM chunks as they are made (`firstPcm`), OmniVoice speaks phrase by phrase after the first complete phrase, the PCM host's renderer accepts the first chunk (`firstPcmAccepted`), the bridge publishes (`published`), the game's lease arrives (`leaseRead`) and the renderer's clock shows sound (`playbackObserved`). Convai: the text goes to the Convai connection (`llmSent`), the cloud returns PCM16 packets that play from at least 400 ms of audio on one AudioWorklet ring in the hidden browser; no local model. A reply with no safe head (a tag, a bracket, a quoted opening) is voiced after it is finished. Time to first sound = `received` to `playbackObserved`; the stages a slow machine stretches are `llmHeaders` to `firstToken` (the model's thread and prompt reading), `ttsSent` to `firstPcm` (Pocket's CPU), `published` to `leaseRead` (the plugin's file worker).
- **Tests:** `bridge/local-turn-diagnostics.test.mjs` (LlamaProcess.raise; the ready model raised for a turn, held, lowered once, not for a warm-up or background work, one raise for overlapping requests, the hold cancelled by the next request and never reaching the next process), `bridge/local-embed.test.mjs` (loads at normal, lowered when up, raised per query), `bridge/pocket-voice.test.mjs` (`urgent` only on the preparation a reply waits on), `scripts/test_pocket_voice_runtime.py` (`PriorityGate` and the urgent rule), `bridge/local-stt-worker.check.py` through `local-stt-worker.test.mjs` (`PriorityGate`), `bridge/realtime-teardown.test.mjs` (the browser arguments). Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, `docs/LOCAL_STT.md`.
- **Live checks (game needed, run after installing the bridge and the Runtime update):** (1) with the game running at full load on the player's kind of machine, a text turn and a spoken turn, in the foreground the whole time: compare `received` to `playbackObserved` in `bridge-latency.json` (or the `[Latency]` lines) before and after; the before was 5 to 7 s extra, the goal is the 1 to 2 s seen after alt-tab. (2) Task Manager Details during a turn: llama-server.exe and the Pocket python.exe at Normal during the turn and Below normal again about 5 s and 3 s after it. (3) FPS and frame-time while a reply is voiced, Pocket and Local AI, against the build before: the extra normal-priority work is only the turn's own generation, but nobody has measured it with the game running. (4) If a turn is still slow with the processes at Normal, look at `published` to `leaseRead` in the stage record: a long step there is the plugin's below-normal file worker, the DLL change in item 3.

Why the turn still failed: a request gets the server's address and key once, at the start of the turn, and both die with the process (a restart has a new port and key), so the retry could never work; Windows also keeps a crashed process listed while it writes its report, so the exit handler had not run yet. Fix: `bridge/local-server-recovery.mjs` (`survivingLoss`, one line in `localRoute`) wraps the route's request: a lost-server failure (refused or reset, or HTTP 5xx, nothing of the reply written, turn deadline set) asks `LocalLlmServer.recover()`, which checks `/health` once, ends and restarts a deaf process when the exit was not reported, waits for the start inside the turn's own time (never less than 3 s kept for one more request) and the request is sent once more at the new address and key. Once per request. Not ready in time: own line (reason `restarting`, "the model server stopped working and was still starting again"). Cannot start again (the old two attempts): the old `crashed` failure; the failed turn now says why after its sentence (`errorDetail` from `unavailableDetail`: pack missing, no graphics card, "the model server stopped working and did not start again"). New notice `local-restarted` "Local AI stopped working and was restarted." with the next reply (event `restarted`, `MistralProvider.noteLocalRestarted`, `mod/notices.lua`, docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md, 15 locales). Turns that arrive while the server is starting or idle-stopped already waited for it (`connect`, bounded) and a test now covers it. Nothing per frame; only runs after a failed request. Details: docs/LOCAL_AI.md "When the model server stops while a turn is asked". Fake llama-server got `FAKE_LLAMA_GO_DEAF_AT`.

**2026-10-20 (error signature `0e895ffe08c86288`, "Convai PCM size does not match its declared duration"; branch `fix/convai-pcm-size` from main, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched; `bridge/` change, needs a bridge restart plus a rebuild of the browser bundle at release):**
- **Cause (inferred, the report carried no numbers).** `ConvaiDataAudio.validateTotals` in `bridge/convai-data-audio.mjs` compared Convai's declared `total_audio_duration_ms` with `total_audio_bytes / (rate * channels * 2)` and allowed only 1 sample plus 1 ms. The declared figure is a rounded millisecond count, probably summed per packet, so on a long reply it drifts by more than 1 ms and the whole turn failed although the bytes were complete and aligned.
- **Fix.** The byte count stays the authority; the duration check now allows 30 ms plus 1 percent of the duration (the facial-duration check, which only drops faces, uses the same allowance). A wrong sample rate or channel count (8 percent or more off) still fails. Both failures now carry the numbers (bytes, declared ms against counted ms, rate, channels, packets), and declared bytes that are not whole samples get their own message. Tests in `bridge/convai-data-audio.test.mjs`. If the signature returns, the message now shows the real figures.
- **Test state.** `npm test` in the worktree: only 4 failures, all from the worktree having no `node_modules` (SDK package.json, playwright inputs, facial-timeline file). Live check owed: none beyond a normal Convai turn after the bridge restart.

- **Removal on start.** `packaging/runtime/apply-removals.mjs` (shipped as `app/launcher/apply-removals.mjs`, added to the launcher file list in `build-release.mjs`) reads `app/defaults/runtime-removals.json` (`{"version": "0.2.3", "removes": ["<path relative to the folder the Runtime was extracted into, forward slashes, as named in the zip>", ...]}`) and deletes the listed files. `start-service.mjs` calls it inside its own try/catch after the log exists and before the data is prepared, at every start, also with `--prepare-only` (summary field `removals`). Files only; allowed roots are the plugin folder, `red4ext/plugins/AiNpcCyberpunkModNative/`, `r6/audioware/CyberpunkConvai/` and `convai_*` / `cyberpunk_convai_*` archives in `archive/pc/mod/` (a small widening of "inside the plugin folder", because the Runtime ships those too); protected: `launcher.ini`, `launcher.log`, `app/release.json`, the list, `app/omni/`, `app/local-ai/`, `data/`, `state/`. Refuses `..`, `.`, empty parts, absolute paths, drives, colons, backslashes, control characters, folders, and a link that leads out of the Runtime's folder; 8 s budget (rest waits for the next start), one log line per start, idempotent, errors logged and never fatal, a Runtime without the module still starts. **MO2:** the install folder is derived from where `app/` really is (four folders up), not from `--game-root`, so the delete is a plain delete in the Runtime's own mod folder; a same-named file in the game folder or another mod is never touched; a non-standard layout is left alone. Every Runtime carries the list, the full one too: `build-release.mjs` writes it from the committed `packaging/runtime-removals.json` (declared extras, empty now) and refuses a declared path that the same Runtime ships or that the start step may not delete (`packaging/lib/runtime-removals.mjs`).
- **Builder.** `node packaging/build-runtime-update.mjs --old <previous full Runtime zip> --new <new full Runtime zip> --out <folder> [--old/--new again for parts] [--from V --to V] [--remove PATH]... [--listing FILE | --no-listing]` compares the zips' directories by path (case-insensitive) + size + CRC-32, copies every added or changed entry out of the new zip (new reader `packaging/lib/zip-entry.mjs`; `listZip` entries now carry `offset`), always the new `app/release.json`, and writes the removal list (old not in new, plus the new Runtime's own declared list, plus `--remove`; a path the start step may not delete or that an optional pack ships is left in place and printed). Output: the zip (deterministic: same inputs, same bytes; independent of how the full zips were made), `<name>.files.json` (path, bytes, sha256) and `<name>.sha256`. Dry run on the real 0.2.2 Runtime zip (read only, old = new): 11,055 files compared in 0.3 s; the three largest entries and `node.exe` extracted with their CRC-32 checked.
- **Install test.** `packaging/test-release-install.mjs` has an update mode: `--update-from <previous Runtime zip>` (repeatable) `--update-from-scripts <previous Scripts zip> [--update-zip <zip>]` extracts the previous Scripts and Runtime, then the update zip and the new Scripts, runs the start step and checks: the update's list is the installed one, the listed files existed and are gone with nothing refused or failed, every file matches the NEW full Runtime's `.files.json` (that file's list entry excepted: the update's list replaces the full one's by design), everything the new Runtime no longer ships is gone or left on purpose, and the plugin folder holds nothing else; the rest of the install test then runs on that installation. Run for real only on fixture zips with a copied `node.exe` (all the update checks passed; the later voice and launcher checks failed there because the fixture has no Python or models), not on a real 0.2.3 build (none exists yet).
- **Tests.** `packaging/runtime-removals.test.mjs` (13: path safety, protected files, folder pruning, idempotence, missing and bad lists, link escape, MO2 mod folder, time budget, the start script and a Runtime missing the step) and `packaging/build-runtime-update.test.mjs` (8: added/changed/removed detection, list contents, determinism, the old Runtime plus the update plus the start equals the new Runtime, several-zip Runtimes, extra removals, entry reading incl. ZIP64 and a damaged entry, the command line).
- **Docs.** `docs/PACKAGING.md` "Runtime update zip" (and a packages-table row), `README.md` and `packaging/PLAYER_README.md` Update paragraphs (players: update zip if you have the previous version, else the full Runtime; Replace is safe), `packaging/HF_MODEL_CARD.md` row (size TBD).

**2026-10-20 (Back on the home page: not possible through MCM's public API; branch `fix/home-back` from main 017612cf, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched).** Owner asked for a footer Back on Home like the sub-pages have. MCM's source (read only) has no public way to close or leave its screen. `api.ui` offers open, setSearch, setScrollPosition, setNavigation (pageId, backActionId, escapeBack, searchMode), setFooterActions, setApplyPolicy, setPresentation, setStatus, setReadOnlyValues, setChoiceStates and clear; none closes. `api.closeMod` only closes the provider's active mod in MCM's core (drafts cleared, active key nil) and leaves the screen and its selected mod showing, which would leave a stale page, so it is not used. MCM has no mod-list page to go back to either: its screen is always the mod list on the left and the selected mod on the right. The only thing that closes the screen is its own Escape (the native Cancel input): `Controller:handleClosing` runs the page's `backActionId` action when `escapeBack` is on, otherwise (no back action, no pending drafts) lets the close through, in the gameplay popup (`m_popupHost.Close()`) and at the title screen (Settings host) alike. Our Home sets no `backActionId` and `escapeBack = true`, so Escape already closes MCM from Home; a footer button there could not do the same, and a button that does nothing would be dishonest, so none was added. Change: a comment in `mod/mcm-host.lua` and one more assertion in the Home test in `bridge/mcm-host.test.mjs` (`escapeBack == true` next to `backActionId == nil`, with the reason). Closest honest alternative if the owner still wants something visible on Home: a one-line hint such as "Press Esc to close" (new string, 15 locales, catalogue) or ask the MCM author (Antrix, already on the list of MCM limits) for a public close call.

**2026-10-20 (live test failures of V talks and Johnny's hologram; branch `fix/vtalks-hologram-live` from main c056e7e8, worktree `agent-a9257027ea9af7b2c`, committed, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not touched, no live Convai or Mistral turn; Lua needs a CET reload, `bridge/` a bridge restart).** The owner's first live test (2026-10-19 evening, dev install of 9af09966 + c056e7e8; settings `vTalks normal`, `johnnyInHead`, `johnnyHologram`, `johnnyRemarks normal`, V's voice on) failed for both features and the manager.
- **V talks: no exchange, no `V talks on their own` line.** Root cause (from `probe.log` 18:46Z, `runtime/battle-cancellations.json` and the code): the fight was 15 s of combat (Johnny's line: `fight over seconds=15 dead=5 alive=1`). `battles.capture().durationSeconds` is the encounter, which ends four seconds after the last combat sample, so it was about 19 s (the cancellation file's clock: combat quiet at 90.4, encounter started about 75.4), and `fightEvent` compared that with `FIGHT_MIN_SECONDS = 20`: the fight was dropped as a scuffle with no log line, and `fightSeen` marked it so it was never looked at again. The service was made (V's voice and the setting were on), the encounter was seen, nothing else gated. Fix: `capture()` carries `combatSeconds`; `FIGHT_MIN_SECONDS` is 10 of those (Johnny counts 8); a fight that does not count logs once (`fight battle-N not counted: N s of combat, a scuffle under 10 s`); the fight event waits 150 s (was 90: the battle line, then Johnny's remark, each followed by 15 quiet seconds, come first; in the live timeline the window was about 45 s before a save reload at 18:47:47). Every wait now says why: the service logs `V talks on their own: waiting, not starting: <reason>` once per reason and waiting spell (busy turn, rate gap or hourly limit, muted voice, the game has the floor, game line, another reaction ended under 15 s ago, handover, no companion within 12 m, quiet time, same trigger, standing still), and `<subject> dropped unsaid: it waited longer than N s` on expiry. Johnny and V talks do not share a cooldown except the 15 s after any automatic reaction (a reason line says so); they do share the Convai shared-key remark pool (10 of 100 a day): Johnny's remarks may now take at most 7 of the 10 (`VTALK_RESERVE` 0.3 in `bridge/shared-key-guard.mjs`), so a chatty Johnny cannot starve V's exchanges; V's exchanges may use all ten. The owner's Mistral turns count none of this.
- **Johnny's hologram: `skipped sit kind=scene reason=dialogue` twice; and the manager's F4 refused on the couch ("Finish the scene first." 15 times in `probe.log` 18:48 to 18:49).** Root cause: V's chairs and couches are scene sits (scene tier 3, `seated-look` kind `scene`), and while V sits the observer's dialogue flag or choice-hub flag is up (the log says `dialogue`, which is either; the sit starts with a `Dialog` or `Device` choice pick a few seconds earlier). `johnny-hologram.lua decide` ends the moment on either flag, `interrupt` would send him away on either, `johnny-head.lua busy` refuses Johnny's talk on dialogue or tier 3, and `nsui-entry.lua` and `mcm-host.lua` refuse the shortcut at scene tier 3. The tests only ever built a tier 3 sample with both flags false, so they passed. Fix: `seated-look.lua M.plain` (pure) says V sits plainly (controller holds a sit with `sitAt`, tier 3 or below and readable, no call, fight, replacer or vehicle, no non-crowd game line since V sat); the observer hook `battleObserver.sitProbe` (set at the top of `init.lua`, globals only) puts it in `sample.sitting`; while true the hologram (decide and interrupt) and Johnny's talk ignore the dialogue and choice flags, and the manager's shortcut asks `convaiPlainSitting()` (one fresh sample, only at tier 3 or above, on a key press; a no logs `Plain sit check: no (seated-look sitting=... dialogue=... choices=... tier=...)`, at most every 5 s). A game line, a call, a fight, tier 4 or a replacer still end the plain sit, so cutscenes and dialogues still block. The hologram's skip, spawn and gone lines now carry `(dialogue=.. choices=.. tier=.. call=.. combat=.. sitting=..)`. The talk keys for companions have no scene gate (checked by search: the talk-key path for party companions in `init.lua` reads no scene tier); the talk keys for the game's own story characters (`world-talk.lua`, tier 3 and above is "hub") and V talks (`module.busy`) are unchanged on purpose: a story character at a scene sit is the game's scene. Open uncertainty: the first sit of the test (18:48:21) has no `seated-look-enter` line in `probe.log` although the hologram heard a sit; if the manager still refuses on a couch, the new `Plain sit check` line says whether the controller held a sit.
- **Seen in passing, not touched:** the dialogue hook logged `choice not recorded (not-dialogue visualizer=Dialog success=true)` for a choice whose visualizer printed as `Dialog` (`game-dialogue.lua N.dialogChoice` compares `visualizerType == Enum.new(...)`); either the enum comparison never matches in the live game or those picks really are not dialogue, and no `choice recorded` line exists in the whole `probe.log`. Worth a look when the dialogue ledger is next touched.
- **Tests:** `bridge/v-talks.test.mjs` (combat time, the live fight, once-per-reason logs, expiry, the reserve), `bridge/battle-reactions.test.mjs` unchanged and green, `bridge/johnny-hologram.test.mjs` (decide and interrupt with the live flags, `flags`, the chain of the real seated-look controller, the real observer and init's probe through to a spawn, and the cutscene variants, `convaiPlainSitting`), `bridge/seated-look.test.mjs` (`plain`, `sitAt`), `bridge/johnny-head.test.mjs`, `bridge/nsui-entry.test.mjs` and `bridge/mcm-host.test.mjs` (the shortcut on a couch and in a real scene), `bridge/johnny-remarks.test.mjs`. Mutation check: removing the `sitting` exemption from `decide` fails the three hologram tests built on the live flags.
- **Recheck steps (the owner; CET reload after installing all committed `mod/` files, bridge restart for the reserve):** (1) V talks Normal, V's voice on, a companion in the party: fight for 12 to 20 s of combat; `probe.log` shows `V talks on their own: noted fight:battle-N`, then within about a minute either `fight part 1 of N` or `waiting, not starting: <reason>` lines; a scuffle shows `fight battle-N not counted`. (2) Johnny in your head and Johnny's hologram on, story past Playing for Time: sit on a couch or bar stool; 4 to 6 s later `Johnny hologram: spawning ...` and `shown`, then `gone reason=done` after about 5 s; the lines carry the flags. (3) While seated (and while the hologram is up), press F4: the manager opens (no "Finish the scene first."); in a real cutscene it still refuses. (4) Johnny's private talk key while seated works. (5) Send the new `probe.log` lines back.

**2026-10-19 (Mei1429's phone chat and idle GPU; branch `fix/mei-phone-gpu` from main 689c9d43, merged main c6ae000d into it; NOT merged to main, NOT pushed, NOT installed, game not launched, no live Convai or Mistral turn; Lua needs a CET reload, `bridge/` a bridge restart; `Extract-UiCatalog.mjs --check` clean).** Nexus report (0.2.1, OmniVoice Ultra): phone chat says "Message could not be delivered. Please try again" and about 3x GPU use with nothing in use. **Phone chat.** That text is the one catch-all of `PhoneChat`'s send (`bridge/phone-chat.mjs`) and nothing was logged behind it. Walked every way into it: contact not supported; world heartbeat stale or changed (`PlayerPhoneKnowledge` codes); memory route not ready; the shared key's daily or rate guard; Convai's concurrency, quota, speaker, memory and key answers; text-provider failures; a stale session; browser or network loss; an invalid reply. Nothing in the phone path waits on the voice engine, TTS or OmniVoice (`ttsEnabled:false`; the voice-route reservation only delays the poll), and nothing needs a prior face-to-face talk. **Real bug, fixed and proven:** `TextProviderHost` returns the session id it was given (`sessionID: config.sessionId`); a first phone message is given `-1`, which `PhoneChat` refused as an invalid reply, so on Mistral, Local AI and the custom endpoint every phone message ended in the generic text (a test with a real `TextProviderHost` and a fake server fails without the fix). A reply with no session is now delivered and no session is remembered; a malformed id is still refused. **Visible reasons:** new `bridge/phone-failure.mjs`: stage (`route`, `binding`, `provider`, `reply`, `publish`) and a reason code per failed message; one log line `Phone chat message failed: reason=... stage=... contact=... provider=...` (never message or reply text); `runtime/phone-failure-state.json` (last reason, stage, provider, counts per reason; classified `exchange` in `packaging/runtime-exchange.json`) carried by the support report as `bridge.status["phone-failure-state.json"]`; the automatic error report for a fault (not for a load or a newer message ending the send). The player text is unchanged. **Two more fixes (coordinator):** the phone's 45 s wait is now the provider's budget plus a margin (`phoneChat.replyWait` in `mod/init.lua`, asked once per sent message: Convai and Mistral 45 s, Local AI 95 s for its 80 s budget with a cold load, custom 125 s), so a Local AI cold load shows the bridge's own explanation instead of "No reply received"; and `quota-shared`, `quota-own`, `key-rejected`, `key-memory-needed` get their own phone status lines, the exact sentences of the game's notices (already in all 15 locales; `phone-chat-style.lua` and `localization/en.json` regenerated). **Most likely for Mei:** if she was on Mistral, Local AI or custom, the session bug explains it fully; if on Convai, the likely causes are the shared plan's concurrency limit (`convai-busy`, retried only on a player's own key), the shared key's rate guard, or a second hidden browser failing to start; the new log line will say which (ask for a support report, `bridge.status["phone-failure-state.json"]`). **Idle GPU** (helper, commit 298047b0, `docs/RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE.md`, `bridge/idle-gpu.test.mjs`): measured with the game closed (Windows GPU Engine counters per process, 75 s idle windows): OmniVoice worker, hidden Edge with the renderer page, Pocket (CPU), llama-server plus the CPU embedder, all 0.000 %; the facial model, phone analysis and recogniser are not on the GPU. The culprit is `NearbyWarm`: with `Auto-connect nearby characters` on (default) it prepared every nearby NPC's OmniVoice voice (1 to 3 s of the card each, repeating as V walks through a crowd; the 8-profile cache is exceeded by a rotation of more than eight) and the Local AI loaded each one's persona. Now, with OmniVoice speaking and playback on (`VoiceSelection.preparesOnGpu`), nearby-only characters are skipped (`NearbyWarm gpuVoice`; the local AI's warm skips role `nearby`), and `warmTalkTargets` (composer hint, talk key, turn start) prepares the speaker when V starts to talk. Partners and spawned followers keep their ahead-of-time preparation; Pocket and cloud voices are unchanged. **Reconciled with `fix/error-reports-round1`:** the local server has one slot and `LocalLlmServer.prewarm` stops an older persona warm-up for another character (`preempt`), so `warmTalkTargets` now reads only the first speaker's persona (a group's other voices are all prepared); a turn calls `preempt(profileKey)` as before and a same-character warm-up is still waited for. **Tests:** new `bridge/phone-failure.test.mjs` (42: 29 reason causes, step names, the log line and record, the recorder, the first message of a text provider, the support report, the bridge wiring), three Lua cases in `bridge/phone-chat.test.mjs` (wait per provider, a slow local reply still arrives, the new status lines), `bridge/idle-gpu.test.mjs` (10). (1) **Bridge crash loop (1 player, 2 signatures):** a Runtime missing one of its four start-up data files; the bridge died five times and the game saw only `bridge-crashed`. New `bridge/runtime-files.mjs` (registered in `BRIDGE_MODULES` and `release-plan.json`): the supervisor checks the files first (`requiredFiles`, passed by `start-service.mjs` and `Supervise-ConversationBridge.mjs`) and publishes `install-incomplete` (the game's "Runtime is incomplete" line); a bridge that finds one missing exits 78 with one line, no restart loop; an unawaited file read that fails with ENOENT/EPERM/EBUSY/... no longer ends the bridge (`installFileErrorGuard`), every other unhandled rejection still does. (3) **Local AI timeouts (2 players, 5 reports; a third player's log shows the same load):** the game fills the card so the Mature model loads with layers on the CPU (231 and 3,208 MiB free; the machine's limit, not fixed), a persona warm-up held the single slot while a turn waited (60 s "no response"), and prompts of 3,900 to 7,600 tokens were re-read at about 3,000 new tokens a turn because the world facts (ranked by V's words) sat first among the world blocks. Fixed: `LocalLlmServer.preempt` (a turn for another character stops a warm-up, the same character waits for it, no second warm-up of a persona being read; the route's `connect` and the `#decide` request carry the key); `worldBlocksInCacheOrder` (facts after the stable blocks; the `authority` sentence got a place-mark key; Convai context unchanged); `PrefillMeter` + soft target in `budgetedChat` (a machine seen to read below 700 tokens/s, or a model with layers on the CPU, is fitted to what the server holds, or the persona on a cold start, plus 8 s of reading, in steps; unreachable target: sent as before); the game's sentence says `the model is partly on the CPU`. Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` ("The first player reports of 0.2.2"), `docs/MISTRAL.md` (prompt order), `docs/ERROR_REPORTS.md`. (4) **Nothing to fix:** `service never` (2 players: Scripts without the Runtime on the first session), `browser-missing` (1: Windows 10 with no Chromium browser), `local-ai not-installed` (1: Convai answered); the in-game lines are clear. **To check in the game (nothing seen live):** a second turn with the same character should show far fewer new tokens in `[LocalTurn]`; on a slow card `(soft target)` and `reads about N tokens a second` in the log; with a nearby character warmed and V talking to another, `persona prewarm stopped` and no wait; a Runtime with `characters/world-knowledge.json` removed shows "Runtime is incomplete" and starts no bridge. Not merged with `fix/idle-gpu` (separate branch that moves the persona warm-up to the start of a talk; it works with this one). Open question for the user: the idle stop after ten minutes makes a reload find little free memory on a card the game fills (the model then loads partly on the CPU); it is what keeps the frame rate, so it was left.

**2026-10-19 (night, branch `fix/mcm-nsui-mirror`, from main 44c5445d): Brokad's report on 0.2.2, "Native setting UI rebuilt this setting. Reopen the mod before applying it again." on any setting change in MCM.** That text is MCM's own (`bridges/native_settings/provider.lua`, `applyBatch`, when `resolveLiveOption` cannot find the option object it captured), so he was changing settings on MCM's mirror of OUR Native Settings UI tab, not on our MCM page. Root cause (from the code; no live repro of his machine): our design is MCM 0.10.5+ hosts the page and no NSUI tab exists, but three paths let the tab exist beside MCM. (1) `M.open` fell back to `connect(true)` whenever the MCM host could not open the page (any refusal of `api.ui.open`, e.g. "No UI renderer is available"), registering the tab for the rest of the session while MCM was installed; MCM's bridge then listed it a second time (`nsui.lua` old M.open). (2) An MCM that is present at onInit but whose public interface is not complete yet is refused by the MCM host and retried once a second, but the NSUI tab was registered at once, so both existed (candidate 1). (3) With MCM older than 0.10.5 only the NSUI host runs and MCM mirrors it; the mirror finds an option again by index, type and path, and our reconcile removed and re-added any row whose label or description changed (state-dependent labels such as "Voice status: ...", or a language change), and the sections of a page whose name changed, so handles held by the mirror went stale. Ruled out by reading and a fake run of the real `provider.lua` over our host (scratch only): a plain value change on a page keeps every handle valid, so a rebuild of the whole tab per apply (candidate 3) is not what happens. Fix, owner's rule (MCM 0.10.5+ and NSUI both installed means MCM only, the NSUI tab must not exist): `mcm-host.lua` gains `present()` and `pending()`; `nsui.lua` never registers the tab while the MCM host is ready (also not as a fallback of the shortcut, which now returns MCM's reason), holds it back for 10 s (once-a-second look, never per frame) while an MCM that may still become ready is present, and takes a tab that was registered before MCM turned up down at the next once-a-second look once it is not on screen (NSUI 1.96 has no removeTab: the sections go through `removeSubcategory` and the empty tab is dropped from `nativeSettings.data`; if MCM's lifecycle helper had already snapshotted the tab, MCM may still list a ghost entry for that session, which is why the wait exists). One log line per session says which situation was met. Beside an MCM older than 0.10.5 (or NSUI alone) the tab now keeps its option tables and its sections in place when only text, limits or a section name change while the tab is not on screen (`retarget`, `renameSection`), and logs one line that MCM mirrors it. Tests: `bridge/mcm-host.test.mjs` (the rule: MCM at onInit, MCM loading after our mod with the tab removed, tab on screen when MCM turns up, MCM present but not ready waits 10 s and then yields to NSUI, MCM older than 0.10.5 no wait, shortcut refusal registers nothing), `bridge/nsui-manager.test.mjs` (a mirror-style holder of handles stays valid across switch/slider/selector/rule changes and a language change; a value change from the screen rebuilds nothing); fixture options `hideMcm` and `earlyClock` in `bridge/manager-fixture.mjs`. Docs: `docs/MANAGER_UI.md` "Both installed". No player text changed. Live check pending (below in the report).

**2026-10-19 (V talks on their own; branch `v-talks`, worktree `wt-v-talks`, from main 120bc54f; NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game; game not launched, no game input): V starts short exchanges with a party companion.** Request from a Nexus player (chiefertain): V replies on their own now and then, after something intense, never endlessly. Design and live checks: `docs/V_TALKS.md`.
- **What it is.** Settings > Conversations > V talks on their own (Off by default, Rare or Normal; `vTalks` in `runtime/settings.json`), right under Johnny speaks up. An exchange is V's line, the companion's answer and, in about four of ten, V's second line and the companion's second answer. V's lines are a reviewed bank in `mod/v-talks.lua` (57 lines: 10 after a fight, 6 to 8 after a job, 10 to 12 on a walk, 6 to 7 in a ride, 8 follow-ups; lifepath only colours the calm lines; the whole bank is scanned by a test for names, outcomes, decisions, Johnny and the Relic). It needs V's voice for typed lines (V's line is spoken in V's voice and shown as V's subtitle); with that off the feature is silent. Written, not generated, because the free shared Convai key has no V character and a generated V could state what the knowledge rules do not support.
- **Triggers.** `fight`: the encounter state of `battle-reactions.lua` read on the 0.5 s sample, one event per ended encounter of 20 s or more (waits 8 s, expires after 90 s). `job`: `journalHistory.onFinished`, a main or side job finished or failed (waits 15 s, expires after 240 s, no gigs or hustles). `walk` and `ride`: a calm spell (open gameplay, no scene tier 3 or above, call, quest conversation or fight) of 10 min at Normal or 20 min at Rare plus up to half again, with V moved 40 m or more (two position reads per spell); V in a vehicle makes it a ride. Only a party companion within 12 m who can speak (never a spawned character, an ordinary NPC, Johnny in V's head or an add-on voice), a fight's witness first.
- **Rate.** Rare: 2 an hour, 15 minutes apart. Normal: 6 an hour, 5 minutes apart. One slot per exchange; a first part nobody heard gives it back. The same trigger (`fight`, `job`, `walk`, `ride`) never starts two exchanges in a row within half an hour (`REPEAT_SECONDS`; strict-forever is `math.huge`: open question 1). Never during scenes (tier 3+), calls, quest conversations, fights, while the composer is open or V talks or records, a group round, a phone chat, within 10 s of a game line, while another automatic reaction (battle, loot, Johnny remark) is the current turn or ended less than 15 s ago, or while a reply plays. Checked at the start, every 0.1 s tick while a step is in flight, and fresh when a reply is about to be heard (a vehicle is fine).
- **How it runs.** `mod/init.lua`: `convaiVTalksService` (loaded only with the setting on and V's voice on, dropped when either goes off), `convaiVTalkSample` (on the existing 0.5 s sample, under pcall: the service is made or dropped, the calm spell is followed, an ended fight is noted), `convaiVTalkNote` (the journal callback, wrapped beside Johnny's), `convaiVTalkTick` (the 0.1 s tick, under pcall: keeps or releases an owned step, otherwise offers an exchange or its second part), `convaiVTalkCanDeliver` (the fresh gate before a reply is heard), the release hook in `cancelAutomatic`, `sendRequest` capturing the turn context for V's gender and the dialogue volume, and one branch in the reply-error path (`vtalk-silent` mutes for 10 minutes). Globals, so no upvalue is added to `updateBattles`; the existing Johnny wiring text is untouched (the owned branch is an `elseif` in front of his). Bridge: `bridge/v-talks.mjs` (new: `parseVTalkReaction`, `vTalkTrigger`, `VTalkLedger`), `protocol.mjs`, `battle-context.mjs`, `shared-key-guard.mjs` (`isRemark` now names `vtalk` too, one cap with Johnny's remarks, no second cap), `v-voice.mjs` (the one reaction that gets a V line is V's own opener; the line is required: the answer waits for it up to 6 s instead of V being dropped), `convai-bridge.mjs` (in `runInput` the allowance is asked before V says a word, a line that cannot be spoken ends the step with `vtalk-silent` and no model request, the ledger carries the first part's lines to the second part's companion), `mistral-prompt.mjs` and `text-provider-host.mjs` (the text providers head V's own line as "V SPEAKS TO YOU", not as an event).
- **Packages.** Scripts: `mod/v-talks.lua`, `init.lua`, `manager.lua`, `manager-ui.lua` (was `mcm.lua` before the merge of main), 15 locales. Runtime: the bridge files above. Not shipped: `localization/en.json` (regenerated: its source line numbers moved), tests, `docs/V_TALKS.md`. `packaging/release-plan.json`, `scripts/development-files.json` and `packaging/runtime-layout.mjs` list the two new files.
- **Cost.** Off: nothing loaded; one settings read per 0.5 s sample and one nil check per 0.1 s tick. On: nothing per frame, no new hook, no new native read per tick; a calm talk reads V's position twice per spell; a started step costs what a battle reaction costs plus one `convaiTurnContext:capture()`.
- **Translations.** The three strings (label, help text, error) in all 15 locales by one Haiku helper, spot-checked against the existing wording of "V's voice for typed lines", "Johnny speaks up", Rare and Normal. `node scripts/Extract-UiCatalog.mjs --check` passes.

Existing tests that pinned one caller were updated (`subtitles.test.mjs`: two `showTyped` callers; `turn-context.test.mjs`: a third `capture()` reader; `battle-lease.test.mjs` and `loot-context.test.mjs`: the poll harness gets a `VTalkLedger`).
