**2026-10-15 (branch `companion-vision`, from main 404ad14c, merged with main 00e7b682 (e0c03b68) and 79e03690; unit-tested, capture measured against the running game with no input; NOT merged into main, NOT installed, no live Convai turn): Companions can see the surroundings.**
- **Research** (`docs/COMPANION_VISION.md`, with links):
  - The realtime Web SDK 1.7.0 we use takes pictures two ways: dynamic vision context (a LiveKit video track sampled by the server into a buffer and attached to the next model turn, with acknowledgements) and `uploadFile` (a byte stream; server behaviour undocumented). Publishing before the text is the documented streaming mode.
  - Vision is account-gated and needs a non-realtime Gemini or GPT model. Our Gemma 4 31B Fast is listed among the realtime models, so `vision_not_enabled` is possible; only a live call can tell.
  - Auth-token mode is unaffected. No per-image price or rate limit is published.
  - Mistral (Ministral 3 takes images on the same endpoint) is postponed by the user. Local AI needs Gemma's mmproj: a download and about 1 GB more VRAM (not built).
- **Design history:** the first build sent a talk-time picture only with lines asking about something visible; then a picture on every turn. The user then pointed out a talk-time picture mostly shows the companion's face, and asked for the surroundings with V and the companion small or absent.
- **Built (final):**
  - Setting "Companions can see" in the Conversation provider section, **on by default**, Convai only.
  - An out-of-process Windows Graphics Capture helper (`native/vision/`, C++/WinRT) captures only the game window: a 768 px JPEG in memory, nothing on disk, `minimised` reported.
  - A rolling buffer (`bridge/companion-vision.mjs`): one picture every 3 s, the last 4 in memory, only while the setting is on, Convai answers, someone V can talk to is near, and no conversation is running (plus 12 s after one). A turn sends the newest frame taken at least 2.5 s before the conversation started, so it shows the place V was looking at, not the companion; nothing older than 2 minutes.
  - Latency: the chosen frame is published to Convai when the composer opens (each speaker's page in a group, retried while a page connects) and right after the talk-key press, so Convai's estimated 0.4 to 0.7 s acceptance overlaps typing or talking. At send the page sees the same picture already staged and waits for nothing. A turn not staged ahead waits at most 350 ms (`visionWaitMs`), beside the context update. An unclaimed picture is withdrawn when the composer closes or after 60 s.
  - The unload rule (`docs/RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE.md`): the helper process exists only while it is capturing; it is stopped when the setting is off, under Mistral or Local AI, with nobody near, or during a conversation.
  - One sentence in the context says the image shows the surroundings from a few seconds before, may show the HUD, V's vehicle or the companion, and not to guess without one. Any failure sends the line without a picture.
  - `companionVision.attachToNextTurn(images, {characterId, ttlMs})` is the entry point for the YouTube-on-TV feature.
- **Measured:**
  - Capture every 3 s: round trip 107 ms median (p95 133), helper CPU 15.6 ms median. Helper start about 0.2 s, cold start plus first capture 338 ms, memory 35 to 51 MiB.
  - Game FPS A/B every 3 s (two runs, 12 and 16 blocks of 20 s): 57.41 against 57.41, and 55.49 against 55.47 (means). Slow frames were not more frequent in windows that held a capture (0.40 per window) than in "with" windows that held none (0.54). The isolated long frames (217 and 227 ms) fell in windows without a capture.
  - Added latency (estimates): talk key about 0; typed with the composer open first about 0; otherwise at most 350 ms.
- **Four views around V:** not built. Script has no render-texture readback; each extra camera is a full scene render every frame, plus streaming hitches; camera or photo-mode moves are visible. The buffer gives a view of the place at no measured cost.
- **The TV as the source** (user, via the coordinator): while a YouTube video plays on V's TV, about one 640 px frame a second of our own TV window (DevTools screenshot, no game capture; the game helper is released) is fed as a live canvas track to the party companions' open pages, which reconnect between conversations with five frames a turn (`TV_VISION_INPUT_CONFIG`). Turns publish nothing and wait for nothing; the context says these are the last seconds of the video. Nothing is grabbed or published without a playing video, with the setting off, under Mistral or Local AI, or with nobody near. API: `youtubeTv.visionSource()` and `companionVision.setScreenSource()`, wired in `convai-bridge.mjs`. Measured against the running game (not seated, game in the background, about 60 fps): no TV 58.97 FPS median, video without frames 59.91, video with 1 frame a second 59.94 (frames over 25 ms per window 0.15 / 0.36 / 0); a grab takes 13.9 ms median in the bridge and returns 14 KB. 2 fps not measured (the game was restarted by someone else mid-run, no crash report).
- **Two bugs fixed in the merged YouTube TV window helper** (`bridge/youtube-tv-window.ps1`, found running it for real): Windows PowerShell 5.1's `[Console]::In.ReadLineAsync()` runs synchronously, so the helper blocked waiting for a second command before handling `attach` while the bridge waited for `attached`, and the TV never opened; and Edge titles the window "<title> - Profile 1 - Microsoft Edge", which the exact title match never found. Now a `StreamReader` over the raw stdin and a prefix match (the title has a random nonce). Regression test in `youtube-tv.test.mjs` runs the real helper.
- **mcm.lua diff:** one `setting('companionVision', …)` row right after the Conversation provider selector, and `companionVision` in the Apply boolean key list.
- **Tests:** `bridge/companion-vision.test.mjs` (20), `bridge/convai-vision.test.mjs` (17), 3 realtime-client cases, 1 youtube-tv case; manager row lists updated; 2 strings in 15 languages; `localization/en.json` regenerated.
- **Live check:** under Open items B2. It needs the user's approval for about 5 to 10 Convai turns.

The frame belongs to the vanilla `WarningMessageGameController` (`tools/redmod/scripts/cyberpunk/UI/hud/warningMessage.script`, read only): it sets the text (upper case), picks the Neutral state and icon, then plays the library animation `warning` from the start to the marker `freeze_intro` (from `idle_start` when `isInstant`), after `StopAllAnimations`. The frame's geometry lives in the game's `.inkwidget` archive and its intro animation, neither of which is in the repo or readable as text, so a layout, margin or clip cause could not be confirmed. Mod-side differences from a vanilla notice that could matter, none proven: (1) joined and ready lines usually replace the held loading notice while it is on screen, so the text changes under an already shown frame; (2) the held notice's refreshes use `isInstant`, which skips the intro and may leave intro-animated frame parts unplayed; (3) our lines are longer than vanilla's (several names, `job.warning` appended, 15 locales). A guess without a way to see the result would have been a blind change to a widget we do not own, so none was made. Next step: the live check in Open items; if it shows a mod-side trigger, the options are a redscript `@wrapMethod(WarningMessageGameController) UpdateWidgets` (reds, game restart) or posting an outcome with the held notice hidden first (Lua only).
**2026-10-14 (branch `v-voice-omni-drop`, from main 8f0b4992; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard or seen in the game, game not touched, no live turn; bridge restart only): V's typed line is now audible with an OmniVoice companion.** Live log: `engine=omni result=dropped reason=reply-voice-started` at 0.88 s and 1.06 s, so V was never heard. Cause: V was rendered whole on OmniVoice's single GPU worker (about 1.3 to 1.9 s to anything audible), the companion's text reply is ready at about 0.9 to 1.1 s and its own OmniVoice request stopped the unheard V; that worker cannot cancel a started render, so the reply's render queued behind V's anyway (late reply for nothing, plus a hidden GPU render and a CUDA graph capture per typed line). Fix (`docs/V_VOICE.md` "OmniVoice companions"): beside OmniVoice, V is spoken by a Pocket worker on the CPU (new `bridge/v-helper-voice.mjs`, wired in `bridge/voice-selection.mjs` `tickVHelper` and `bridge/v-voice.mjs` `helper`): loaded once in the background after OmniVoice is ready, only while OmniVoice is committed and the V setting is on, released before any other Pocket worker starts (one work-folder lock), never beside a cloud voice, the Pocket voice or the Convai voice. Estimated (not measured live): V audible at about 0.25 s, reply start 0 to 0.3 s later than with V off for an ordinary line and 0.4 to 0.9 s sooner than the old path; the options (a) play V on Omni first with a cap (reply at about 4 to 4.5 s, GPU cost) and (c) start earlier (already done, 3 to 7 ms) were rejected. Costs: one extra Python process, the 418 MiB Pocket student plus runtime, CPU only, 0 VRAM, about 45 s background load; no V on a non-English turn beside Omni (Pocket is English only); a failed helper means silent V until the setting or voice changes. New tests: `bridge/v-helper-voice.test.mjs` (9), nine Omni cases in `bridge/v-voice.test.mjs`. Packaging lists (`packaging/runtime-layout.mjs`, `packaging/release-plan.json`) gained the new file. Live check: "V's voice with an OmniVoice companion" in Live checks owed.

**2026-10-14 (branch `holocall-native-look`, from main 3e1e7b2f; unit-tested, redscript compiles against the real game cache; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): holocalls follow the game's own video/voice rule, and the live picture is rebuilt the way the game films a caller.** Research (extracted quest files in `research/cyberpunk/cache/game/raw/`, the 2.x script dump, and a third-party holo studio write-up with in-game measurements, github.com/blackpotoftea/cyberpunk_docs `holo_studio/`): the game's video holocall is `holocall_camera.ent` (`RenderToTextureCamera`) filming the caller's real body in an out-of-bounds lit studio into `holocall_camera_render_texture.dtex`, which the call window's holocall image shows; `StartHolocall` only switches the window. The body is staged by a per-character quest scene (`base\quest\holocalls\<name>\` 69, `ep1\quest\holocalls\` 20; facts `holo_<name>_calls_v_*` and `holo_v_calls_<name>_*`, the latter set by story quests), so characters without a setup only ever get voice calls with the portrait. The mod cannot use that path (quest facts, scenes, a global lock). Changes: `mod/holocall.lua` `STAGED` maps 59 of the mod's contacts to the game's setups; only those get the live picture (with the setting on), everyone else the portrait voice call with nothing spawned (`cast=video|voice` in the dialing line). The live picture now searches (one candidate per 0.25 s tick, at most nine) for a level floor 10 to 90 m above V, straight up or 30 m around, hidden from V's eyes, with room for the lens; spawns the copy there with the character's own record (validated first); spawns the game's camera at the game's framing (20.4 degrees round, level, fov 35, a 0.5 m frame = 0.79 m); keeps the off-screen copy animating (`SetForcedVisible`); holds her talk pose; turns her eyes to the lens (`LookAtAddEvent`, speed 80, renewed every 5 s); at hang-up clears all of that and deletes the camera 1.5 s after switching it off (same-frame free crashes the render thread). Why the old one stayed empty: a copy 40 m up in mid-air falls (or is inside a building), nothing kept its animation alive, no look at the lens. `Holocall.reds`: the game's ring popup sound (`PhoneCallPopup`/`OnOpen`) and the full pick-up sound set. Not solved: light (no studio lights; the copy is lit by the sky, so night pictures may be dark). Setting recommendation: keep `holocallLiveImage` off by default until one live round shows a picture; then make it on by default and drop "(experimental)" (or remove the option, leaving the STAGED rule). Tests: `bridge/holocall.test.mjs` 17 (4 new). Pre-existing unrelated failure: `scripts/lua-upvalues.test.mjs` still expects `addons/skippy` and `addons/delamain` (moved out in a0ba725c).

**2026-10-14 (branch `delamain-voice-mute`, from main 3e1e7b2f; unit-tested in fengari and node, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched, no live Convai turns, nothing pushed; main part needs a CET reload of `mod/addons.lua` and `mod/game-dialogue.lua`, the add-on part is in `cyberpunk-convai-delamain`): the Delamain cab's own welcome and goodbye are switched off and the add-on's own play in their place.** Why the cab voice could not be muted: it is not script code. The 12 Delamain lines of `delamain_taxi.scene` are played by the scene system and the audio director (Wwise VO switches set natively), nothing in redscript starts or stops them, so there was no call to hook and no event name; the add-on declared `audio = {}` and could only hide the subtitle. The runtime `line.id.hash` is a small counter, not the string id, so the lines are recognised by the speaker name (the exact ids are recorded in the add-on's `line-ids.lua`). Two mechanisms. (1) **Welcome:** the game has its own skip switch, the quest fact `delamain_skip_dialog` (scene node 730: set, the scene skips the greeting and goes straight to the Ready state and the destination map, then clears the fact itself). The add-on sets it from `ObserveBefore DelamainTaxiComponent.OnVehicleStartedMountingEvent` when V starts to climb in at state 1 or 2 (one fact write, before the scene reaches node 730 about 1 to 3 s later), puts it back only if V gets out first, the cab is ready with it still set, or the player turns the option off mid-boarding, and writes no other fact; the map, the fare and the drive are the game's. Its own welcome is asked for as soon as V sits down (the ride record now starts at the mount and survives the Ready write), so it is generated while the game opens the map, plays about when the map appears, waits like every remark for the scene and game lines, and is dropped for the ride-start greeting if V picks a destination first. (2) **Goodbye, arrival and "your wish is my command":** no switch exists, so the main mod stops the voice with `AudioSystem.Stop(event, speaker entity)` for `vo_3d`, `vo_2d`, `vo_3d_important` (candidates: the tag-less core VO events) and filters the subtitle, over a window that now starts when V climbs in and ends with the ride (states 1 to 7, V in or entering the cab). New in the main mod: `N.stopAudio` returns a function that re-sends the same stops (it holds the entity id value and the event names, never the entity), `ruleLine` hands it to `M.mutedLine` as `info.repeatStop`, and `M.tick` repeats it at 0.3, 0.8 and 1.6 s (at most 6 lines tracked, dropped on `M.reset`; only for a rule that has voice events), because a scene voice can start just after its subtitle. The goodbye stop is **not heard-tested** (`audioVerified` stays false: a remark still waits for a line that keeps playing, so the worst case is the old order, the game's goodbye then ours). The persona, trigger guidance and the `gameVoiceReplaced` fact now make Delamain greet and say goodbye himself while the game's lines are off (and not repeat them when the option is off). "Replace the game's own lines" and "Mark our lines (AI)" work as before; with the option off nothing is written and the game's lines play. Tests: add-on 56 (55 against this branch's main, the one failure is the unrelated `remarkCap = false` assertion another session added, which needs main-side support not on this branch; 56 against the main checkout), main `addons-lua` 29, `game-dialogue` 21, `addons` and add-on neighbours green. Live check (also item 10 of the live list in `docs/ADDON_API.md`): ride a cab with the option on; the cab's greeting must be silent with no subtitle, the map must open a few seconds after sitting down, and the add-on's welcome must play about then; at arrival read probe.log for `muted game line: Delamain ... audio=stop-sent(vo_3d,vo_2d,vo_3d_important)` and listen whether the game's goodbye really stops; if it still plays, the next candidates are other Wwise events (see the add-on's `docs/DELAMAIN_RESEARCH.md` 2.4) and `volume_dialogue`; check that `delamain_skip_dialog` is 0 again after the map opens. Install `mod/addons.lua`, `mod/game-dialogue.lua` and the add-on folder, CET reload.

**2026-10-14 (branch `guard-and-upvalues`, from main 0b3e8318; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, game not touched; bridge restart only): the Mature guard follows the loaded model and covers add-ons; the LuaJIT upvalue limit is 120 in CET, not 60.** (1) `TextProviderHost` now asks `#guardOn(route)` per turn: the guard (input screen, output screen, first-sentence reject, and the adults-only plus HARD LIMITS lines via `systemHead({guard: true})`) runs on the local route when the Mature setting is on OR the loaded model is uncensored (`allowanceFor(model, hints).uncensored`, pack models and hand-flagged ones), even with the setting off. A stopped server is started first to learn the model (the request would have started it anyway); a normal model costs one name lookup. The add-on text hosts (`addonTextHost`, convai-bridge) now pass `matureContent` and `guardOnly: true`: the same guard, never the crude layer. Normal model + setting off is byte for byte the old prompt (tests compare it to `systemHead`). New `guardLayer()` in `bridge/mature-content.mjs` is the last two lines of `matureLayer` (unchanged text). Tests in `bridge/mature-content.test.mjs`. (2) `scripts/lua-upvalues.mjs` (fengari's compiler, `_ENV` excluded to match LuaJIT) and `scripts/lua-upvalues.test.mjs` count every function's upvalues in `mod/*.lua` and `addons/**/*.lua`. Main and the installed copy both have 71 in the `onUpdate` closure (`mod/init.lua:2791`), and the game loaded it fine (10:53 and 11:08, no upvalue error in any CET log). The CET plugin explains it: its LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3 passes 0x78 = 120 as the upvalue limit (the "local variables" limit next to it is the stock 200), so the test enforces 120; `--limit 60` shows what stock LuaJIT would reject (only that one function). Nothing was refactored. Headroom: 49 upvalues.

**2026-10-14 (branch `skippy-hologram`, from main 15e2d625; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard or seen in the game, game not touched): Skippy remarks that showed a subtitle but could not be heard; his voice from the gun; why the game's hologram text cannot carry our remarks.** Cause of the silent remarks, from the 2026-10-14 logs: the bridge cut remarks the game had already accepted. The reaction lease (`runtime/reaction-lease.json`) said `playing` only on the add-on tick after the game accepted the reply, and its deadline was floored to whole seconds (`os.time()`), so a short remark could look expired the moment it began. Example from probe.log: companion-kill played and was released in the same second, and the bridge logged `Continuous speech owner changed`. Separately, one refused or half-written lease read (Windows sharing, an atomic replace in flight) made `reactionCurrent` return false, and `tick()` aborted a playing turn. During play the lease is rewritten every second (fight-start was cut about 1 s in). Fixes: `canDeliver` writes `playbackStartedAt` at once (`mod/addons.lua`); the deadline adds a second for the rounding; `reactionCurrent` retries EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES/ENOENT and half-written JSON three times, 15 ms apart, and keeps a playing turn through up to 1 s of unreadable lease (`bridge/convai-bridge.mjs`). New `reactionLeaseProblem` (`bridge/battle-context.mjs`) names the reason. New log details: ` voice-stopped=<speech state> (<error>)` on `Remark released` when the voice ended early, and `(lease: <reason>)` on the bridge's `did not reach the player`. Voice position: new speaker option `voiceFrom` (`docs/ADDON_API.md`); Skippy passes his active weapon, so the browser voice takes its pan and distance from the gun (asked once per reply, dropped back to V if the gun is not within 3 m of the camera; the native Omni phrases still play on V). Hologram: the game's text beside the gun is a fixed onscreen string per voice line id (`vo_onscreens`, 19 entries, all mq007), drawn by something no script feeds. `Invisible` lines are rejected by both script subtitle controllers, so our text cannot be routed there and the subtitle fallback stays (detail and sources: `docs/addons/SKIPPY_RESEARCH.md` 1.4.1). Tests: `battle-lease` (retries, the bounded grace, refusal reasons), `addons-lua` (playing at once, the deadline, voice-stopped, voiceFrom, the init seam), `continuous-speech` (gun position, fallback, ordinary replies untouched), `loot-context` (adapter). Live check: Live checks list, "Skippy remarks heard and his voice from the gun".

Evidence it is the vanilla taxi and not the mod: every main-mod hook on the taxi or AutoDrive is an Observe with read-only bodies (`mod/init.lua` `OnAutodriveToggled` after, `OnStopAutoDriveOnDestinationReachedRequest` before); the only `Override`s are phone, MCM and subtitle UI classes; the only setters near the cab are the companion mount and unmount commands (`mod/companion-vehicle-native.lua`, V's companions, not the cab) and `DisableAutoDriveRequest` in `companion-chauffeur-native.lua` `M.disable`, which refuses a Delamain journey and is only for old reload receipts; the add-on itself never writes a fact; the probe log shows no companion exit or chauffeur line near the event. **2026-10-14 (branch `teardown-safety`, from main 7d1379a8; unit-tested; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): session-teardown review after two crashes during a save load (`Cyberpunk2077.exe+0x53F9D4` on 14 Oct, one second after "Session references released: player detached"; `+0xE6ABAD` on 12 Oct). Neither stack contains the native plugin (it only registers RTTI natives, holds no game object between calls and installs no hook). No single culprit is proven; four paths that made engine calls on objects being destroyed, and several strong handles that pinned them past the unload, were closed.** (1) `companion-locomotion.lua`: the `AIMoveToCommandHandler.UpdateCommand` observer (every walking NPC, every frame) stayed switched on after `companions.abandon` because only `companions.update` refreshed `convaiLocomotion.active`, and update is skipped until the next session is up; with a party it therefore called `GetOwner(context)` and `npc:GetEntityID()` on AI contexts the engine was destroying. It is now false from the start and set false in `companions.abandon` (fast travel too; the next update turns it on again). Both crash sessions had mod companions. (2) Add-on hooks (`addons/delamain`, `addons/skippy`) ran with no session check: the cab hooks read the quest system and `component:GetEntity()` during the unload, and Skippy's weapon-swap and crosshair hooks read the player and weapon (and could set `holding` true again after `sessionEnded`). New add-on API call `handle:live()` (true from the first tick of a session until the main mod releases it; documented in `docs/ADDON_API.md`); both add-ons return at once when it is false. Delamain counts the ignored callbacks by name and logs them at the next session start ("cab callbacks ignored while the previous session was released"), which shows which callbacks the engine sends during a teardown. A cab found at the start of a session is still picked up by `sessionStarted`. (3) `seated-look.lua`: the Workspot exit hooks called `CancelDelay` on the engine's delay system (and the pending id was never cleared) while the player's state machine left Workspot during a load; with the session released they now only forget (`live` = not `worldSuspended`, passed from `init.lua`); entering is not gated so a save loaded while V sits is still widened. (4) Handles held across the unload (a CET handle is a strong reference, and `onUpdate`, which would have cleared them, does not run until the next session): the face writer's cached actor rows (`companions.expressionActors` cache plus the `convaiExpressionFrame` context) held every ready copy's and nearby candidate's NPC; the gesture and seating controllers held V (`self.player`); the MCM page held old settings-screen widgets (`statusOriginal`, `contentHold`) and would have called into them on the next update. All dropped in `abandonSession`/the modules' abandon; `abandonSession` then runs one `collectgarbage` (not on fast travel, never per frame; unproven in game, a one-off hitch at a load) so the engine objects are released while the world still owns them, not by a Lua finalizer in the middle of the unload or the next session's start. Not changed: adoption records keep a hidden world NPC across a fast travel on purpose (needed to show it again); `mod/face-test.lua` (developer tool) has no abandon. Tests: `bridge/companion-behavior.test.mjs`, `bridge/companion-duplicates.test.mjs`, `bridge/companion-expression-playback.test.mjs`, `bridge/seated-look.test.mjs`, `addons/delamain/delamain.test.mjs`, `addons/skippy/skippy.test.mjs`. Reviewed and found sound: the whole `abandonSession` chain (pure Lua, file writes only, no native call), `companions`/`vehicles`/`actuator`/`equipment`/`reload-cleanup` abandon, speech/subtitles/continuous speech, `ConvaiTurnStep` delay callbacks (weak refs, generation checked), Codeware callbacks registered by UI controllers (unregistered in `OnUninitialize`), `ConvaiKnowledgeState` (unregisters in `OnDetach`). Still suspicious, unchanged: the Codeware `Entity/Extract` callback in `Face.reds` (untargeted, runs `GetDynamicEntitySystem().IsTagged` for every entity the engine builds, including during session start and end; a `dynamic.IsReady()` guard was NOT added because the redscript API could not be verified without the compiler); `Session/BeforeEnd` (already registered in `KnowledgeState.reds`) fires before the player detaches, while the Lua mod only learns of a teardown at `PlayerPuppet.OnDetach`, so callbacks arriving before that are not gated; the un-gated UI hooks (`phone-input.lua`, `phone-layout.lua`, `phone-chat-style.lua`, `subtitles.lua` `ChatterLineLogicController.SetLineData`).
**2026-10-14 (branch `holocall-contacts`, after live feedback; unit-tested, redscript compiles against the real game cache with `scripts/Compile-Redscript.ps1`; NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): holocalls now start from the phone's ordinary Contacts list.** User feedback: keep the phone button out of the chat (Contacts already has a call button), pressing F in a chat just stayed in the chat, and the setting does not belong in Development. Changes: removed the Holocall action and label from the Chat list and the Call hint and key handling inside an AI chat (the Call key in a chat is swallowed and does nothing, as before holocalls). New hook: `NewHudPhoneGameController.CallSelectedContact(contactData)` wrapped in `Holocall.reds`, the one function both `CallContact` paths (Contacts Call key/glyph, secondary action on Messages) end in, called after the game's own checks (callable, calls enabled). For a contact id that `mod/holocall.lua` registered (`ConvaiHolocallRegisterContact`, once per world on the phone drain: the `phone-contacts.json` rows with a conversation profile, never Johnny) it queues a holocall request and returns; anything else calls `wrappedMethod`. No quest call request, fact or phone blackboard write. The old label push (`pushLabel`, `ConvaiHolocallSetLabel`) and the string "Holocall" (15 locales, `localization/en.json`) are gone. Research (decompiled scripts): the game's own call path (`questTriggerCallRequest` -> `PhoneSystem.TriggerCall`) writes the quest fact `phonecall_player_with_<contact>` and the `UI_ComDevice.PhoneCallInformation` blackboard that many systems read, so the mod never uses it. Instead it drives the HUD call window directly (`NewHudPhoneGameController.holoAudioCallElement`; `ShowIncomingContact`, `StartAudiocall`, `StartHolocall` and `ShowEndCallContact` on its logic controller; the game's own ring and connect sounds). Entry points: the Chat list's secondary action (now labelled Holocall) and the Call button inside an AI chat. Quest calls always win: a game Incoming or StartCall preempts the mod call before vanilla's handler, which always runs; a mod call never starts while the game has one or calling is disabled; input is never consumed. Talk goes through the same private path as face-to-face talk (warm on dial, voice at V with zero distance, no gaze, no gameplay actions), and the turn context says she is on a voice call or holocall and not with V. The call ends on hang-up (tap the phone button or hold reject), calling her again, combat, a scene, a replacer, a quest call, disabling her conversations, 3 min idle, 30 min, or the HUD going away. Changed: `PhoneChatTabs.reds`, `PhoneChat.reds`, `init.lua`, `speech.lua`, `continuous-speech.lua`, `subtitles.lua`, `manager.lua`, `mcm.lua`, `notices.lua`, the bridge `protocol`, `turn-context` and `mistral-prompt`, and docs NOTIFICATIONS and PHONE_CHAT. 11 new strings in 15 locales (Haiku helper; extractor `--check` clean). **2026-10-14 (branch `crouch-relaxed`, from main 5279552f; unit-tested; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): companions did not crouch outside combat because the stance alone shows nothing in the Relaxed state; the crouch now raises the high-level state first, with a head-height read-back.** Live (probe.log 19:29Z): V crouched outside combat, `Companion stance: crouch hls=Relaxed (evelyn-parker)`, no retry line, and Evelyn stayed standing; `stand hls=Relaxed` 23 s later. The stance request was accepted (no error, no `crouch again`, so the stance blackboard read Crouch), yet no pose. Cause, from the decompiled 2.31 scripts (`cyberpunk/NPC/components/npcStateComponent.swift`, `NPCPuppet.swift`; fetched read-only from the public dump already cited in `docs/addons/SKIPPY_RESEARCH.md`): `NPCPuppet.ChangeStanceState` only queues an `NPCStateChangeSignal`; `NPCStatesComponent.UpdateStanceState` then sets the `stanceState` anim feature, the Stance blackboard and the `inCrouch` wrapper weight. The locomotion wrappers that carry the walking poses are keyed by the HIGH-LEVEL state (`GetAnimWrapperNameBasedOnHighLevelState`: Alerted `alertedLocomotion`, Combat `combatLocomotion`, Stealth `stealthLocomotion`, Relaxed none). So in Relaxed nothing consumes the crouch (this is the likely cause; it is read from code, not yet seen in game, and the new head reading will decide it). Vanilla followers crouch only when their own AI is in Stealth. Ways the game itself reaches Stealth, all read in the dump: `NPCPuppet.ChangeHighLevelState(npc, Stealth)` from `AIFollowerTakedownCommandHandler` and from the move command handlers when `alwaysUseStealth` is set (AIMoveTo/AIMoveOnSpline/AIMoveRotateTo, NOT AIFollowTargetCommand, which has no stealth or crouch flag: fields are target, desiredDistance, tolerance, stopWhenDestinationReached, movementType, lookAtTarget, matchSpeed, teleport), plus the `StealthState` AI task. `AIFollowerRole.OnHighLevelStateEnter(Stealth)` barks only with a hostile threat; the Stealth case of `OnHighLevelStateEnter` in the state component does nothing (no senses preset change, no registration). Alerted by contrast calls `TryRegisterToPrevention` and `RefreshCachedReactionPresetData`, and the installed `ApproachVehicleDecorator` refuses boarding while Alerted, so it is the fallback, not the first choice. Companions never enter Alerted on their own (`AlertedCondition` returns false for player companions). Fix (`mod/companion-stance.lua`): crouch = `NPCPuppet.ChangeHighLevelState(npc, Stealth)` first (only from Relaxed; a state the game chose is never changed), the stance call 0.15 s later (two state-change signals in one frame may overwrite each other), then the Head slot height above her feet is read once after the stance call (same `GetSlotTransform('Head')` read `init.lua` already uses) and compared with her standing height read before the crouch: down 0.2 m or more = confirmed; not down within 2 s = the next method (Alerted), then none (Relaxed restored, the old stance-only behaviour). Stand: stance Stand first, then Relaxed 0.15 s later, only while the state still reads the level we raised (never over Combat, Fear, Unconscious); both read back, re-issued every 0.6 s up to three times, head compared with the standing height; `stand not kept by the game` if still wrong. If the AI resets the raised state to Relaxed while crouched, it is raised again up to three times, then `keeps resetting`. A stand because of a blocker (vehicle, lift, tactic, ...) restores Relaxed too, and V crouching again before the restore keeps ownership of the raise. No per-frame work: one 10 Hz tick, one blackboard observer, bounded timers (0.15 s gap, 0.6 s read-back, 0.5 s re-check while crouched, head read until confirmed only). Known side effects while she is crouched in Stealth: gestures stay off (they already do), and the holster handoff waits for Relaxed (`NPC is not relaxed autonomous AI`). **Log lines for the next live test (install `mod/companion-stance.lua`, CET reload; all start `Companion stance:`):** V crouches: `crouch issued via stealth (hls Relaxed -> Stealth, then stance Crouch) stance=Crouch hls=Stealth`, then within about 1.5 s either `crouch confirmed via stealth: head down 0.4x m stance=Crouch hls=Stealth` (works), or `crouch NOT visible via stealth: head down only 0.0x m ...; trying alerted` followed by `crouch confirmed via alerted: ...` (Alerted works, Stealth does not; make `methods = {'alerted'}` the default), or `crouch NOT visible via alerted ...; no method left, hls back to Relaxed` (neither works: the pose needs something else, e.g. a direct `stealthLocomotion` wrapper weight, and the head numbers tell how far off), or `crouch confirmed via stealth by the blackboards only (no head reading)` (the Head slot read failed: then judge by eye). Other lines: `crouch: hls fell back to Relaxed, raised again (stealth)`, `crouch: the game keeps resetting hls to Relaxed after stealth`, `crouch not kept by the game`. V stands: `stand issued via stance, then hls Stealth -> Relaxed stance=Stand hls=Stealth`, then `stand confirmed stance=Stand hls=Relaxed, head back (0.0x m below standing)`; bad cases `stand: blackboards read Stand but the head is still down ...`, `stand again`, `hls Relaxed again`, `stand not kept by the game`. If the stand line shows `hls=Stealth` after confirmation, gestures will say `not relaxed`: report it. Also watch that she draws no weapon and nobody nearby reacts. Tests: `bridge/companion-stance.test.mjs` (35 tests; 14 new: order and gap of the two calls, stand restore, Alerted escalation, no-method fallback, game-chosen states untouched, combat takeover, AI reset retries, ignored restore, crouch-again ownership, blocker, no-head-reading, stance-only adapter, bounded reads, adapter wiring).

Every reason it can wait: the conversation service has not answered yet (starting, or busy loading models; no fresh receipt), its turn in the queue (more than 8), the memory service, the voice model loading, her connection opening (also a connection waiting for a free place), and in gameplay the game placing her (shared frame budget, adopted-character gate). **2026-10-14 (branch `delamain-timing`, from main 5279552f; unit-tested in fengari and node, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not launched, no live Convai turns; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload): the Delamain cab's welcome, ride and goodbye lines no longer collide with the game's own cab lines, no longer get cut off, and no longer get lost.** Live report from the user's second cab ride: the first message never played (too close to the intro), his replies were cut off abruptly, the welcome and ending did not play (they probably coincide with the game's own message), and the driving looked messy (he hit cops and a fight started). Causes: (1) cut-off replies: a bridge bug, not timing. `continuousSpeech.onGenerated` in `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` threw "Conversation receipt owner changed" for every add-on turn, because an add-on speaker has no knowledge receipt; the reply was cut when the first chunk landed (seen in bridge.stderr.log). Fixed: an add-on turn with no receipt skips the knowledge calls and only has to be the current turn (a turn that lost ownership is still rejected). (2) welcome and ending lost: the game's `delamain_taxi.scene` plays its greeting and farewell as quest-scene subtitle lines, and the host only knew scene flags from the 0.5 s observer sample; a flight that met a scene was released and never asked for again (the old retry only covered queue drops). (3) first message lost right after the intro: the same path, plus a pending request with no reply held the queue (36 s seen). Fixes in `mod/addons.lua`: a remark can have `patience` (seconds) and a `relevant()` check; while a game scene, a scene tier or a game subtitle line is up it is held, not dropped (its ttl does not run), and sent after the scene clears plus 1.2 s of quiet if still relevant, with a fresh clock; a patient remark taken back in flight (a scene hit before it was heard) is asked for again, twice at most; a request that gets no reply within ttl plus 2 s is withdrawn ('stale') so it cannot block later remarks, and a patient one is asked again; no game line playing means no wait at all. New `M.gameLine(seconds, kind, measured)` is fed by `mod/game-dialogue.lua` `noteLine` (Regular, OwnerlessRegular, Holocall, SceneComment and Radio lines, once each, with their own duration or an estimate of 2.5 words/s, clamped to 1.5 to 10 s; the mod's own replies, crowd chatter and TV never count), through `onGameLine` in `mod/init.lua`, only while an add-on is live (no cost otherwise, no per-frame work; the host's 0.1 s tick already runs only while an add-on is live). A speaker can set `playThrough`: a line already playing finishes over an ordinary scene (dialogue, choices) instead of being cut; a call, Johnny (replacer), a tier 4+ cinematic or the player's own turn still stops it. Why play through rather than hold the game's subtitle off ours: the cab's greeting and farewell are a quest scene we cannot delay or reorder, so the workable options are to wait for it before we start (done) and not to be cut by it once we have started (done). Delamain add-on (`addons/delamain/init.lua`): a `WAIT` table gives each event its patience and the ride states it stays relevant in (boarded 30 s / READY, ride-start 20 s / STARTED, district-passed 12 s / STARTED, arrival 25 s / ARRIVED or FINISHED, ride-interrupted 20 s / CANCELLED); the arrival and goodbye stay relevant briefly after the ride ends while V is still in the cab; the old RETRY machinery is removed; a destination chosen while the greeting still waits turns into one ride-start line that greets (the greeting is cancelled; one line, not two). Docs: `docs/ADDON_API.md` (Patience section, `playThrough`, `requeued`, new reasons), `addons/delamain/EVENTS.md`. Tests: `bridge/addons-lua.test.mjs` (patience, relevant and expiry, requeue twice at most, stale withdrawal, game lines, playThrough), `addons/delamain/delamain.test.mjs` (welcome taken back and said again, game line holds the greeting, plays through, arrival after the farewell, no arrival to an empty cab, destination chosen during a held greeting), `bridge/game-dialogue.test.mjs` (noteLine), `bridge/voice-routing.test.mjs` (add-on turn without receipt); the harness `bridge/addon-lua-harness.mjs` now names the failing test line. Full suite: only environment failures in this worktree (no `node_modules` here: facial-timeline, the companion-actions SDK adapter test, the runtime-bootstrap playwright test) plus the known timing-flaky voxtral spacing test, which passes alone. The unknown only the game can settle: which scene signal the cab ride raises (dialogue, tier, or only a subtitle line); the logs name it. **Driving verdict: nothing in the mod or the add-on writes to the cab's driving.** The Delamain add-on is voice only (it reads ride state from the `delamain_taxi_state` fact and the observer; it never sets vehicle or driver AI, speed or route). The main mod's chauffeur modules (`companion-chauffeur-native.lua`, `companion-chauffeur.lua`) explicitly refuse the Delamain cab (`delamainCab`) and treat a foreign AutoDrive journey as someone else's; the companion vehicle code only seats companions (taxi seat order is back-left, front-right, back-right, front-left last, so the driver seat is used only with four or more companions); seated gaze writes look-at only; the work done while the cab moves is read-only sampling. The cop collision is most likely the game's own autodrive (the vanilla Delamain does hit traffic and police); it cannot be ruled out from code alone, so a live A/B is the answer. Cleanest live A/B: the same short ride, same start and destination, twice: once with the mod disabled in CET (or add-on and companions off, nobody in the party), once as in the report; also read probe.log for `Native core: vehicles=native|lua`, `journey-start`, `seat-reserved`, `mount-requested`, `taxi-arrived`, and check that no companion took `seat_front_left`. **Log lines to look for in the next ride:** `[Addons] Remark held: ... reason=scene|scene-tier|game-line signals=... patience=Ns` (what held it, and the signal the cab scene raises), `[Addons] Remark: ... waited=N.Ns` (it went after the wait), `Remark released: ... reason=scene signals=... (taken back; it is asked for again)`, `Remark plays through a game scene: ... signals=...`, `Remark dropped: ... reason=expired|irrelevant`, `Game line: <kind> for about X s (its own duration|estimated); patient remarks wait for it`; in bridge.stderr.log there must be no `Bridge request failed: Conversation receipt owner changed` for Delamain turns.

**2026-10-13 (branch `custom-local-models`, from main; unit-tested with the fake llama-server, NOT installed, NOT live; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload for the Lua and locale files; not merged): players can add their own GGUF chat models by hand to the Local AI model row.** A player drops a `.gguf` into a `custom/` folder of the Local AI folder and lists it in `manifest.custom.json` (`{version: 1, models: [{file, name?, uncensored?, auto?, family?, contextSize?, chatTemplate?}]}`; also read from the dev Local AI folder when only that has it). `bridge/custom-models.mjs` validates each entry strictly (relative path inside the folder, `.gguf`, name 1 to 60 characters, booleans, `contextSize` 2048 to 262144, `chatTemplate` name; at most 16) and logs each bad entry once as `[custom models] ...`, never throwing. Requirement checks run at detection time on the settings poll (at most every 5 s, never per frame; stats every look, the first 2 MiB of a file read only when its size or time changed): GGUF magic and version 2 or 3, `general.architecture`, an embedding model rejected from its architecture or a non-zero `<arch>.pooling_type`, a file under 1 MiB, a split model's parts summed. A failing model is listed in the log and in the row's help as "Not usable: <name>: <reason>"; the VRAM estimate (file plus the tier headroom) is in the help; a model needing more than the card's total memory (from `--list-devices` after the first start, else one `nvidia-smi` call at most once a minute) is listed as "too large for this graphics card" and never chosen. Listing: ids `custom:<file name>`, after the built-in ones, "(custom)" label. Auto: custom models only with `"auto": true` (then they compete by size; equal sizes keep the built-in first); with Mature content on, a custom model joins the uncensored group only with both `uncensored` and `auto` true (decision for the user to confirm: the spec said both that `uncensored` makes a model eligible for Mature Auto and that custom models are used by Auto only with `auto: true`; the stricter reading is built). A pin always works if it fits. The server starts a custom model with its `contextSize` and `--chat-template`, otherwise the same flags; one that fails to start or dies while warming up is marked broken (until its file changes or reset) and the start is repeated with Auto's choice, with one `local-model-fallback` notice whose text now also says "or did not start" (all 15 locales updated). `allowanceFor(name, {uncensored, family})` honours the manifest flag in both directions instead of the file name. Added `bridge/custom-models.mjs` to the bridge allowlists (`packaging/runtime-layout.mjs`, `packaging/release-plan.json`). Tests: `custom-models.test.mjs`, `custom-model-choice.test.mjs`, the custom block in `local-llm-server.test.mjs`, a custom-row test in `manager.test.mjs`, `mistral-key.test.mjs`; fixture `FAKE_LLAMA_EXIT_FOR_MODEL`. **2026-10-13 (branch `crouch-sync`; unit-tested; NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): companion crouch syncing.** Live bug (Carol Emeka, probe.log 09:48Z): she did not crouch at first, then crouched, and stayed crouched after V stood. Read from the log: `crouch` 09:48:11, an idle flavour gesture began 09:48:25 while she was meant to be crouched, `stand - workspot` 09:48:26, `crouch` 09:48:28, gesture `exit not relaxed` 09:48:29, `stand` 09:48:36 (logged, no visible effect). Causes found in code: (1) idle and talk gestures never looked at the crouch, so the workspot started over the pose and the stance module took the pose apart (stand, then crouch) while the workspot was still ending; (2) a stand was fire-and-forget: `NPCPuppet.ChangeStanceState` returns nothing and returns early when the blackboard already matches, so an ignored stand was never noticed, while a crouch was already read back and retried; (3) V crouching again while a stand was unconfirmed left her crouched with no record, so the next stand never came. The trigger is an event (`PlayerPuppet.OnLocomotionStateChanged`) applied at the next 10 Hz tick (at most 0.1 s) or, when a blocker holds her, at the next 0.5 s re-check; the code does not explain a visible delay and the stuck pose is not proven to come from the stance (see open question). Fix: `companions.lua` passes `crouched` to the gesture owner; `companion-gestures.lua` starts nothing while it is set and leaves at once (`exit` reason `crouching`); `companion-stance.lua` reads every stand back (re-issues up to three times while the stance reads Crouch, then `stand not kept by the game`), adopts a still-present crouch when V crouches again, exposes `holds(serial)`, logs `crouch waiting - <reason>` once per reason when a blocker holds her, and adds `hls=<high-level state>` to the crouch, stand and not-kept lines. Open question for the next live test: if `hls` is not Relaxed after a crouch or stand, the visible pose comes from the high-level state (Alerted or Stealth locomotion wrapper) and the next step is to restore Relaxed; if `hls` is Relaxed and the stance reads Stand but she looks crouched, the animation graph does not re-read the stance while she idles. No per-frame work was added. Install: `mod/companion-stance.lua`, `mod/companion-gestures.lua`, `mod/companions.lua`; CET reload.

What was written:
- `docs/addons/SKIPPY_BIBLE.md`: the character bible. It covers voice, the two modes, the comedy rules (a device kit, so 10 to 30 remarks a fight do not repeat a shape), lore, the never-do list, spoiler care, and the changes the builder and the API should make.

Scores:
- Built-in judge: 8.2 to 8.5.
- Blind Haiku judge: about 4.5 out of 10, where 5 is filler. So most lines are filler and a few are very good.
- Dropped repeats: 6 to 10 per pass, not zero.

What limits quality:
- **Asterisks:** `cleanReply` deletes the word inside asterisk emphasis, which hits 15 to 30 percent of replies.
- **Builder bridge:** sample echoes, tone angles that pull off voice, metres given on every shot, and raw keys like `firstBlood` that leak into lines.
- **No length cap:** a third of lines go over the word limit.

ministral 14B: the built-in judge scores it higher and it drops fewer repeats, but the blind judge rates it the same as 8B.

Open:
- The builder adopts the device rotation from bible section 11.
- The API fixes the asterisk deletion, checks new lines against the samples, and caps remark length.
- Live and Local AI listening checks.

It is visible and usable without it, off by default, Local AI only, with the 18+ line; with stock models it mostly changes language, violence and tone. The pack (the uncensored GGUFs) only changes the setting's help text (installed or not, with a pointer to the GitHub releases page) and is distributed ONLY as an optional file on the project's GitHub release, never on Nexus: `packaging/MATURE_PACK_NEXUS.md` became `MATURE_PACK_RELEASE_NOTES.md` (no adult-flag or tag instructions), the release workflow neither builds nor uploads the pack (tested; it stays out of the default package set), `release.config.json` has `releaseNotes` instead of `nexusText`. The guard (`bridge/mature-guard.mjs`, terms in `mature-guard-terms.mjs`, whenever the setting is on, on any model): the input screen reads V's message before any model request and refuses a minor cue (age under 18, child, teen, school, "pretend you're 15", de-ageing) with romantic or sexual intent, in character from per-character pools, with no model call and nothing stored; a window of the last 10 turns' flags (never the text) catches a cue in one message and the romance in the next; the output screen reads the first sentence and the whole reply, drops a hit, answers with the refusal and stores nothing in the history, the memory or the summaries; a reply to a message that named a minor is dropped if it has any romance; the prompt layer says that the character and V are adults. English plus the 15 UI languages, normalisation of width forms, invisible characters, spaced and dotted letters, leet and look-alikes; under 1 ms (about 0.1 to 0.2 ms), no model call, nothing per frame, counters only in the log. Tests: 180 adversarial and 169 benign scenarios (`bridge/mature-guard.fixtures.mjs`), 0 missed and 0 false positives; a stress set of 47 harmless child-word-plus-romance messages of which 15 are refused on purpose; on 213,689 sentences of character files and UI strings the reply screen dropped 21, all statements of the rule itself. **2026-10-13: the Local AI prompt is fitted to the server's context, a turn it cannot answer goes to the cloud or says so (unit-tested and run against the fake llama-server; NOT yet seen in the game).** Live record 2026-10-12: the player talked to Judy and heard nothing; `The local AI request (8790 tokens) exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens)`. Root cause: the server ran at a fixed 8,192 tokens while the prompt was bounded only in characters (persona and rules about 4.5k tokens, the rest up to 9k+), and the refusal was a code-less, non-retried, non-falling-back error. Fix: `bridge/prompt-budget.mjs` fits every Local and Groq (8,000 tokens a minute) request to n_ctx minus a reply reserve, estimated with a learned ratio and counted with `/tokenize` near the limit, cutting jobs, journal history, recent events, gear, retrieved memories, older turns, the summary, the tracked quest and the world facts in that order (discrete cuts, so the prefix cache holds) and never the persona, rules, right-now block or the player's words; a refusal that still comes is learned from and retried once. Context per tier: the supervisor asks for 16,384, then 12,288, then 8,192 by free video memory and reads the real n_ctx from `/props`; measured +136 MiB (standard, 3,008 to 3,144 MiB) and +104 MiB (lite, 1,399 to 1,503 MiB) from 8k to 16k, q8_0 KV saves only 75 to 90 MiB and is not used. A failed local turn falls back to Mistral (key saved) or Groq, with the notice `local-turn-fallback`; with no cloud provider the game says `local-failed`. EPERM on `knowledge-status.json`: a reader without the delete share (CET `io.open` in the Lua heartbeat check) blocks the rename; the bridge's retry already outlasts it, the log line is now rate-limited, the plugin needs no change. Detail: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md`. Still to do: a live Local AI turn in the game with a deliberately small context (`CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_CTX=4096`) to see the trimming and the fallback notice.

**2026-10-13: companion actions now work on the Mistral and Local AI text paths (unit-tested and measured against the real Mistral API; NOT yet seen in the game: needs a bridge restart and a CET reload; Gemma measured only in part).** Root cause of Judy ignoring "drive for me": the text path never read `config.companionAction` at all (no action prompt, no parser, no delivery), so only Convai could act, and the replies were pure talk. Convai's actions are drive to the waypoint, attack the marked target, follow, and leave the party; there is no wait, stay, sit or stop action in the game. Design (`bridge/text-actions.mjs`, wired in `TextProviderHost`): a separate 12-token classifier request (one word, temperature 0, runs beside the memory lookup, failure means plain talk) decides, the reply prompt gets a `GAME ACTIONS` note in the volatile block (stable prefix untouched) that says what is asked or what V has to do first, and the host delivers the same message Convai would send after a good reply; stray `[CODE]` tags are stripped before the voice. New `driveUnavailable` code (Lua `gameplay-actions.lua` -> `protocol.mjs` -> `companion-actions.mjs`, text routes only) carries why a ride is impossible. Rejected: tool calls (ministral-8b returns no speech on action turns and picks the wrong tool) and a code at the start of the reply (recall 12% or precision 58%). Eval (`scripts/Eval-MistralPrompt.mjs --actions`, ministral-8b, 6 characters, 27 situations, n=3): before 0 of 196 asked actions fired; after precision 100% (195/195), recall 99% (195/197), 0 false triggers in 288 turns; a Haiku judge scored false promises on impossible requests 19% before and 3% after, and replies that name what is needed 12% before and 26% after (wait and sit still draw a promise 17% and 6% of the time). Gemma 4 E4B through the same classifier (own llama-server, 2 characters, 16 situations, n=2, 64 replies; it takes about 7 s a reply on this GPU): precision 100% (13/13), recall 81% (13/16: one follow and two leaves missed, so a miss means V repeats the request); before is 0 by construction. Open: watch the first live "drive for me" with a car, a waypoint and V on foot; add a local-model eval cell for multi-turn history.

**2026-10-13: Convai sign-in backend built on branch `convai-auth`, nothing deployed, bridge mode OFF by default (unit-tested only; no live Convai, Vercel or Upstash call was made).** Design: `docs/CONVAI_AUTH_BACKEND.md`. Backend: `auth-backend/` (Vercel Node functions: `POST /api/convai/token`, `GET /api/admin/turns`, `/api/healthz`, `/api/readyz`; no dependencies). Every limit is one Redis script call (one Upstash command per token request): per-install and per-address hourly limits, new installs per address per day, a global daily mint cap ("busy"), a server-side turn backstop (an install whose reported UTC-day turns reach 100 gets no new token, "daily limit reached"), kill switch, minimum mod version, blocklist, signed requests (HMAC plus a +-120 s timestamp; obfuscation only, the secret ships in the bridge), fail closed when Redis is down. Two modes behind `CONVAI_AUTH_MODE`: `shared` (default, one token per warm instance) and `per-install` (own token per install, revoked on the cap; needs a live test because Convai's mint limit is unpublished). Bridge: `bridge/convai-credential.mjs` (`TokenSource`: fetches in the background at start, renews 8 to 10 minutes before expiry, never on a turn; install id in `runtime/convai-install.json`), `ConvaiKeys.credentialFor`, `RealtimeHost` `credential` hook, `realtime-client.mjs` passes `authToken`, `player-memory-api.mjs` backend mode (API-AUTH-TOKEN header, no character list/read/update), `scripts/Enable-CharacterMemory.mjs` (developer-side, NOT run). Switch on with `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_AUTH_BACKEND=1`, `..._AUTH_URL`, `..._AUTH_SECRET` (or `runtime/convai-auth.json`); `..._AUTH_FALLBACK=0` removes the embedded-key fallback (default on; logged only in bridge.stderr.log; only used when the backend is unreachable, never when it refuses). A player's own key is untouched. Open: deploy steps are in `auth-backend/README.md` (CLI-driven); step 0 of the design doc (token on memory calls, revoke shape, mint limit) still needs one live check; a release step must write `convai-auth.json` with the signing secret into the package; run `Enable-CharacterMemory.mjs --apply` before players use backend mode.

**2026-10-13 (late): four live findings on the native core, fixed in branch `native-core` (DLL `7442124bd33c...`, plus CET reload; NOT yet proven in game).** (1) `vehicles=lua (mounting keeps answering unavailable)`: `GetMountingFacility`, `GetMappinSystem`, `GetScriptableSystemsContainer` (and `GetSceneSystem`, used by `faces`) are NOT global functions. Parsing `r6/cache/final.redscripts` (the format: header, six tables; names, name offsets, definitions of 20 bytes) shows each as a native static function of the script class `GameInstance` (native `ScriptGameInstance`) with one parameter `self`; the only globals that take a `GameInstance` are `GetPlayer`, `GetMainPlayer` and `GetPlayerObject`. The old lookup searched the globals only. `convai::game::GameSystem` now looks in the statics of `ScriptGameInstance` / `GameInstance`, then the globals, then all class functions, and else asks the instance's own system lookup for the native class; the route is logged (`Game access: GameInstance.GetMountingFacility resolved as ... (static function of class ScriptGameInstance)`). (2) `NPCPuppet.IsInCombat not found`: the game registers the static as `IsInCombat;ScriptedPuppet` on `NPCPuppet` itself (the compiler appends parameter types after a `;`; PlayerPuppet's member is `IsInCombat;`), so `GetFunction("IsInCombat")` finds nothing; the earlier claim that it lives on `ScriptedPuppet` was wrong (that is its parameter type). One matcher (`ScriptNameIs`, headless-tested) now serves `game::Method`, `game::StaticFunction`, `FindMember` and `vreflect::StaticFunction`, so the actuator and faces read the combat flag natively and the chauffeur's `P` section and `ProbeJson` get `IsInCombat` too; faces' `GetSceneSystem;GameInstance` global (also not a global) goes through `GameSystem`. The parity gate compares the combat field (new counters, proof needs it compared on every counted sense, `PARITY MISMATCH in combat`, proven line says who reads it). (3) Judy in a car: `seated-look-skip {"reason":"in a vehicle"}` is V's own camera widening (`mod/seated-look.lua`), not her gaze; her gaze has its own gates and none of them was logged, so the cause is not provable offline (the Oct 2 live pass used the same Lua with narrower limits). Changes: a `Companion recovery seated-gaze {...}` probe line when her seated attention changes (selected, gate, style, speed, error), seated limits widened (full 100/150/150, narrow 60/120/150; V is about 90 degrees off a passenger's axis, where the old 70/120 faded the look to about 60 percent), `calculatePositionInParentSpace` set for seated requests (as the game's in-vehicle look-at does), and speed bands (full to 8 m/s, narrow to 20, none above, 2 m/s margins). (4) `companions.update` 6.3 to 10.6 ms/s: from the perf snapshots the jump is Judy appearing (3 ms/s before her, 12.8 in the parity window, 12.6 proven, no drop after the proof at 21:03:28Z), and FPS drives the row (7.4 ms/s at 40-50 FPS, 14.5 below 30); proven native vs plain Lua is not separable from that data (other native systems differed between the sessions; matched-FPS rows showed proven native 1.5-2 ms/s higher, not a controlled comparison). Fixes: the combat read no longer falls back to Lua every tick, the window after the first 40 senses narrows to one sense in four while only walking is missing (a standing companion used to hold it open at twice the cost), and perf rows `tickNative.life/sense/commandState` make the A/B possible. **2026-10-13: vehicle group merged onto the current `native-core`; names audited against the game (one DLL now carries every system; NOT live).** Registration: the three classes use `StaticClass(name, system)` and plain `Static()` calls, so `rtti::CommitAll` checks every parameter and return type (`String`, `Bool`, `Int32`, `Double`, `handle:gameObject`, `handle:IScriptable`; no `array:Double`) and trips a system whole when one is missing; the per-class `TypesExist` helpers are gone. Names checked against the RED4ext SDK headers (native `NAME` against script `ALIAS`) and the strings of `r6/cache/final.redscripts`: the enums `gamePSMVehicle`, `gamedataVehicleType`, `gameAutodriveDestinationType`, `gameAutodriveLaneValidityResult` and the struct `gamemountingMountingInfo` are the native names; `NPCPuppet`, `PlayerPuppet`, `AutoDriveSystem`, `AIVehicleCommand` and `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` have no alias; `DynamicEntitySystem.IsReady/IsManaged/IsTagged` are Codeware natives. Two real bugs found by that audit, both fixed: (1) `CClass::GetFunction(shortName)` answers the first function of that name, statics before members, so overloads such as `IsAttached`/`IsVehicle`/`IsDestroyed`/`IsInCombat` (member and static versions under one short name) can resolve to a function with other parameters; this is also why the live actuator logged `NPCPuppet.IsInCombat is not a one-argument static function` (the nearest `IsInCombat` is a member, the static `IsInCombat(puppet)` is declared on `ScriptedPuppet`). The vehicle group now resolves members by name AND parameter count (`vreflect::FindMember`, nearest class first, statics skipped), statics from the nearest declaring class (`StaticFunction`), refuses an argument list that does not fill the parameters, caches only hits and logs what the class does have on a miss. NOT applied to the actuator (`ActuatorGame.cpp` `CombatFunction` still uses `GetFunction`): the same fix would let the plugin read the combat flag there. (2) The three global functions (`GetMountingFacility`, `GetMappinSystem`, `GetScriptableSystemsContainer`) are tried as `<name>;GameInstance` and then by short name with one `ScriptGameInstance` parameter among all global functions; the resolved name is logged. Shims: passage's self-test wait no longer fails after five waits (same rule as clearance: wait, retry every 2 s then 10 s); all three honour `runtime/native-verify.txt` (`api.verifying`); every doc and comment names only the file switches. Tests: node 21 (vehicles), 18 (passage) and 28 (chauffeur) shim tests (new: native-verify.txt in each, passage waits, a source contract on the vehicle group), ctest 61 + plugin_host.

**2026-10-11: Local speech-to-text for the voice key on the Mistral route (bridge + packaging; BRIDGE RESTART; UNVERIFIED in game; `docs/LOCAL_STT.md`).** Moonshine Tiny English int8 (MIT, 27 M parameters) run by sherpa-onnx 1.13.6 (Apache-2.0) on the CPU, in the Pocket Python. Chosen by measurement on 26 clips / 130 s (game actors, LibriSpeech, Windows voices with game names): WER 11.4-11.7%, final decode p50 0.18 s / p95 0.28 s on 2 threads and 0.45 / 0.67 s on 1, against faster-whisper tiny.en 12.0% at 0.82 s, base.en 10.4% at 1.9 s, small.en 7.6% at 8 s, a streaming Zipformer 12.7% (game 28%) and Moonshine Base with no gain for 3x the size. Default is ONE thread (onnxruntime pools spin-wait: 2 threads cost 3x the CPU for 30% less time), below-normal priority, live words from a decode of the newest 8 s every 1.2 s at about 15% duty, and a live decode that already covered the recording is reused as the final text (about 3 ms). No process runs outside a recording; the worker quits after 90 s idle. Audio: `bridge/local-stt-capture.mjs` opens a 16 kHz mono AudioWorklet in the hidden Chrome (served from memory, mic granted per context), 100 ms Int16 chunks to the bridge; the existing `MicrophoneSession` states, notices, 700 ms minimum, spam handling and `microphone-heard.json` words run unchanged, and an empty transcript becomes the existing no-speech notice. Wired as `mistralSpeech` in `convai-bridge.mjs` (`createLocalSpeech`); the Convai route never starts it. Model in the HF bucket `final/stt-model/moonshine-tiny-en-int8/` (124 MB, manifest updated by `scripts/Upload-SttModel.py`), `release.config.json` group, `models/stt` in the package, wheels in `pocket.lock.txt`, notices, closure lists, install test transcribes the Pocket sentence. Tests: `local-stt.test.mjs` (16) and `local-stt-capture.test.mjs` (12, includes Chrome's fake mic through the real worker); bench: `node scripts/Bench-LocalStt.mjs --synth --live`. Live check: Provider Mistral, press the voice key, say a sentence with a name, press again: the words show while speaking and the reply follows; silence gives the no-speech notice.

**2026-10-11: V no longer keeps walking after the talk box: the box waits until no movement key is held (redscript; GAME RESTART, plus CET reload for the Lua half; UNVERIFIED live).** Cause (user confirmed it is the text talk box, not the phone): a movement key released while the Codeware popup owns input never reaches gameplay, so the axis still reads held after the box closes and V walks on until the key is pressed again. No retail API to release input was found (and none is used), so the fix keeps the key-up from being lost: `Composer.reds` `ConvaiMoveWatch` is registered on the player from `OnGameAttached` (removed in `OnDetach`) for exactly two actions, `MoveX` and `MoveY` (`r6/config/inputContexts.xml` MovementActions: A/D and W/S plus the left stick). The game calls it only when an axis value changes, it stores the two values (held = either above 0.15) and consumes nothing, so there is no per-frame work. `init.lua`: the talk hotkeys (F6/F7 and the group one) ask `player:ConvaiMoveHeld()`; if a direction is held, the box is not opened but the request waits (`convaiTalkGate`, serviced from onUpdate only while a request waits) until the axis is released, at most 1.5 s. At the cap the box opens anyway (chosen over a hint or a refusal: a talk request is never dropped, and no new localised text is needed), the stuck reading is forgotten (`ConvaiMoveForget`) so the next press is not delayed, and in that one case a key released inside the box can still be lost (known issue stays in `packaging/PLAYER_README.md` until verified). A second press while waiting only changes private/group; the wait is dropped on menu, pause or world change. `Composer opened:` log line keeps `speed=` and adds `moveAxis=held|free|n/a` (n/a = redscript tracker not installed, the box then opens at once) and `waited=` when it waited; `Talk box waits for the movement keys to be released` is logged when a press is deferred. Tests: `phone-input.test.mjs` (tracker shape and the two named registrations, Lua gate: immediate open, wait then open once, cap with forget, second press, world drop). Live check: hold D, press the talk hotkey, release D: the box opens at once on release (probe.log `moveAxis=free waited=0.xx`); hold D past 1.5 s and the box opens anyway; walk with D, tap the hotkey after releasing, type, close the box, V must stand still. If the tracker shows `moveAxis=held` while standing, a key-up was missed earlier (menu, vehicle): the next press waits 1.5 s once and clears it.

**2026-10-11: a locked state file no longer stalls companion preparation (bridge; restart the bridge).** Report: "Alex could not prepare: Companion preparation is not responding" with `bridge.stderr.log` lines `Preparation poll: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...companion-invitations-state.json.<uuid>.tmp'` between 14:40 and 14:48 IST. Cause: `guarded-file.mjs` `atomicFile` (the shared writer of every game-facing state file) retried the rename only 5 times over 80 ms; when the game's Lua reader or an indexer held `companion-invitations-state.json` longer, it threw, `CompanionInvitations.publishSnapshot` passed the error up, and `pollPrefetch` aborted before it ran the rest of the poll, so the receipt aged out and `invitation-readiness.lua` gave up after 15 s. (`memory.prepareCharacter` itself writes nothing, so it is not involved; the two orphan `.tmp` files in the game runtime folder were from 5 and 10 Oct and are deleted.) Fix: `atomicFile` now tries the rename 6 times with a 10/20/40/80/150 ms backoff (about 300 ms), retries EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY, keeps the old file and removes its temp file (with `rm` retries) when it still fails; `publishSnapshot` catches a failed or throwing write, returns false and counts it (`publishFailures`, `lastPublishError` in the invitation diagnostic), so the poll goes on and the next one writes the fresh receipt. Tests: `guarded-file` (EPERM twice then success, always failing keeps the old file and leaves no temp, default backoff timing), `companion-invitations` (poll survives failed and throwing writes, keeps its stage and writes again). Not changed: private registry writes (`player-memory.json`, `knowledge-service`) have their own writers and are not read by the game.

[Alex=memory]` and at 09:11:00Z / 09:11:21Z `Alex could not prepare: Companion preparation is not responding` (`invitation-readiness.lua`: the bridge receipt did not move past the `memory` stage within 15 s). NOT proven to be timing. Defensive changes anyway: `companion-records.lua` logs `Companion spawn record: ...` (original, `Armed_<name>`, or `armed clone failed (reason)`) to probe.log; `companions.lua` retries `CreateEntity` with the original record when the clone cannot be created; creating `runtime/armed-clones-off` (or `M.armedClones = false`) disables the clone with no code change. **2026-10-11 (Alex 2 spawned a little up and floated while talking: relocations and tall-navmesh spawns now go to the Static floor; Lua only; CET reload; needs a fresh invite or a relocation to see it).** Log 08:40-08:54Z (Alex, serial 1 and 2, trace z compared with V's 7.156): there was no new `relocated` line with a floor value; every relocation target in the log is a round navmesh value: `fast-travel` to z 7.3000007 (08:49:37Z, floor 7.156, so 14 cm up) and 9.4000006 (08:19:09Z), `blocked` to 11.4496, `stance` to 10.9515, `lift-arrival` to 8.4000034 and 49.500022 (08:13:56Z: she was still at 49.5000 ten seconds later, 30 cm over the 49.2 floor). Cause: `placement.find` returns the navmesh point plus 10 cm and `relocate` teleported her there with `actuator.teleport` without the floor correction of `6804d73`; an AI-driven copy keeps the height she is put at until she first walks, so a stance played meanwhile floats her and the exit drops her (Round 5g). The fresh-spawn correction also missed the apartment case: the spot is navmesh plus 10 cm, so a navmesh 30 cm over the floor is 40 cm over it and the 5-35 cm window rejected it (she was then lowered by `settleOnFloor` half a second after attach, a visible hop). Fix (`mod/companions.lua`): `floorBelow` takes a window; fresh copies and `relocate` use 5-45 cm for a placement spot (`placeDrop`), and `relocate` puts the target on that Static floor (one ray per relocation, on demand; `lift-board` keeps the spot, a car floor is not Static ground; if the frame budget is spent it retries the same plan twice, then places her as found). Same out-of-view rules, nothing per frame. Not changed, on purpose: the gesture workspot device stays at her entity position (the stance never moves her, entity z is constant through it, Round 5g; a device on the floor under a floating entity would pull her down and the exit would put her back); not covered: `carTeleport` (lift car floor), seating stand-up teleports, and the party-car `recover` in `companion-vehicle-native.lua`, which is still a plain transform teleport at navmesh plus 10 cm (undone by the AI, not touched today). Tests: `bridge/companion-placement.test.mjs` (spot 40 cm over the floor is created on it, 50 cm is not), `bridge/companion-passage.test.mjs` (a floor-change relocation lands on the floor, and keeps the spot when no floor is found). Open: confirm live after a CET reload on a fresh invite and after a fast travel or a floor change (z in the movement trace should be the floor, and a stance should neither lift her nor drop her at the exit).

**2026-10-11: Fight/Distract finally find a target: a marked or aimed crowd-flagged gang member is accepted, the look-at can no longer be blocked by a companion, and the character is told when there is no target (Lua = CET reload; `bridge/` = BRIDGE RESTART).** Live evidence (probe.log 08:50Z): `Tactic target: none; skipped aimed-companion=1 companion=1 crowd=2` (also `crowd=19`, `15`, `1`), `companion-actions.json` stayed `{"action":"none"}`. Breaks found along text intent -> bridge action -> `companion-actions.json` -> Lua target -> combat command: (1) `companion-marking.lua` `verdict` refused every `IsCrowd` NPC, and ambient gangers are crowd-flagged, so the tagged ganger was dropped. Now a crowd flag alone disqualifies only the nearest-NPC guess; a tagged or aimed crowd NPC is judged on the same evidence as anyone else (needs ganger, police, cyberpsycho, machine, armed or, new, already hostile to V; civilians, children, vendors, invulnerable, story-controlled, friendly non-police, protected and our own companions are still refused). The offer now carries `code = 'no-target'`; `gameplay-actions.lua` capture sets `context.tacticUnavailable`, `protocol.mjs` and `companion-actions.mjs` carry it (strict parse, never with a real tactic offer, private chat only) and the context tells the character to decline in character and ask V to tag or aim at an enemy. (4) The log now says why a mark was refused: `Tactic target: none; skipped ...; tagged <name> rejected: <reason> [<signals>]`. Precedence unchanged: tagged beats the crosshair beats nearest. The combat command (`native.startFight`: hostile attitude both ways, `AddThreat` persistent, `SetThreatPersistence` with `CommandInjectThreat`) matches the game's own `AIInjectCombatThreatCommand` in `vendor/reference-game-scripts` (attitude, AddThreat, persistence) but has NEVER run in game, so it is still unverified live; a crowd target's own reaction (flee) is also unverified. `IsCharacterGanger`/`IsCrowd` are native imports with no script body, so whether a crowd gang member reads as `ganger` is only checkable live (the new rejection log line shows the signals if not). **2026-10-11: typing no longer swallows key-ups; talk box and phone typing leave speed evidence in probe.log (`PhoneChat.reds` = GAME RESTART; `mod/phone-input.lua`, `mod/phone-chat.lua`, `mod/init.lua` = CET reload).** Bug (live): after typing to an NPC V kept strafing right until D was pressed once. (1) Our phone-typing guards consumed presses AND releases (`PhoneChat.reds` `OnAction`/`OnHandleMenuInput`, `mod/phone-input.lua` overrides on `gameuiInGameMenuGameController`). Now every press is still consumed, but a release is consumed only when it is one of the menu actions that controller acts on (verified in `vendor/reference-game-scripts`: `RegisterInputListenersForPlayer` lists OpenPauseMenu, OpenMapMenu, OpenCraftingMenu, OpenJournalMenu, OpenPerksMenu, OpenInventoryMenu, OpenHubMenu, QuickSave, QuickLoad, FastForward_Hold; the pointer callback is `OnPostOnRelease`, so every event there is a key-up and only back/toggle_* are swallowed; the phone popup keeps cancel, phone_open_journal, up_button, down_button, click). A blanket pass-through of releases was NOT used: the in-game controller opens the pause menu and journal ON RELEASE, so Esc/J would open menus while typing. Honest limit: those two controllers only register menu actions, so they never saw D at all; this part is a guard, and the likelier cause is (2). (2) The talk box (Codeware `GenericMessageNotification.ShowInput`) switches the input context, so gameplay can miss a key-up that happens while it owns input. NOT fixed: no verifiable API. `ReleaseAllInput`/`FakeReleaseButton` exist only in Codeware's dump of the dev-only `FunctionalTestsGameSystemInterface`, unproven in retail, so not called; deferring the open until movement stops cannot work (V pushing into a wall has speed 0 with D held) and reading held keys needs a per-event listener. (3) Evidence: `Composer opened: ... speed=<m/s>` (`mod/init.lua`, one `GetVelocity` read per open) and `Phone chat typing opened: contact=... speed=...` (rising edge inside the existing 10 Hz phone tick, only while a chat is open). A recurrence shows whether V was moving when the box opened. Tests: new `bridge/phone-input.test.mjs` (9, in `npm test`); isolated redscript compile passes. Live check: hold D, open the talk box or phone chat, release D while open, close it; V should stop. If V still drifts after the talk box closes, it is the input-context loss in (2) and probe.log shows the speed at open.

**2026-10-11: the mod never touches game-placed characters (world follow dropped; Lua + docs; CET reload; no bridge change).** Decision from the user for release 0.2. (1) World NPCs can no longer join the party: `companion-adoption.lua` offers nothing (the character gets the existing `unavailable` decline advisory, so a pedestrian says no in character) and `queueFollow` refuses; the adoption code is kept behind `allowWorldFollow`, set only by tests. (2) A named or story character the game placed gets no Convai at all: `profileIdentity` passes `world = true` and `characterCatalog.resolve` returns no profile for a roster record or name (the real Judy; our spawned copy still resolves through its managed key), never falls back to an archetype or resident for a quest-flagged, `q###/sq###/mq###` or MaxTac record. That one lookup covers the talk keys, voice, group, auto-connect scan and look counting, the distract voice and the game-dialogue speaker lookup. (3) New central predicate `convaiWorldPolicy` (`ours`, `protected`, cached per entity, on demand): the tactic target (`companion-marking.lua`) and the perception/attitude changes near it (`tactic-perception.lua`) skip protected characters; `beginFocus` (look-at, bark muting) refuses anything that is neither ours nor a talk-path profile; the passive gaze response now applies to our companions only (an ordinary NPC is faced toward V when a conversation starts, not when V merely looks at it). Auto-connect is unchanged (a bridge warm-up, no game-side effect). Cars, gestures, idle pools, seating and recovery only iterate our own party entries. Not changed, for the user to confirm: Fight/Distract still target ordinary hostile NPCs (a tactic needs an enemy), and a Side/Minor-quest-flagged vendor can still be talked to (the vendor exception) but nothing else touches it. `packaging/PLAYER_README.md` no longer says pedestrians can follow. Tests: `bridge/world-policy.test.mjs` (new), `character-catalog`, `world-companions`, `companion-tactics`. Live: see the open item "Game-placed characters are untouched".

**2026-10-11: phone Chat first message was slow because everything opened after Enter; it now opens while V types (built offline, NOT yet live: **CET reload** for `mod/phone-chat.lua`, **bridge restart**).** Report: the first phone text message takes long, later ones are fine; would Convai's core text API be faster?
